S20261026-01.h: Trump rules out strike 'today' but keeps Iran deal-or-destruction ultimatum open
S20261026-01.s: Trump said no attack would happen on Sunday while saying he must choose between a deal with Iran and 'finishing it off'. He also said senior Iranian officials have been killed and that the US must work out whom it is negotiating with. Reports say US Ambassador Tom Barrack had called a strike 'absolutely' possible.
S20261026-01.t: Renewed US-Iran war would hit Türkiye's border, energy and trade interests, so Ankara has a direct stake in the outcome of Trump's decision.

S20261026-02.h: CENTCOM strike plan on Iran reportedly ready, awaiting White House nod after midterms
S20261026-02.s: Reports say the Pentagon and CENTCOM have drafted strike plans, to be considered after the 3 November midterms. Potential targets named include Fordow, the Arak heavy water plant, research centres, energy sites and transport networks. A former US adviser suggests a limited strike, possibly on Pickaxe Mountain, which the US is monitoring.
S20261026-02.t: A strike window tied to the US election calendar gives Ankara a few weeks to plan for refugee, energy and security spillover.

S20261026-03.h: Qatari mediators travel to Tehran as Trump weighs deal against force
S20261026-03.s: Qatari mediators went to Tehran as part of efforts to de-escalate the conflict and head off another round of US-Iran war. Trump says he is weighing a deal against further military action.
S20261026-03.t: Doha's mediation role shows Gulf diplomacy leading the de-escalation track, in which Türkiye is only a secondary voice.

S20261026-04.h: Israeli army chief demands signed order as Netanyahu pushes new Iran strike before election
S20261026-04.s: Netanyahu reportedly ordered the army to prepare a new strike on Iran before the election. Chief of Staff Zamir asked for a signed written order. Military leaders reportedly fear Netanyahu may launch an offensive before voting day.
S20261026-04.t: Israeli unilateral action against Iran in the final days before the vote would raise regional escalation risk on Türkiye's doorstep.

S20261026-05.h: Tehran vows unimaginable response to any new attack, says it remains open to talks
S20261026-05.s: Iranian officials, including parliament speaker Ghalibaf, warned of a response beyond adversaries' expectations. The warnings include strikes on energy and civilian targets and nuclear escalation, while interceptor stocks are reported to be strained. The Foreign Ministry says Iran has not left the table but accuses the US of unilateral demands.
S20261026-05.t: Iranian threats against regional energy infrastructure would raise energy prices and security risks for Türkiye.

S20261026-06.h: Araghchi says Hormuz management and regional order will not return to the old model
S20261026-06.s: Iran's foreign minister said management of the Strait of Hormuz will not be as before and that another strike would produce no different result. He said Iran wants regional security handled by regional states, including Gulf neighbours, without foreign interference. He also said military action closed Hormuz and disrupted gas supplies.
S20261026-06.t: A new Iranian-led Gulf security framework would change shipping and energy conditions that matter to Türkiye.

S20261026-07.h: Hormuz disruption deepens: nearly 500 vessels affected after new tanker attack
S20261026-07.s: Nearly 500 vessels face disruption after a tanker attack, and an oil slick has reached UAE beaches. CENTCOM says over 95% of ships transit safely, and its commander flew over the strait. Obama said Iran now holds veto power over Hormuz.
S20261026-07.t: Turkey imports much of its energy and exports through routes exposed to Hormuz-driven price shocks.

S20261026-08.h: US officials: Iran plotting assassinations of US diplomats, threat highest since war began
S20261026-08.s: A report says Iranian officials called US diplomats fair game. US officials judge the threat to Americans the highest since the war began in February, and say Iran is in advanced stages of planning assassinations.
S20261026-08.t: Türkiye hosts many US and allied diplomatic and military sites that could be exposed if Iranian targeting widens.

S20261026-09.h: Iran says air defences downed US Lucas drone over Bandar Abbas
S20261026-09.s: Iran's army said air defence shot down a US Lucas-type drone over Bandar Abbas. The claim is not independently confirmed in the items.

S20261026-10.h: Riyadh airport reopens after two weeks, then Houthis claim fresh strike
S20261026-10.s: King Khalid International reopened partly after about two weeks of closure, with flights listed from Dubai, Paris and Cairo. The Houthis claimed a new strike hours later, and a drone and a missile were intercepted over Riyadh. Over 7,800 Saudi flights have been cancelled since 8 October.
S20261026-10.t: The Houthi campaign against the Saudi capital threatens a key Gulf partner for Türkiye, including its new defence ties with Riyadh.

S20261026-11.h: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi missile and drone barrages across kingdom
S20261026-11.s: The coalition said it intercepted ballistic and cruise missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh, Khamis Mushait and southern regions. The Houthis say they hit military facilities in retaliation for alleged massacres in Yemen. Debris injured two people and damaged homes and cars.

S20261026-12.h: Houthi missile threats toward Mecca and Medina draw Saudi 'red line' warning
S20261026-12.s: Saudi Arabia said threats to Mecca and Medina cross a red line, and the GCC called the attacks on Makkah a serious escalation. Imams of the two holy mosques condemned the targeting as a crime. Saudi air defences reportedly intercepted missiles near Mecca.
S20261026-12.t: An attack on Islam's holy sites would likely draw a strong Turkish political response and deepen Ankara's alignment with Riyadh.

S20261026-13.h: US orders non-emergency staff and families out of Saudi Arabia
S20261026-13.s: The US ordered non-emergency personnel and their families to leave Saudi Arabia amid Houthi missile and drone attacks.

S20261026-14.h: Türkiye offers help to Saudi Arabia as Yemen praises ties with Ankara
S20261026-14.s: Yemen praised its relations with Türkiye, and Türkiye offered assistance to Saudi Arabia amid Houthi spillover into the kingdom.
S20261026-14.t: Ankara is positioning itself as a security partner of Riyadh, in line with the Mecca Defence Alliance.

S20261026-15.h: Egypt weighs helping defend Saudi Arabia, haunted by 1960s Yemen war
S20261026-15.s: Egypt is considering whether to help defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks. Its experience in the 1960s Yemen war weighs heavily on the decision.

S20261026-16.h: Yemeni government rejects talks letting Houthis rearm as fighting widens
S20261026-16.s: Yemen's foreign minister said a decade of talks with the Houthis failed and rejects negotiations that let them rearm. The army reports heavy operations and a smuggling interception. Houthi missiles hit near Aden and attacks on Taiz caused civilian casualties.

S20261026-17.h: Türkiye warns Washington new strikes on Iran would widen regional conflict
S20261026-17.s: Türkiye warned the US against fresh military strikes on Iran, arguing a new attack would widen the regional conflict.
S20261026-17.t: Ankara is publicly distancing itself from a US strike while it keeps channels open to both Washington and Tehran.

S20261026-18.h: Turkish parliament committee starts debate on ratifying Mecca Defence Alliance
S20261026-18.s: Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee begins debating the bill to ratify the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on Tuesday. It sits alongside the 2027 budget debate.
S20261026-18.t: Ratification would formalise Türkiye's defence commitments to Gulf partners just as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia escalate.

S20261026-19.h: Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt sign statement blaming Israel for instability
S20261026-19.s: The four states signed a statement blaming Israel for regional instability, reflecting alignment among major regional powers.
S20261026-19.t: The statement shows Türkiye working in a bloc of regional powers against Israeli policy.

S20261026-20.h: Türkiye's SİPER long-range air defence Product-2 passes test
S20261026-20.s: Türkiye's long-range SİPER air and missile defence system Product-2 passed a test demonstrating a new capability.
S20261026-20.t: SİPER is central to Türkiye's layered air defence and its drive for indigenous systems.

S20261026-21.h: MKE's TOLGA and PIRANA hit targets in Turkish naval drills
S20261026-21.s: TOLGA close-air defence and the PIRANA kamikaze unmanned boat hit targets in the TURNAs-2026 drill. The Navy concluded its unmanned naval systems exercise with an observer day showing NATO-compatible systems.
S20261026-21.t: The drills show maturing Turkish unmanned naval capability and export potential.

S20261026-22.h: France reportedly weighs delaying Great Sea Interconnector after Türkiye-Libya deal
S20261026-22.s: France is reportedly considering postponing the cable linking Greece, Cyprus and Israel after the Türkiye-Libya maritime deal. A Cypriot legal expert warns Türkiye may use the Libya deal as a precedent against Cyprus's maritime rights.
S20261026-22.t: A delay would be a gain for Türkiye's Eastern Mediterranean maritime claims.

S20261026-23.h: Israel and Greece hold naval exercise simulating sinking hostile ships
S20261026-23.s: Israel and Greece held a joint naval exercise with both navy commanders attending, simulating the sinking of hostile ships.
S20261026-23.t: The Israel-Greece military tie is viewed in Ankara as directed at Türkiye in the Eastern Mediterranean.

S20261026-24.h: Turkish fund and market probes widen, with arrests of ex-AKP MP and insurer executive
S20261026-24.s: Former AK Party MP Ertan Aydın was arrested after re-detention in a capital markets fund investigation. A Türkiye Sigorta deputy manager was also arrested, and a fraud probe covers opposition lawmaker Mustafa Sarıgül. The Justice Minister says prosecutors will prioritise protecting well-intentioned investors.

S20261026-25.h: Rallies in Istanbul and Ankara against arrests and media takeovers; opposition feuds
S20261026-25.s: Thousands rallied against arrests, media shutdowns and state-appointed administrators at news outlets. The CHP and the New Party are in a cash dispute, and Özgür Özel says the country is in a 'civil coup process'.

S20261026-26.h: Erdoğan cabinet to discuss market measures and Terror-Free Türkiye process
S20261026-26.s: Erdoğan's cabinet meets at Beştepe to discuss financial market measures, the process to end PKK violence and regional issues. Slavoj Žižek wrote to Öcalan backing his role in the process.

S20261026-27.h: Russia pounds Ukraine: 1,600 guided bombs, 48 missiles, 2,300 drones in a week
S20261026-27.s: Zelensky says Russia used these weapons in one week. Overnight attacks killed several civilians in Vinnytsia, Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk and elsewhere, and hit energy sites and retail chains.
S20261026-27.t: The intensity of the war keeps Black Sea security and Türkiye's mediation role in play.

S20261026-28.h: Kremlin ready to resume trilateral talks after 4 November; Zelensky sets conditions
S20261026-28.s: Ushakov says Moscow will resume talks with the US and Ukraine after 4 November, expecting only a preliminary meeting, and says Europe should be included. Zelensky says technical talks must precede any leaders' summit and territory is a red line. Zelensky announced a security meeting in Brussels this week.
S20261026-28.t: A restart of talks gives Türkiye room to offer venues and mediation, which has been largely crowded out by Abu Dhabi.

S20261026-29.h: Kremlin says preparations begin for Putin-Trump-Xi summit
S20261026-29.s: Ushakov says Moscow, Beijing and Washington are ready in principle for a trilateral summit in China. A Putin-Trump meeting at APEC is possible but not arranged.

S20261026-30.h: Ukraine hits Russian industry, including Perm titanium plant and Iskander battery maker
S20261026-30.s: Drones hit the Avisma titanium plant in Perm Krai, over 1,400 km from the border. Missiles reportedly hit the Energiya plant in Yelets, which makes batteries for Iskander and Kinzhal missiles. Ukraine also struck radar stations and command posts and hit Belgorod and Omsk.

S20261026-31.h: Zelensky offers refinery-for-grid strike trade as sign of Russian intent
S20261026-31.s: Zelensky said Ukraine would halt strikes on refineries if Russia stops attacking the power grid. He said an energy truce could signal real Russian readiness and that Putin's peace statements may be a trick.

S20261026-32.h: Musk says Starlink was restricted over Ukraine's offensive drone use; service restored
S20261026-32.s: Musk said SpaceX restricted Ukraine's access for using Starlink militarily, and service was later restored. He says the front would collapse without it.

S20261026-33.h: Russia ready to export diesel to the US as Trump praises diesel deal
S20261026-33.s: Deputy PM Novak said Russia can export as much diesel as the US needs. Trump called the deal very good.

S20261026-34.h: Vučić concedes defeat as student-led list wins Serbia's election
S20261026-34.s: Serbian President Vučić conceded defeat to the Student List movement. He said the winners will impose anti-Russian sanctions by spring and called the result a revolution.
S20261026-34.t: A Serbia shift toward the EU would change Balkan alignments where Türkiye has influence.

S20261026-35.h: Israel's election on 27 October: Eisenkot narrowly ahead, neither bloc near 61 seats
S20261026-35.s: Final rallies and polls show a tight race with Eisenkot leading Netanyahu, but neither bloc likely reaching a majority. Security, democracy and the post-war future dominate the campaign.
S20261026-35.t: The result will shape Israel's Gaza, Syria and Iran policy and its relations with Türkiye.

S20261026-36.h: Netanyahu campaigns on Iran fear, posts AI nuclear image over Tel Aviv
S20261026-36.s: Netanyahu warned that Iran and its proxies could attack during the election, telling Tehran 'don't test us'. He also posted an AI-generated image of an atomic bomb over Tel Aviv. Opposition leaders accused him of spreading panic.

S20261026-37.h: Trump urges Israelis to vote Netanyahu and 'finish the job' on Iran
S20261026-37.s: Trump reaffirmed his endorsement of Netanyahu. Axios reports the White House sees Netanyahu's lobbying for it as a sign of desperation, while US officials say they can work with any government.

S20261026-38.h: Israel locks down Hebron, displacing 2,200, and closes West Bank crossings for election
S20261026-38.s: After two Israeli soldiers were killed in Hebron, forces forcibly removed about 2,200 Palestinians, demolished buildings and turned homes into posts. All West Bank crossings will close on election day. A large West Bank operation was also reported.

S20261026-39.h: Israeli strikes continue in Gaza despite ceasefire; post-truce toll passes 1,550
S20261026-39.s: Strikes killed several Palestinians, including three at the Islamic University in Gaza City. Netanyahu has postponed Gaza security arrangements, including the international force, until after the election.
S20261026-39.t: The delayed international force question affects Türkiye's hopes for a role in Gaza.

S20261026-40.h: Israel on alert over Syria's Druze as Damascus defends actions as sovereignty
S20261026-40.s: Israel is on alert for renewed attacks on Syria's Druze, and Damascus told it that its actions aim at sovereignty, not civilians. Experts criticised Barrack's accusations against Syrian Druze, Israeli forces detained three in a southern Syria incursion, and gunmen blocked the Sweida-Damascus highway.
S20261026-40.t: Israeli activity in southern Syria competes with Türkiye's influence in Damascus.

S20261026-41.h: Iraq shuts Iran crossings to avoid being drawn into fighting
S20261026-41.s: Iraq closed its crossings with Iran. Maysan officials gave Baghdad three days to reopen the al-Shib crossing, and the Kurdistan Region denied hosting Ukrainian drones.

S20261026-42.h: Iran reportedly strikes Iranian Kurdish base in Iraq with drones
S20261026-42.s: Asharq Al-Awsat reports Iran hit an Iranian Kurdish base in Iraq with drones.
S20261026-42.t: Strikes on Kurdish groups in Iraq bear on Türkiye's own Kurdish and border security calculations.

S20261026-43.h: Gunmen attack on Jordan church kills eight; hunt for attackers continues
S20261026-43.s: Thousands mourned eight victims of the attack on St George's Church in Karak. The hunt for the gunmen continues.

S20261026-44.h: Europe's opposition to renewed Iran strikes grows with energy costs; Tehran rebukes Germany
S20261026-44.s: Rising energy costs and protests are increasing European opposition to renewed US-Israeli attacks. Iran's Foreign Ministry criticised Germany and EU states for contradictory stances.

S20261026-45.h: Pezeshkian to visit Moscow as Iran seeks closer Russian gas and trade ties
S20261026-45.s: Pezeshkian is set to visit Moscow next week for talks with Putin. Iran also seeks gas cooperation at the GECF summit in Russia and Russian supplies to reduce reliance on southern ports.
S20261026-45.t: Russia-Iran gas coordination affects Türkiye's role as a regional energy hub.

S20261017-01.h: Houthi missiles hit Aden presidential palace, killing five
S20261017-01.s: Houthi ballistic missiles struck the Al-Maashiq presidential palace in Aden, the government's interim capital, killing five and injuring 16. It was the first attack on the palace. The prime minister and other ministers were unhurt. The Houthis said they targeted a Saudi military operations headquarters at the complex. A Yemeni official said the government will stay in Aden.
S20261017-01.t: Escalation in Yemen raises questions about whether Ankara could be drawn into a Gulf-Houthi war.

S20261017-02.h: Iran says Hormuz stays closed to uncoordinated shipping; burning tanker spotted
S20261017-02.s: Iranian army officials repeated that the Strait of Hormuz remains closed to uncoordinated passage. The army chief said it stays closed until Iran's rights are respected. The Iranian Navy reported spotting a non-compliant oil tanker on fire in the strait.
S20261017-02.t: A prolonged Hormuz closure keeps energy prices and Türkiye's import bill under pressure.

S20261017-03.h: Trump says US may need to strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain
S20261017-03.s: President Trump said the US may have to target Pickaxe Mountain, a site linked to Iran's nuclear programme. Iranian outlets responded with commentary that a strike would not rescue Trump from the war. Iran's ambassador in Berlin called the new US threats a sign of desperation.
S20261017-03.t: Renewed US strike talk against Iran's nuclear sites threatens wider regional instability on Türkiye's border.

S20261017-04.h: Drone attacks on seven Black Sea ships; Bulgaria asks NATO for support
S20261017-04.s: Seven commercial ships were hit by drones in the Black Sea. Bulgaria's defence minister asked NATO for support after the attacks increased. Ukraine and Türkiye discussed securing shipping with $10bn in exports at risk. Ukraine's foreign minister said the Black Sea could become a second Hormuz for food security.
S20261017-04.t: Türkiye is the Black Sea's key littoral state and NATO member, so the Article 5 debate and the shipping risk land in Ankara.

S20261017-05.h: Trump calls Zelensky harder to deal with than Putin; Europe rallies behind Kyiv
S20261017-05.s: Trump called Ukraine's renewed refinery strikes 'a disgrace' and said Zelensky is 'more difficult to deal with than Putin'. Zelensky replied that Ukraine has the right to defend itself and that he finds Trump easier to talk to than Putin. EU leaders rallied around him, and Politico sources said they did not ask him to tone down his criticism.
S20261017-05.t: A US-Ukraine rift complicates Ankara's mediation role and its balancing between Washington, Kyiv and Moscow.

S20261017-06.h: US-Russia 'diesel deal' draws Zelensky warning and congressional bills to block it
S20261017-06.s: Zelensky warned that Washington's diesel deal with Moscow could open the door to broader sanctions relief, with gas and banks next. EU leaders regretted the temporary lifting of US sanctions on Russian diesel. US lawmakers including Gregory Meeks introduced bills to block the deal. Putin said Russia and the US will soon announce further joint initiatives.
S20261017-06.t: Easing of Russian energy sanctions would shift the energy and trade calculus Ankara works within.

S20261017-07.h: Houthi-Saudi air war: coalition downs drones, Houthis claim a Typhoon
S20261017-07.s: The Yemen coalition said it shot down three drones over southern Saudi Arabia and the Riyadh region and destroyed two cruise missiles over the Red Sea. Houthi-aligned forces claimed to have downed a Saudi Typhoon over Sa'ada. The UN Security Council condemned Houthi attacks, and Saudi organisers said the Asian Cup is on schedule. A Turkish op-ed asked whether Türkiye could be dragged into the Yemen war.
S20261017-07.t: A Turkish opinion piece asks whether Ankara could be pulled into the war if Washington asks.

S20261017-08.h: Houthis hit Aden airport with two missiles
S20261017-08.s: The Yemeni government says the Houthis fired two missiles at Aden airport, with no casualties reported by police. It was the second such attack on the airport in less than a week.

S20261017-09.h: Houthis besiege Taiz as Yemeni army claims gains in Marib
S20261017-09.s: The Taiz governor says the Houthis have closed all roads into the city for 15 days, and power and water stations have shut for lack of fuel. Fighting intensified south of Taiz. The army separately says it recaptured strategic sites in Marib and neutralised over 430 Houthi fighters in 24 hours.

S20261017-10.h: Iran offers to mediate Saudi-Yemen dispute, denies role in Houthi operations
S20261017-10.s: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman offered to mediate and denied any Iranian role in Yemen's military operations. Araghchi stressed historical Iran-Yemen ties. A former Yemeni insider told Iran International that Tehran spent years cultivating the Houthis through Hezbollah recruiters and IRGC officers.

S20261017-11.h: Trump says Israel helped against Houthis; Abraham Accords with Riyadh back on table
S20261017-11.s: Trump said Israel aided the war against the Houthis and that Saudi Arabia may accept Israeli help. He expressed confidence the Abraham Accords could gain renewed momentum. Haaretz reports Netanyahu is trying, with US mediation, to persuade Riyadh to allow Israel to play a role.
S20261017-11.t: Saudi-Israel normalisation and Israeli military roles near the Red Sea would reshape the regional balance Ankara watches.

S20261017-12.h: US blockade bites Iran, but some LPG and jet fuel still ship
S20261017-12.s: CENTCOM says 1.3 billion barrels moved under US escort in Hormuz and Iran is cut off from $25bn in crude exports. Reuters and UANI data show Iran still shipped some LPG and jet fuel despite the blockade. Pezeshkian calls it the toughest blockade since 1979 and says Iran will not bow to coercion. South Korea is reviewing an expanded Middle East mission.
S20261017-12.t: Blockade leakage and Iranian economic distress affect Türkiye's border trade and energy sourcing.

S20261017-13.h: Lavrov to visit Tehran on October 19 as Iran courts Moscow
S20261017-13.s: Russia's foreign minister will meet Araghchi in Tehran. Iran's ambassador in Moscow said the US is not serious about negotiating and that force will lead nowhere. Tehran also plans to invite Gazprom to develop Iranian gas fields.
S20261017-13.t: Closer Russia-Iran energy and diplomatic coordination touches Türkiye's gas supply options.

S20261017-14.h: Netanyahu says he spoke with al-Sharaa over Druze unrest; Katz mocks Damascus
S20261017-14.s: Netanyahu said he spoke with Syria's leader to stop violence against the Druze. Damascus has not confirmed the call, and Syrian sources say the two talked last year with US and Arab mediation. Katz said al-Sharaa is waiting for Netanyahu's election defeat.
S20261017-14.t: Israeli-Syrian channels shape the limits of Türkiye's own influence in Damascus.

S20261017-15.h: Israeli incursion in Quneitra; Syria and EU invoke 1974 disengagement accord
S20261017-15.s: Five Israeli military vehicles entered the southern Quneitra countryside. Syria reaffirmed its commitment to the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and called for an end to incursions. The EU backed Syria's institution-building and urged Israel to respect the agreement.
S20261017-15.t: Israeli ground presence in southern Syria constrains Türkiye's own Syria posture and deconfliction.

S20261017-16.h: Syrian FM visits Riyadh, meets Saudi counterpart
S20261017-16.s: Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani arrived in Riyadh heading a delegation and met Faisal bin Farhan.
S20261017-16.t: Saudi-Syrian ties show competing Gulf influence in Damascus alongside Türkiye.

S20261017-17.h: Syria and Türkiye foreign ministers discuss ties and stability by phone
S20261017-17.s: Syrian Foreign Minister al-Shaibani held a phone call with his Turkish counterpart on bilateral ties and stability.
S20261017-17.t: Routine contact keeps Ankara close to the Damascus government.

S20261017-18.h: Syria captures Assad-era militia leader Mihraç Ural, wanted by Türkiye
S20261017-18.s: Syrian authorities announced the arrest of Mihraç Ural (Ali Kayali), a Turkish-born militia leader. A Syrian source said he was captured in Lebanon. Ankara sought him over the deadly Reyhanlı bombings, and Syria links him to the 2013 Baniyas massacre.
S20261017-18.t: Ankara has sought Ural over the Reyhanlı bombings, so his capture is a security and justice win for it.

S20261017-19.h: Hezbollah says seized explosives were for attacks on Israel; Rubio urges non-return
S20261017-19.s: A Hezbollah lawmaker said the confiscated explosives were meant for attacks on Israeli troops. Rubio urged Lebanon not to return them to the group, and Lebanese figures fear they were meant for assassinations. Haaretz profiles Nabih Berri as Hezbollah's shield.

S20261017-20.h: Qatar's PM in Beirut pledges energy projects, urges Israeli withdrawal
S20261017-20.s: Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman met Lebanese leaders, reaffirmed support for Lebanon's sovereignty and announced a large solar plant. He called for Israeli withdrawal. Lebanon's foreign minister said Beirut wants an international force to replace UNIFIL.
S20261017-20.t: Qatar, a close Turkish partner, is expanding its role in Lebanon's reconstruction.

S20261017-21.h: Gaza malnutrition gains fragile as Israel halts commercial goods
S20261017-21.s: The UN says Gaza's malnutrition gains are fragile after Israel halted commercial shipments over a dispute. Commercial goods have not entered for two days. Israel is also blocking wastewater equipment, and UNICEF says over 340 children were killed despite the ceasefire. The Security Council discussed rising violence.
S20261017-21.t: Ankara presses for action over the Gaza humanitarian crisis.

S20261017-22.h: Israeli fire kills Palestinians in Gaza despite ceasefire; IDF kills Hamas commander
S20261017-22.s: An Israeli drone strike killed a Palestinian in northwestern Gaza and another died of wounds. The IDF said it killed a Hamas Nukhba commander who took part in the October 7 Re'im base attack.

S20261017-23.h: Israel blocks US contractor from entering Gaza for Board of Peace base
S20261017-23.s: A US contractor awarded a project to build a fortified base for 150 international troops has been unable to enter Gaza, according to the Guardian, as Israel's election nears.
S20261017-23.t: Türkiye is engaged in the Gaza Peace Council track, so obstruction affects its stake.

S20261017-24.h: Settlers burn olive groves and attack journalist in West Bank
S20261017-24.s: Masked Israeli settlers burned olive trees at Abu Falah and Turmus Ayya and attacked farmers and a Washington Post photographer during the olive harvest. A rabbi reportedly said harvesting Palestinian olives demonstrates ownership.

S20261017-25.h: Sisi rejects Smotrich Sinai remarks, says Egypt buildup is defensive
S20261017-25.s: Egypt's president reaffirmed the peace treaty and rejected suggestions of territorial ambitions after Smotrich's comments. He said 'if they attack, there will be no Sinai' and that Egypt's military expansion is not aimed at Israel, amid reports Netanyahu questioned it.

S20261017-26.h: Italy names Katz and senior Israelis in flotilla activist abuse probe
S20261017-26.s: Italian prosecutors named Defence Minister Katz and senior military, police and prison officials in an investigation over alleged abuse of flotilla activists across two missions.

S20261017-27.h: Colombia opens embassy in Jerusalem; Iran, Qatar and others condemn
S20261017-27.s: Colombia opened its embassy in Jerusalem after restoring ties with Israel. Iran and 19 other countries and Qatar condemned the move.

S20261017-28.h: Israeli election race tightens as Eisenkot challenges Netanyahu
S20261017-28.s: Netanyahu is rallying right-wing voters while Eisenkot makes his move. Lieberman says Eisenkot is keeping open a minority government with Netanyahu. Anadolu notes the main parties reject Palestinian statehood.

S20261017-29.h: Zelensky asks EU for €70bn extra for 2027 and frozen Russian assets
S20261017-29.s: At a Brussels summit Zelensky said the war will cost €155bn next year and asked for at least €70bn more, plus Patriot missiles. Von der Leyen confirmed a €70bn shortfall. The Danish PM and Sybiha urged use of frozen Russian assets, and a new sanctions package is on the way. Leaders deferred big budget and funding decisions to later meetings.

S20261017-30.h: Zelensky: Europe building separate dialogue track with Russia
S20261017-30.s: Zelensky said Ukraine is negotiating with European partners to set up a separate European track for dialogue with Russia aimed at ending the war. Kallas said Europe is trying to convince the US to pressure Russia.
S20261017-30.t: A European channel could compete with Türkiye's own mediation hosting role.

S20261017-31.h: Zelensky and Hungary's Magyar agree to resume high-level talks
S20261017-31.s: In their first one-on-one meeting Zelensky and Hungarian PM Péter Magyar agreed to resume high-level talks and bilateral visits. Magyar said Hungary is ready to give diplomatic help toward a ceasefire. Sybiha called it a fresh start.

S20261017-32.h: EU sets Ukraine task force on rule of law as Moldova track debated
S20261017-32.s: The EU and Ukraine agreed a joint task force on justice and anti-corruption reforms. Ukraine hopes to open the last negotiating clusters by year-end. Zelensky urged keeping Moldova's bid tied to Ukraine's, while commentary says Moldova could overtake it.
S20261017-32.t: EU enlargement moves highlight Türkiye's own stalled accession.

S20261017-33.h: Starlink access for Ukraine's military only partly restored
S20261017-33.s: Zelensky said speed restrictions hampered military and humanitarian operations and called the US limits a 'dangerous and unpleasant surprise'. Speeds are recovering but not fully restored, and Kyiv is working with France on alternatives. Trump denied limiting access, and Ukraine says it gets ballistic missile launch data from the US.

S20261017-34.h: Ukraine resumes refinery strikes after 'energy ceasefire' collapses
S20261017-34.s: Zelensky said Ukraine is resuming strikes on Russian oil refineries because Russia did not respect the energy ceasefire. He said Ukraine would stop if the US provided Starlink coverage inside Russia. The Kremlin claims the attacks never stopped, and Putin warned Kyiv over strikes on energy sites and data centres.

S20261017-35.h: Ukraine hits Siberian chemical plant, Su-34s, radar and Yandex data centres
S20261017-35.s: Drones started a fire at an industrial facility in Russia's Surgut district, about 3,000 km from Ukraine. Ukraine also reportedly destroyed Su-34 aircraft on the ground and a Nebo-U radar near Krasnodar worth about $100m. Strikes on Yandex data centres disrupted Russian court operations.

S20261017-36.h: Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi regains ground in Donetsk
S20261017-36.s: Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi reclaimed more occupied territory in Donetsk, with Starlink playing a key role. Over 300 clashes were reported in 24 hours, most in the Pokrovsk sector.

S20261017-37.h: Putin: 'security zone' in Ukraine non-negotiable, Dobropillia taken
S20261017-37.s: Putin said a security zone along the border is not subject to peace talks. He said Russian forces took Dobropillia and are advancing along the whole front, and that massive strikes will continue. Russian outlets claim further villages taken and control of the Volchansk-Budarki highway.

S20261017-38.h: Russia presses mass strikes on Ukraine's energy grid ahead of winter
S20261017-38.s: Gerasimov confirmed massive strikes on Ukrainian energy and other infrastructure. A New York Times report says Russia aims to cut power, heat and water in Kyiv, Kharkiv and Odesa to force surrender. Ukrenergo says winter scenarios worsened. Russia launched 315 drones and 15 missiles on October 16, and Ukraine downed 253 drones and nine missiles.

S20261017-39.h: UN: civilian casualties in Ukraine at record levels; Kharkiv strikes kill several
S20261017-39.s: The UN said 328 civilians were killed and 2,105 injured in September, with energy attacks intensifying. Russian strikes on Kharkiv killed at least five across several attacks, including a market, and a drone attack injured seven in Rivne.

S20261017-40.h: Pope Leo asks Putin for truce in Oleshky; Putin agrees to cooperate
S20261017-40.s: In a phone call Pope Leo XIV asked Putin for a ceasefire to deliver aid and evacuate civilians from occupied Oleshky. Putin agreed to cooperate and blamed Kyiv for the humanitarian situation.

S20261017-41.h: Russian drones violate Moldovan airspace; Poland scrambles jets
S20261017-41.s: Several drones entered Moldova's airspace during overnight Russian attacks on Ukraine. Poland scrambled fighters as Russia struck western Ukraine.
S20261017-41.t: The spillover raises NATO flank concerns that bear on Black Sea security.

S20261017-42.h: Belgium to send 10 F-16s to Ukraine; allies add air-defence support
S20261017-42.s: Belgian PM De Wever said ten F-16s will be delivered by year-end. Macron said France is accelerating missile deliveries. Zelensky said Europe has enough Patriot missiles for the winter, and Sweden and Finland discussed air defence, Gripens and shelters.

S20261017-43.h: Trump says US, Russia and China to sign nuclear arms control agreements
S20261017-43.s: Trump said he raised nuclear arms control with Putin and that the US, Russia and China will sign agreements.

S20261017-44.h: Deadly floods hit Istanbul in worst rainfall in 80 years
S20261017-44.s: Torrential rain caused deadly floods in and near Istanbul. One missing man was found dead and a search continues for three others. Türkiye put 55,560 personnel on alert, Erdoğan said state institutions are working in coordination, and Pakistan offered assistance.
S20261017-44.t: The disaster strains Istanbul's infrastructure and AFAD capacity just before COP31 hosting.

S20261017-45.h: İmamoğlu trial defence alleges $85bn zoning giveaway by ruling party
S20261017-45.s: Jailed Istanbul mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu used his trial defence to accuse the AKP of allowing an $85bn zoning giveaway. Medyascope published the full text of his defence.
S20261017-45.t: The trial keeps domestic polarisation and Türkiye's rule-of-law image in focus for Western partners.

S20261017-46.h: MSCI freezes Turkish index changes as Erdoğan says fund crisis controlled
S20261017-46.s: MSCI restricted changes to its Turkish stock indexes over concerns about possible coordinated trading and warned of a downgrade. Erdoğan said the fund crisis is under control and that 'terrorising' capital markets undermines the economy. Regulators fined two TV stations over fund coverage, and police detained a journalist and relatives of an opposition lawmaker in a money-laundering probe.
S20261017-46.t: A possible market downgrade would hit investor confidence and financing costs.

S20261017-47.h: CHP expels 48 members as Muğla mayor quits party
S20261017-47.s: The CHP's disciplinary board expelled 48 members and officials, including Selin Sayek Böke, accused of serving rival wings. Muğla Metropolitan mayor Ahmet Aras resigned from the CHP to continue as an independent.
S20261017-47.t: Opposition infighting weakens the main challenger to Erdoğan.

S20261017-48.h: Erdoğan adviser signals March or April 2028 elections
S20261017-48.s: Mehmet Uçum said Türkiye is likely to vote in presidential and parliamentary elections in March or April 2028.
S20261017-48.t: The election timing frames Erdoğan's constitutional and succession calculations.

S20261017-49.h: Azerbaijan-Türkiye row over school headscarf ban escalates
S20261017-49.s: The AKP called for easing tensions with Azerbaijan over its school headscarf ban. Azerbaijan charged a Turkish columnist with calling for the violent overthrow of the government. Iranian hardliners also condemned the rules.
S20261017-49.t: Friction with Baku, Türkiye's closest partner in the Caucasus, is awkward for Ankara.

S20261017-50.h: Erdoğan hosts Cambodia's Hun Manet; military cooperation deal signed
S20261017-50.s: Erdoğan received Cambodian PM Hun Manet, called Cambodia an important Southeast Asian partner and welcomed it as a founding member of the Gaza Peace Council. Türkiye and Cambodia signed a military cooperation deal.
S20261017-50.t: The deal extends Türkiye's defence-diplomacy footprint in Southeast Asia.

S20261017-51.h: Türkiye welcomes new Iraqi cabinet appointments
S20261017-51.s: The Turkish Foreign Ministry welcomed Iraq's parliamentary confidence vote on new cabinet members. It expects faster cooperation on the Development Road project, energy and water.
S20261017-51.t: Cooperation on the Development Road, energy and water is at stake.

S20261017-52.h: Fidan to attend OIC foreign ministers' meeting in Baghdad
S20261017-52.s: Hakan Fidan is expected to call for unity on Palestine and discuss regional security at the OIC meeting.
S20261017-52.t: The meeting lets Ankara press its Palestine and regional-security agenda.

S20261017-53.h: Gazprom's Miller meets Turkish energy minister on gas cooperation
S20261017-53.s: Gazprom CEO Alexey Miller and Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar discussed prospects for natural gas cooperation.
S20261017-53.t: Russian gas remains central to Türkiye's supply and hub ambitions.

S20261017-54.h: Erdoğan stresses defence-tech push; Türkiye shows 53 new weapons
S20261017-54.s: Erdoğan said Türkiye exported over $10bn in defence and aerospace products in 2025, to 180 countries and regions, and called investment in advanced technology a necessity. Türkiye also showcased 53 weapons for the first time.
S20261017-54.t: Defence exports are a growing source of Turkish leverage and revenue.

S20261017-55.h: Israel likely to miss COP31 in Antalya amid security fears
S20261017-55.s: Israel is likely to miss the climate summit in Türkiye next month amid security concerns and diplomatic isolation. Türkiye's UN envoy said COP31 aims for concrete results.
S20261017-55.t: Türkiye's role as COP31 host collides with its tensions with Israel.

S20261017-56.h: Kurtulmuş says 'Terror-Free Türkiye' process advances with public support
S20261017-56.s: Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş said the process is proceeding in line with overwhelming national support and urged people not to panic.
S20261017-56.t: The process to end PKK violence is central to Türkiye's domestic politics and Syria and Iraq policy.

S20261017-57.h: Iran diplomacy draws Kurdistan region leaders together as divisions deepen
S20261017-57.s: Remarks by senior Kurdistan region leaders at the MERI Forum have put relations with Iran in focus, even as political divisions deepen.

S20261017-58.h: EU-Türkiye summit in October aims to restart Cyprus talks
S20261017-58.s: Euronews reports that an EU-Türkiye summit in October aims to restart Cyprus talks.
S20261017-58.t: A reset with the EU on Cyprus could unlock wider ties.

S20261017-59.h: US senator Scott blames Turkey and Erdoğan for Cyprus problem
S20261017-59.s: Senator Rick Scott said the Cyprus problem was 'all caused by Turkey' and Erdoğan. Cyprus's energy minister told him of the island's need for an electricity interconnector.
S20261017-59.t: Hostile US congressional rhetoric complicates Ankara's Washington relations.

S20261017-60.h: Cypriot concern over Israel's growing influence and pro-Israel lobby
S20261017-60.s: Al Jazeera reports that Israel's reach into Cyprus's water, gas, health and defence worries many Cypriots. A pro-Israel parliamentary lobby group launched in the Greek Cypriot administration, sparking a political row.
S20261017-60.t: Israel-Cyprus ties add to Türkiye's Eastern Mediterranean security concerns.

S20261017-61.h: Türkiye plans tender for Kanal İstanbul project
S20261017-61.s: The Transport and Infrastructure Ministry aims to invite bids and begin construction 'as soon as possible'.
S20261017-61.t: A canal would affect the Montreux regime and Black Sea balances.

S20261017-62.h: Spiegel: Turkish crime gang may have burned Starlink station in Poland for Russia
S20261017-62.s: Russian intelligence may have hired the Turkish criminal gang the Daltons to set fire to a Starlink ground station in Poland, Spiegel reports.
S20261017-62.t: Turkish organised crime used in Russian sabotage in a NATO state would be a reputational and security problem for Ankara.

S20261018-01.h: IRGC says second supertanker hits mine in Hormuz as US and Iran claim control
S20261018-01.s: The IRGC Navy says a second supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels of crude caught fire after hitting a sea mine in the Strait of Hormuz. It alleges the vessel switched off its tracking at US instigation. Trump says the US Navy blockade has stopped all Iranian ships, and the IRGC warns vessels breaking its Hormuz rules.
S20261018-01.t: Turkey, an energy importer, has called for free navigation in Hormuz, and a prolonged closure threatens its fuel costs and trade.

S20261018-02.h: Iran sets Hormuz conditions as US threatens 'devastation' and indirect talks continue
S20261018-02.s: Araghchi says Iran will not yield to pressure but stays open to dialogue, and calls the choice on its Hormuz terms America's. An Iranian lawmaker says indirect talks continue through Qatar and Oman. Hegseth says Tehran must choose between a deal and devastation, and Trump says US forces may stay longer. Al-Monitor reports the diplomatic window may be closing.
S20261018-02.t: A failed US-Iran track or renewed strikes would hit Turkey's border security, energy supply and trade.

S20261018-03.h: Houthi missiles and drones hit Saudi Arabia; coalition intercepts and claims Apache downing
S20261018-03.s: The Saudi-led coalition says it downed drones over Riyadh and eastern and southern Saudi Arabia. It also intercepted ballistic and cruise missiles, including one headed for Yanbu, and destroyed two Houthi launch platforms in Saada. The Houthis claim they shot down a Saudi Apache near the border, and alerts sounded in Riyadh, Abha and Khamis Mushait.
S20261018-03.t: Escalation in the Red Sea and Arabian Peninsula threatens regional stability and Turkey's Gulf economic and defence ties.

S20261018-04.h: Houthi missiles strike Aden airport and presidential palace, landing near passenger plane
S20261018-04.s: The Yemeni government says the Houthis fired two missiles at Aden airport, which landed near a passenger plane. Al Jazeera also reports strikes on the presidential palace. The government calls the attack a direct threat to passengers and a violation of international law.

S20261018-05.h: WSJ: Iran gives Houthis targeting intelligence for strikes on Saudi Arabia; Tehran denies, offers mediation
S20261018-05.s: The Wall Street Journal reports Iran is supplying the Houthis with targeting intelligence for their most sophisticated attacks yet on Saudi Arabia. Iran's Foreign Ministry denies a role in the attacks and says it is ready to help resolve the Saudi-Houthi dispute.
S20261018-05.t: Iranian proxy escalation against Riyadh complicates Ankara's balancing between Tehran and the Gulf.

S20261018-06.h: UAE agrees with Saudi Arabia to re-enter Yemen conflict as Houthis gain
S20261018-06.s: The Guardian reports the UAE will reportedly resume payments to Yemeni forces after Houthi gains alarmed Gulf states. Yemeni government forces claim about 800 Houthis killed or wounded in 24 hours, while Al Jazeera asks whether their offensive can be sustained under Houthi missile threats to supply routes.
S20261018-06.t: A re-united Saudi-UAE line in Yemen shifts Gulf alignments Ankara must account for.

S20261018-07.h: Sisi seeks parliament backing to defend Saudi Arabia if asked
S20261018-07.s: Egypt's president says Cairo would take any measure to defend Saudi Arabia if Riyadh requests it. He asked for an emergency parliamentary session to authorise this. Separately, Saudi Arabia's foreign minister discussed the Houthi escalation with his Syrian counterpart.
S20261018-07.t: Egyptian military backing for Riyadh marks a new Arab security alignment that Turkey, now repairing ties with Cairo, must watch.

S20261018-08.h: Sisi says his presidency ends in 2030, rules out constitutional change
S20261018-08.s: Sisi said his term will end in 2030 and that this is entirely settled. He rejected speculation about amending the constitution and outlined a plan to prepare future leaders.

S20261018-09.h: Trump waives Graham Act Russia sanctions and tariffs; Zelensky calls it wrong
S20261018-09.s: Trump signed an order suspending the main sanctions and tariffs under the new Graham Act, which would have raised duties on Russian goods by up to 500% and targeted importers of Russian energy. Zelensky calls it a reward for Putin and an 'American sanctions blackout', and expects more relief to follow the 'diesel deal'.
S20261018-09.t: Sanctions relief affects Russian energy flows, Turkey's gas and oil trade with Moscow and its role as a mediator.

S20261018-10.h: US lawmakers move to block Trump's Russian diesel deal; EU leaders voice regret
S20261018-10.s: Democrat Gregory Meeks introduced a bipartisan House bill restricting US investment in Russia's energy sector to block the diesel deal. EU leaders expressed regret over the deal in their summit conclusions, and Macron called it inappropriate and ineffective.

S20261018-11.h: Russia touts first tanker of oil to world markets as Novak warns of Hormuz price risk
S20261018-11.s: Russian Deputy PM Novak says the first tanker carrying Russian oil has been loaded and departed. He said oil prices could rise if Hormuz is not settled, as stockpile capacity to stabilise markets is almost exhausted. Russia also says it will deliver 39 bcm of gas to China via Power of Siberia, and Indian commentators see Trump's tariff waiver as relief.
S20261018-11.t: Higher prices and Russian rerouting of oil and gas bear on Turkey's energy import bill and hub ambitions.

S20261018-12.h: Russia hits Ukrainian energy grid and steel plants in one of largest attacks
S20261018-12.s: Russia launched over 330 drones plus Iskander, Kalibr and Kh-22/32 missiles overnight. Zelensky says more than 15 energy facilities were hit, and Ukrainian air defences downed 289 drones and four Kalibrs. Strikes killed several people, cut power to about a million and hit Zaporizhstal and Kryvyi Rih metals plants, while Moscow says it hit defence-linked enterprises.
S20261018-12.t: Black Sea and energy-grid attacks sustain pressure on Ukraine and on regional security Turkey borders.

S20261018-13.h: Zelensky: Russia wants ballistic missiles in Belarus to hit western Ukraine
S20261018-13.s: Zelensky says signal repeaters in Belarus already help Russian drones reach western Ukraine and Moscow wants to deploy ballistic missile systems there. Ukraine is reinforcing air defence in the west, which Kyiv sees as an attempt to draw it into the war, and Poland scrambled aircraft during strikes in the west.

S20261018-14.h: Starlink speed limits cripple Ukraine's drone interception; Musk reportedly proposed them to Trump
S20261018-14.s: Zelensky says Starlink speed limits apply only in Ukraine and make it impossible to use on interceptors against jet-powered Shaheds. Europe is working on alternatives, and the Telegraph reports Musk proposed the slowdown to Trump. Italy's defence minister called the US move a major mistake.
S20261018-14.t: The episode shows how dependence on a single US-controlled satellite network can constrain military operations, a lesson for Turkey's own defence industry.

S20261018-15.h: Zelensky says US-Ukraine teams may meet next week; Putin meeting unconfirmed
S20261018-15.s: Zelensky says Ukrainian and US negotiating teams may meet next week and the US is working on a possible meeting with Putin. Neither Washington nor Moscow has confirmed a Miami or G20 trilateral, and Trump says he does not know whether Putin will attend the G20 in the US.
S20261018-15.t: Turkey has sought to host Russia-Ukraine talks, and a US-run track diminishes that role.

S20261018-16.h: EU summit pledges Ukraine support, tasks Commission with €70bn for 2027
S20261018-16.s: EU leaders reaffirmed support for Ukraine, backed security guarantees, and promised more pressure on Russia's energy revenues. They tasked the Commission with finding €70bn for Ukraine in 2027 while demanding reforms as a condition for funding. They also called for restored Black Sea navigation and an end to outside help for Russia.
S20261018-16.t: EU Black Sea navigation language and Ukraine security guarantees touch Turkey's Montreux role and NATO position.

S20261018-17.h: Fico says Slovakia and Hungary will not fund EU's extra Ukraine aid for 2027
S20261018-17.s: Slovak PM Fico says Slovakia and Hungary will not join the €70bn EU package Zelensky sought. Hungarian PM Péter Magyar met Zelensky in Brussels, spoke of a 'new foundation' for ties and said he has no objection to Ukrainian grain transit, but a Zelensky Budapest visit is unlikely this month.

S20261018-18.h: Ukraine contests Russian claims of capturing Dobropillia and Kostiantynivka as fighting intensifies
S20261018-18.s: Russia claims control of eight more settlements and an advance toward Zaporizhzhia. Ukraine's General Staff and Azov deny this, and report 238 clashes in a day, with Pokrovsk the hottest sector. Ukrainian officials say Russian commanders ordered capture of Orikhiv by end of October.

S20261018-19.h: Ukraine strikes Russian drone plant and Ryazan refinery as Moscow airports close
S20261018-19.s: Ukraine's General Staff confirms hitting the Roboavia drone plant in Rostov Oblast and a missile brigade depot. Ryazan refinery halted a main unit after a drone attack. Moscow reported waves of drones, 144 overnight, and its airports restricted flights for a second night.

S20261018-20.h: Romanian F-16s shoot down two Russian jet-powered drones over Black Sea waters
S20261018-20.s: Two Romanian F-16s downed two Geran-family drones that entered Romanian territorial waters on Saturday evening. Commentary says Black Sea drone strikes could test NATO's response.
S20261018-20.t: A NATO ally shooting down drones in the Black Sea raises the spillover risk for Turkey's own littoral.

S20261018-21.h: Ukraine says Russian troops executed prisoners of war in Zaporizhzhia sector
S20261018-21.s: Ukrainian forces say soldiers of Russia's 38th Motorised Rifle Brigade executed captured Ukrainian soldiers near Huliaipole. Law enforcement has opened a pre-trial investigation.

S20261018-22.h: Hundreds in Kyiv demand Mayor Klitschko resign over winter preparations
S20261018-22.s: Residents rallied outside the city administration over anger at Kyiv's preparations for winter amid attacks on the grid. They called for Klitschko to step down.

S20261018-23.h: European troops to rehearse deployment into Ukraine in Poland in November
S20261018-23.s: The Times reports 1,500 European troops will practise deploying forces to Ukraine in the event of a ceasefire. Poland is also mulling Trump's Russia concessions amid a rift with Washington.

S20261018-24.h: Fidan meets Iraqi, Egyptian and Iranian counterparts at OIC session in Baghdad
S20261018-24.s: Fidan met Iraqi PM al-Zaidi, Egypt's Abdelatty, Iran's Araghchi and Iraq's president on the sidelines of the 52nd OIC foreign ministers' council. Talks covered energy, security, counterterrorism and the Development Road, and he urged the Islamic world to act together on Palestine and regional crises.
S20261018-24.t: Turkey hands the OIC presidency to Iraq and uses Baghdad to push the Development Road, energy and counterterrorism cooperation.

S20261018-25.h: Araghchi at OIC calls for regional security without foreign interference
S20261018-25.s: Araghchi told the OIC council the choice is security together or insecurity together. He met Lebanese, Algerian, Libyan and Egyptian counterparts, and Iran is pushing the OIC to reapprove a resolution on the 12-day war. Iran also urged the UN Security Council to hold Israel to account.

S20261018-26.h: Lavrov tours Gulf and visits Tehran for talks with Araghchi
S20261018-26.s: Lavrov arrived in Bahrain for the 9th Russia-GCC Strategic Dialogue as the first stop on a Middle East tour, and will visit Tehran on Monday to meet Araghchi. Analysis points to Russia-Iran ties amid the US sanctions controversy.
S20261018-26.t: Russian diplomacy with both the GCC and Iran shows Moscow positioning itself in the Gulf crisis Turkey also mediates in.

S20261018-27.h: Lebanon sends military delegation to US-backed trilateral talks with Israel on Oct. 20
S20261018-27.s: President Aoun says a military delegation will attend talks in Florida and press for an end to Israeli attacks, seeking outcomes consistent with the framework agreement. He also asked for UNIFIL's mandate to be extended. Haaretz says Israel is holding back the Lebanese government and giving Hezbollah room to recover.

S20261018-28.h: Lebanon probes abduction of ex-Assad officer taken to Syria
S20261018-28.s: Lebanese judicial and security authorities are investigating the abduction of a former Syrian officer transferred to Syria. Lebanon's justice minister also warned that transporting and storing large quantities of explosives threatens national security.

S20261018-29.h: Settlers attack European diplomats in West Bank; Belgium demands EU sanctions, Netanyahu cites smear
S20261018-29.s: Masked settlers attacked a convoy of European diplomats at Taybeh and beat a visiting French mayor. Belgium called for further EU sanctions, the Israeli military condemned the violence, and Netanyahu's office alleged a smear campaign. A Washington Post photographer was also wounded in settler violence, drawing apologies and condemnation from Herzog, ex-security chiefs and US lawmakers.

S20261018-30.h: Israeli drone strikes in Gaza kill Palestinians despite ceasefire
S20261018-30.s: Israeli strikes killed at least six Palestinians across Gaza, and Israeli forces opened fire and shelled areas of Khan Younis. UNICEF says over 340 children have been killed since the ceasefire began a year ago.
S20261018-30.t: Turkey, a Gaza ceasefire guarantor-aspirant, faces continued violations of the truce.

S20261018-31.h: Israeli forces make new incursions in southern Syria as locals report abuses
S20261018-31.s: Two Israeli military vehicles entered western Daraa countryside under drone cover, and Quneitra's governor urged the UN force to document violations. Al Jazeera reports raids and arrests pushing the population to the brink.
S20261018-31.t: Israel's growing presence in southern Syria constrains Ankara's own influence in Damascus.

S20261018-32.h: Syria's Kurdish autonomy fading as Arab unrest challenges Damascus control
S20261018-32.s: The Jerusalem Post says the Kurdish-led authority was dissolved on paper but many institutions still function. A Syrian army engineer was killed clearing mines near al-Tanf, and Germany weighs Syrian returns as a US lawmaker unveils a bill on minority persecution.
S20261018-32.t: The unwinding of Kurdish self-rule in Syria bears directly on Turkey's goals on the SDF and the PKK process.

S20261018-33.h: Turkish officials say transition to 'Terror-free Türkiye' cannot be stopped
S20261018-33.s: Interior Minister Çiftçi said the process will succeed, and Anadolu commentary says completing the transition will start Türkiye's rise and an era of major reforms.
S20261018-33.t: The government keeps framing the PKK disarmament process as irreversible, tying it to domestic reforms.

S20261018-34.h: İmamoğlu ends final defence in İBB trial, challenging Erdoğan
S20261018-34.s: On the last day of his defence in the İBB case, İmamoğlu challenged Erdoğan and sent messages on the opposition and the judicial process.
S20261018-34.t: The trial of Erdoğan's main rival continues to shape domestic politics and Türkiye's external image.

S20261018-35.h: Turkish fund scandal widens as regulator seeks prosecution of 37 and Özel attacks Erdoğan
S20261018-35.s: Turkey's securities regulator sought prosecution of 37 people, among them a former ruling party lawmaker, over a fund scandal. Özel accuses Erdoğan of dodging responsibility and cites a claimed $110bn loss, and analysts discuss the effect on the AKP.
S20261018-35.t: The scandal erodes government credibility and could affect investor confidence.

S20261018-36.h: Turkish courts jail seven in Etimesgut probe and four in Halk TV takeover case
S20261018-36.s: A court jailed two deputy mayors and five others pending trial in a corruption probe at Ankara's Etimesgut municipality. Another court jailed four people in the investigation behind the state takeover of Halk TV.
S20261018-36.t: The cases continue the pressure on opposition municipalities and media.

S20261018-37.h: Erdoğan sends Osman Gazi floating gas platform to Black Sea's Sakarya field
S20261018-37.s: Erdoğan marked the departure of Türkiye's first floating production platform, Osman Gazi, calling it a new chapter in energy history. It will double gas output at the Sakarya field. Energy Minister Bayraktar also hinted at new oil news from Gabar.
S20261018-37.t: Doubling Sakarya output reduces Turkey's import dependence on Russia, Iran and Azerbaijan.

S20261018-38.h: Turkey-Azerbaijan friction over headscarf ban and 'secret meeting' claims
S20261018-38.s: Azerbaijan's school headscarf ban is opening a rift with Turkey, and a hijab dispute also feeds Iran-Azerbaijan tension. Turkey's Baku embassy denied that Fidan held a secret meeting during his visit, while Bahçeli stressed the two countries' unity on Azerbaijan's independence day.
S20261018-38.t: Strain with Baku, Ankara's closest ally in the Caucasus, could affect the Turkey-Azerbaijan axis.

S20261018-39.h: Turkish gang may have carried out Starlink arson in Poland for Russian intelligence
S20261018-39.s: A report says a gang from Turkey may have carried out an arson attack on a Starlink station in Poland on behalf of Russian intelligence.
S20261018-39.t: Turkish criminal networks used by Russian services could strain Turkey's standing with NATO partners.

S20261018-40.h: Cyprus leaders attend joint festival as Turkish Cypriot fuel strike ends
S20261018-40.s: Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Erhürman jointly attended the Pyla festival and sent a message of peace. K-Pet workers ended their strike after layoffs were reversed, and the European Council backed Cyprus's Amalthea Gaza aid corridor.
S20261018-40.t: Erhürman's joint appearance signals movement on the Cyprus file that bears on Turkey-EU ties.

S20261018-41.h: CENTCOM chief: US blocked $25bn of Iranian oil as militias send pay to IRGC
S20261018-41.s: Adm. Brad Cooper says the US has blocked at least $25bn in Iranian oil exports. Iran-aligned militias are reportedly sending money to the IRGC amid Iran's economic crisis. A Jerusalem Post analysis says oil above $100 could drive escalation before elections.

S20261018-42.h: Israeli politics: critics warn Netanyahu could escalate before elections
S20261018-42.s: A former Shin Bet chief warned Netanyahu could deliberately escalate tensions before elections, and Yair Golan questioned the current Shin Bet chief's ability to safeguard the vote. Ben-Gvir seeks $250M for the October 7 tribunal.

S20261018-43.h: Blast at PMF headquarters in Baghdad prompts Iraqi inquiry
S20261018-43.s: Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi ordered a special investigative committee after an explosion at a Popular Mobilization Forces headquarters in eastern Baghdad. Iraq's oil minister called US companies a pillar of the sector, and the KRG says it got 4.2% of Iraq's budget over 12 years.
S20261018-43.t: Instability in Iraq affects Turkey's oil pipeline, Development Road and operations against the PKK.

S20261018-44.h: Bank of England governor walks out of IMF session as Russian minister speaks
S20261018-44.s: Andrew Bailey and other finance leaders left an IMF session in Bangkok when Russia's finance minister addressed the group. The IMFC chair said the global economy was resilient.

S20261019-01.h: Egypt pledges support to Saudi Arabia against Houthis, first aircraft land
S20261019-01.s: Egypt's presidency and National Defense Council pledged all necessary support to defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks. Parliament opened an emergency session on a possible troop deployment and adjourned until Monday. At least two Egyptian C-130H aircraft landed at King Fahd Air Base, while the Houthis warned Cairo against military intervention.
S20261019-01.t: Egypt's first confirmed military move into the Yemen war widens the Gulf-Red Sea conflict and shifts the Arab security balance Ankara has to work within.

S20261019-02.h: Saudi coalition and Houthis trade strikes as attacks reach Riyadh
S20261019-02.s: The Saudi-led coalition and the Houthis traded strikes on Sunday. Four drones were intercepted over Riyadh, the Eastern Province and the south, and a 'hostile projectile' injured six people in a southwestern Saudi city. Riyadh's Kingdom Centre ordered remote working after repeated attacks, and two crew died in a Saudi AH-6i crash near Najran.
S20261019-02.t: Houthi pressure on Saudi cities and Red Sea routes raises regional energy and shipping risks that affect Türkiye.

S20261019-03.h: Tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz, IRGC says
S20261019-03.s: The IRGC Navy reported tankers striking mines south of the Strait of Hormuz, with an engine-room explosion and fire. Al Jazeera reports two tankers, each carrying about two million barrels of crude, caught fire after using what the IRGC called an unauthorised route.
S20261019-03.t: A disrupted Hormuz raises oil prices and import costs for Türkiye.

S20261019-04.h: Iran presses US to accept seven-day Hormuz reopening offer
S20261019-04.s: Iran says its offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days is still on the table and urges Washington to accept. Tehran says the strait would reopen on the sixth day if the US meets its conditions, with negotiations in parallel.
S20261019-04.t: A Hormuz deal would ease energy-price pressure on Türkiye, while failure raises the risk of renewed escalation.

S20261019-05.h: Trump says US may 'soon finish the job' on Iran, endorses Netanyahu
S20261019-05.s: Trump endorsed Netanyahu nine days before Israel's October 27 election and warned the US could 'soon finish the job' on Iran. Reports say he suggested the US could face Iran alone if Netanyahu loses and declined to say whether he would work with another prime minister.
S20261019-05.t: A US-Israeli campaign against Iran tied to Israel's election politics raises escalation risk on Türkiye's border.

S20261019-06.h: Netanyahu vows to topple Iran's regime, warns of missiles reaching US
S20261019-06.s: Netanyahu called the election existential and, per Anadolu, pledged to topple Iran's regime in his national security doctrine. He told Fox News that Iran may seek missiles able to reach the US, and said Israel must finish its tasks while Trump is in office.
S20261019-06.t: Open regime-change aims against Iran raise the prospect of regional war and refugee and border pressure on Türkiye.

S20261019-07.h: Iranian officials threaten retaliation, hint at nuclear policy shift
S20261019-07.s: Iranian officials raised the possibility of a shift in nuclear policy and threatened retaliation for any new US-Israeli attack. Araghchi said Israel would be turned into 'scorched earth' if energy sites are hit. Armed forces, IRGC and Basij figures said Iran's response would be unpredictable.
S20261019-07.t: A possible nuclear doctrine shift in Iran would transform Türkiye's southeastern security environment.

S20261019-08.h: Iran's parliament confirms missile veteran Akhlaghi Ketabchi as defence minister
S20261019-08.s: Parliament approved Mehrdad Akhlaghi Ketabchi, a sanctioned veteran of Iran's missile industry with IRGC ties, as defence minister. The post had been filled on an interim basis after his predecessor was killed. He said Iran's forces are ready against Israeli attacks.
S20261019-08.t: Missile-industry leadership at the defence ministry signals Tehran's emphasis on deterrence.

S20261019-09.h: Vance: US seeks final Iranian commitment never to rebuild nuclear programme
S20261019-09.s: Vice President Vance said Washington wants a final and decisive Iranian commitment never to rebuild its nuclear programme. He said fuel prices will fall when the conflict with Iran ends.
S20261019-09.t: The US demand sets the terms of any settlement that Türkiye would have to adjust to.

S20261019-10.h: Lavrov in Manama proposes Gulf security framework, backs GCC against wider war
S20261019-10.s: At the Russia-GCC Strategic Dialogue in Bahrain, Lavrov backed GCC efforts to prevent full-scale war and proposed an updated collective security concept for the Gulf. He met Saudi and Kuwaiti ministers and discussed Yemen. GCC states urged Moscow to press Iran and support their role in talks.
S20261019-10.t: A Russian role in Gulf security architecture affects the diplomatic space in which Türkiye operates.

S20261019-11.h: Lavrov to visit Tehran Monday with mediation message
S20261019-11.s: Lavrov will be received by President Pezeshkian on October 19 and hold talks with Araghchi, Iranian officials say. Iranian press describes the trip as having a mediation flavour. Lavrov criticised Trump's approach to Iranian leadership.
S20261019-11.t: Russian mediation between Iran, the Gulf and the US competes with possible Turkish diplomatic roles.

S20261019-12.h: GCC condemns Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, urges firm international stance
S20261019-12.s: Gulf ministers condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and backed its right to self-defence. They called for a return to pre-February 28 conditions in Hormuz and for dialogue on US-Iran tensions. Fighting has displaced more than 233,000 people across Yemen.
S20261019-12.t: A unified GCC line shapes the regional framework Türkiye engages with on Yemen and Iran.

S20261019-13.h: Saudi defence minister meets UAE leaders on Gulf coordination
S20261019-13.s: Prince Khalid bin Salman met UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed and Sheikh Mansour in Abu Dhabi to discuss regional developments and joint Gulf action. Anwar Gargash said UAE-Saudi security is shared.

S20261019-14.h: Yemeni forces advance on several fronts as Houthis besiege Taiz
S20261019-14.s: Saudi-led forces struck positions around Taiz to break the Houthi siege, and government forces retook an area south of the province. Houthis fired eight ballistic missiles at Marib. Fuel and gas shortages deepen the humanitarian crisis, and forces continue operations around Bab al-Mandeb.

S20261019-15.h: Iran may object to OIC Yemen resolution; Yemen rejects Iranian mediation
S20261019-15.s: Araghchi said Tehran may openly object to a proposed OIC resolution on Yemen and wants it balanced. Asharq Al-Awsat reports the Yemeni government rejected an Iranian mediation bid while Iran continues to arm the Houthis.

S20261019-16.h: OIC foreign ministers meet in Baghdad; Fidan holds talks with Egypt, Iran
S20261019-16.s: Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan met Egyptian counterpart Abdelatty and Iran's Araghchi on the sidelines of the 52nd OIC Council of Foreign Ministers in Baghdad. Araghchi told Iraq's PM that Washington disrupted diplomacy and caused maritime insecurity, and Iranian officials called border security a red line.
S20261019-16.t: Fidan used the OIC meeting to call on the Islamic world to unite and to meet key players in the Iran and Gulf crises.

S20261019-17.h: Iraq proposes '6+1' Baghdad meeting between Iran and Gulf states
S20261019-17.s: Iraq's foreign minister announced a '6+1' initiative to bring the six GCC states and Iran together in Baghdad. Baghdad is working to organise the meeting.
S20261019-17.t: A Baghdad channel between Tehran and the Gulf could complement or crowd out Turkish mediation.

S20261019-18.h: Araghchi phones Egyptian and Pakistani counterparts on de-escalation
S20261019-18.s: Araghchi held calls with Egyptian FM Abdelatty and Pakistani FM Dar on regional developments and de-escalation. Pakistan and Egypt separately condemned Houthi attacks and reaffirmed solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

S20261019-19.h: Iran's parliament speaker warns Gulf states over military-linked AI firms
S20261019-19.s: Ghalibaf warned regional governments against supporting AI and data firms he links to aggression on Iran and said a 'Persian Gulf Data Authority' is coming. He urged states and investors to stop backing such firms.

S20261019-20.h: Israeli forces shell and raid southern Syria; Damascus appeals to world
S20261019-20.s: Israeli artillery hit Quneitra's northern countryside and Israeli forces carried out temporary incursions in several areas of southern Syria. Syria's Foreign Ministry urged the international community to act.
S20261019-20.t: Continued Israeli military activity in Syria constrains Türkiye's own plans and influence there.

S20261019-21.h: Syria and World Bank agree to set up recovery fund
S20261019-21.s: Syria's finance minister said an agreement with the World Bank to establish a Syria recovery fund opens a new phase of cooperation with international institutions.
S20261019-21.t: A reconstruction fund opens room for Turkish contractors and supports stability on Türkiye's border.

S20261019-22.h: Hezbollah challenges Beirut as Israeli fire isolates villages beyond 'Yellow Line'
S20261019-22.s: Tensions mount in Lebanon as Hezbollah challenges the state's authority and Israeli fire isolates villages beyond the 'Yellow Line'. Israel-Hezbollah negotiations are under way, and residents dread a looming UN peacekeeper pullout.

S20261019-23.h: Ammunition blast at Popular Mobilization Forces base in Baghdad injures five
S20261019-23.s: An explosion hit an ammunition store at a PMF base in Baghdad, injuring five, and the prime minister ordered an investigation. The Jerusalem Post describes it as a mysterious explosion striking an Iran-backed group.
S20261019-23.t: Instability around Iran-aligned groups in Iraq bears on Turkish security interests there.

S20261019-24.h: Kurdish opposition group attacked in Iraq amid Iran tensions
S20261019-24.s: A Kurdish opposition group was attacked in Iraq amid heightened tensions with Iran, according to the Jerusalem Post.

S20261019-25.h: Settlers attack European diplomats and French mayor in West Bank; EU demands accountability
S20261019-25.s: Masked settlers attacked a European delegation, including French and Belgian consuls and a French mayor, near Taybeh during the olive harvest. A Washington Post photographer was also injured. The EU, France, Cyprus, the US ambassador and others condemned the attacks, with France saying Israel must 'stop these acts of terror'.
S20261019-25.t: Rising settler violence feeds Ankara's case against Israel and widens European criticism of it.

S20261019-26.h: Netanyahu doubts settler attack as US presses Israel to crack down
S20261019-26.s: Netanyahu cast doubt on the attack witnessed by a Guardian reporter, and a European diplomat rejected his doubts. Rubio said the US is 'very disturbed' and wants Israel to crack down, and US officials visited Taybeh. Israeli army radio said forces failed to respond for three hours.

S20261019-27.h: Israel to let UAE do infrastructure work in designated Gaza area
S20261019-27.s: Netanyahu said Israel will allow the UAE into a designated Gaza area for infrastructure work, an exception to its ban on reconstruction. UAE aid convoys continue to enter Gaza under Operation Gallant Knight 3.
S20261019-27.t: Emirati reconstruction access in Gaza sidelines Türkiye's own ambitions for a role there.

S20261019-28.h: Senior Hamas official says Gaza political chief wounded in Israeli strike
S20261019-28.s: A senior Hamas official revealed that the group's Gaza political chief was wounded in an Israeli strike.

S20261019-29.h: Gaza toll tops 74,475 as Israeli fire kills more Palestinians
S20261019-29.s: Seven Palestinians were killed in 24 hours and Gaza's death toll passed 74,475. Remains of 75 people were buried after recovery from rubble in Gaza City, and Israeli soldiers' testimonies describe civilians being targeted.

S20261019-30.h: Documents show Israeli governments urged Qatar to keep funding Gaza
S20261019-30.s: A TIME investigation says successive Israeli governments helped set up and preserve the Qatari funding channel to Gaza. Bereaved families are seeking a criminal probe of Netanyahu over his October 7 account of Qatari funding.

S20261019-31.h: Israeli election tightens: polls split, Ben-Gvir disputes Europe assurances
S20261019-31.s: Four polls put Eisenkot's Yashar party ahead of Likud, though neither bloc has a majority, while a Kan poll gives Netanyahu's bloc 51 seats against 52 for the opposition. Ben-Gvir claims Netanyahu promised Europe his exclusion from the next government, which Netanyahu denies. The vote is on October 27.
S20261019-31.t: The election outcome will determine Israel's posture toward Iran, Syria and Türkiye.

S20261019-32.h: Ukraine launches massive drone attack on St Petersburg oil and data facilities
S20261019-32.s: Ukraine used more than 1,000 drones against Russian oil depots, logistics facilities and data centres, with St Petersburg's oil facility, a bridge and data centres hit. At least one person was killed in the city, and Russia reports downing 1,256 Ukrainian drones in a day.
S20261019-32.t: Strikes on Russian oil and Black Sea region energy infrastructure affect regional energy markets and the war's trajectory.

S20261019-33.h: Kremlin: systematic strikes on Ukraine will continue in response
S20261019-33.s: Peskov said Russia's strikes aim to reduce Ukraine's strike potential and are systematic and yielding results. Moscow says its aircraft, drones and missiles hit transport infrastructure used by the Ukrainian army.

S20261019-34.h: Russian missile and drone barrage hits Kyiv, Odesa and western Ukraine
S20261019-34.s: Russian strikes hit 20 locations, killing 10 and injuring 73 nationwide, including ballistic missiles on Kyiv and a medical centre. Air defence downed 152 of 180 drones overnight. Odesa and Ternopil lost power and Poland scrambled aircraft.

S20261019-35.h: Zelensky: Russia hit energy sites 76 times since Trump announced truce
S20261019-35.s: Zelensky told Trump that Russia has attacked energy, oil and gas facilities 76 times in a week since the energy ceasefire announcement. Kyiv says Moscow has failed to honour any commitments.

S20261019-36.h: Trump waives Russia sanctions to keep talks alive, attacks Zelensky
S20261019-36.s: Trump blocked sanctions and tariffs on Russia days before they took effect to avoid driving Moscow from the bargaining table. He criticised Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries and Zelensky. Bessent said sanctions were waived, not lifted, and a report says Ukraine has run out of Patriot interceptors.
S20261019-36.t: A US pivot toward Moscow reshapes the war and Black Sea balance, and opens room for Turkish mediation.

S20261019-37.h: Zelensky warns US siding with Russia would be 'historic mistake'
S20261019-37.s: Zelensky told NBC that a formal US shift to Russia would be a historic mistake, while saying Trump is still an ally. He spoke with Witkoff and Kushner about next steps and said he would run in elections held before the war ends.

S20261019-38.h: US resumes intelligence sharing with Ukraine, Zelensky says
S20261019-38.s: Zelensky said the US resumed sharing intelligence, including on Russian missile launches, after a pause, and that it now works.

S20261019-39.h: Starlink restrictions dispute: Rubio says Ukraine has no Starshield access
S20261019-39.s: Rubio said Ukraine lacks access to military-grade Starshield and its future is under discussion, and that the US was not involved in limiting Starlink speeds. Zelensky said the signal came from the US government, and Bessent called that claim 'very reckless'.

S20261019-40.h: Türkiye to import Russian diesel under US-Russia deal
S20261019-40.s: Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar said Türkiye will import some Russian diesel made available to global markets under a US-Russia arrangement. Lavrov said the diesel deal concerns only Russia and the US.
S20261019-40.t: Türkiye gains fuel supply from the waiver, while staying aligned with a US-Russia arrangement.

S20261019-41.h: Russia and Ukraine contest Dobropillia and Zaporizhzhia advances
S20261019-41.s: Zelensky and Ukrainian commanders denied Russian claims of capturing Dobropillia and Malokaterynivka. Moscow claims it destroyed a Ukrainian unit of about 2,000 in Dobropolye, and Kyiv says it has retaken more territory than Russia captured this fall. Ukraine reports 173 clashes, fiercest near Pokrovsk.

S20261019-42.h: Drone enters Lithuanian airspace; NATO scrambles Italian jets
S20261019-42.s: A drone entered Lithuanian airspace and damaged a car, and two Italian Eurofighters were scrambled under NATO command. Ukraine says Russian electronic warfare likely caused it, while Lithuania investigates a suspected Ukrainian drone.
S20261019-42.t: Spillover incidents on NATO's eastern flank test alliance cohesion that Türkiye is part of.

S20261019-43.h: British, French, German and Polish troops to rehearse post-war Ukraine deployment
S20261019-43.s: Military personnel from Britain, France, Germany and Poland will hold exercises next month in Poland simulating a post-war deployment to Ukraine.

S20261019-44.h: EU-GCC summit planned for Riyadh on October 24 postponed
S20261019-44.s: The second EU-Gulf Cooperation Council summit, planned in Riyadh for October 24, has been postponed.

S20261019-45.h: Cyprus talks stall as Guterres calls steps 'discouraging'
S20261019-45.s: Christodoulides accused Turkish Cypriot leader Erhürman of setting preconditions for resuming talks. Erhürman said Guterres told him the cancellation of the Barcelona camp was 'discouraging' and that actions blocking confidence-building are discouraging.
S20261019-45.t: The UN chief's remarks back the Turkish Cypriot complaint of obstruction, but there is no sign of a resumption of talks.

S20261019-46.h: Turkish Parliament to monitor PKK disarmament; Speaker consults parties
S20261019-46.s: Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş will hold talks with parties this week to advance the process to end PKK terror and set up parliamentary monitoring of disarmament.
S20261019-46.t: Parliamentary oversight is the next institutional step in the process to end PKK violence.
