S20261019-47.h: PKK evacuates some Matin tunnels but remains in Gara and Khwakurk, source says
S20261019-47.s: A source in Amedi says the PKK evacuated several Mount Matin tunnels to Turkish forces but remains present in Matin, Gara and Khwakurk.
S20261019-47.t: The continued PKK presence in the Kurdistan Region tests the pace of disarmament.

S20261019-48.h: Erdoğan: Türkiye aims to double Black Sea gas output by 2027
S20261019-48.s: Erdoğan said Türkiye's Black Sea natural gas production is expected to double to 20 million cubic metres per day, touting the Osman Gazi platform.
S20261019-48.t: Higher domestic gas output reduces dependence on imports from Russia and Iran.

S20261019-49.h: Macron condemns nationwide rioting in France, 2,000 arrested
S20261019-49.s: Macron denounced 'unbridled violence' after days of unrest, blamed far-left groups, and stopped short of a state of emergency or curfew. Prefects may ban some demonstrations, and National Rally's Bardella called for his resignation.

S20261020-01.h: Houthi missile strike on Shabwa training camp kills at least 53 government troops
S20261020-01.s: Houthi ballistic missiles hit a government forces training camp in Yemen's Shabwa governorate during an exercise. Officials put the toll at 53 dead and about 200 wounded, the deadliest single attack since the civil war reignited. Early reports said 18 dead before the toll rose.
S20261020-01.t: The escalation in Yemen tests Ankara's balancing between Saudi ties and curbing Iranian influence.

S20261020-02.h: Houthis claim strikes on Aramco, Riyadh airport; Saudi Arabia postpones investment forum
S20261020-02.s: The Houthis say they fired ballistic and cruise missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Yanbu, Saudi airports and a naval base. Riyadh's airport has been closed for a prolonged period, Saudi civil defence issued alerts, and the US Embassy in the UAE urged heightened vigilance. Saudi Arabia postponed the Future Investment Initiative conference to 2027.
S20261020-02.t: Attacks on Saudi Arabia's core infrastructure raise pressure on Türkiye under the Mecca defence pact and threaten Red Sea and Gulf trade.

S20261020-03.h: Egypt moves toward parliamentary authorisation to back Saudi Arabia against Houthis
S20261020-03.s: Egypt's parliament is expected to vote this week on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia. Cairo says it is ready to give Riyadh the support it needs. Pakistan said it would give Saudi Arabia whatever support is needed, and the Pakistani and Egyptian foreign ministers condemned the Houthi attacks and sought a quadrilateral meeting.
S20261020-03.t: A Saudi-Egyptian-Pakistani alignment may draw Türkiye into a wider Mecca-pact security arrangement while it avoids offensive involvement.

S20261020-04.h: Saudi offensive and Taiz operation pressure Houthis as Iran's backing is probed
S20261020-04.s: Saudi-backed forces are stepping up operations against the Houthis, including an operation in Taiz, aimed at securing Bab el-Mandeb. Al Jazeera reports new claims of Iranian support for the Houthis, and Beijing says it is ready to help investigate reports of military components reaching them. Iranian media accuse Riyadh of miscalculation and Israel of exploiting the war.

S20261020-05.h: Trump endorses Netanyahu a week before Israeli election, as US-Israeli Iran strike talk grows
S20261020-05.s: Trump publicly backed Netanyahu ahead of the 27 October election and predicted a big win. Netanyahu hinted at further action against Iran, telling Trump there is a job left to finish. Analysts say renewed US-Israeli strikes are being weighed and that a new campaign could target missile and nuclear sites.
S20261020-05.t: A renewed US-Israeli war on Iran would hit Türkiye's border region, energy supply and trade, and Ankara fears being drawn in.

S20261020-06.h: Iran warns of stronger response to any new US or Israeli attack
S20261020-06.s: Araghchi said Netanyahu seeks more war before the election and that Iran has its own 'unfinished jobs'. The armed forces chief of staff and the IRGC warned of retaliation, including for any strike on energy infrastructure. The IRGC spokesman claimed Iran's missile and drone capabilities have grown by at least 50% since the war began.

S20261020-07.h: Lavrov visits Tehran, pledges to honour economic deals and offers mediation
S20261020-07.s: Sergey Lavrov held talks with Araghchi and met Pezeshkian on his first visit since the US-Israeli war on Iran began. The two sides rejected military solutions on Hormuz and agreed Russian experts are returning to Bushehr. Lavrov said Russia will keep its economic agreements with Iran despite the 'challenging situation' and would respect an Iranian decision to join the Mecca Pact. Araghchi blamed US behaviour for regional instability.
S20261020-07.t: Closer Russia-Iran coordination and Moscow's mediation bid affect Türkiye's own mediation role and its position on the Hormuz and Caspian issues.

S20261020-08.h: GCC presses Moscow to halt Iranian attacks; Lavrov floats Gulf security framework
S20261020-08.s: Gulf states pressed Russia to help stop Iranian attacks and reopen the Strait of Hormuz ahead of Lavrov's Tehran trip. Lavrov proposed a Gulf security framework and said it is important to return to the pre-crisis situation in the Gulf.

S20261020-09.h: Trump says Russia has done nothing for Iran, welcomes limits on Moscow's support
S20261020-09.s: Trump said Russia has done very little to help Tehran and praised Moscow's role. Lavrov nonetheless backed Iran during his visit and promised continued political and economic cooperation.

S20261020-10.h: Iran keeps seven-day Hormuz reopening proposal on table, blames US
S20261020-10.s: Araghchi said Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days remains available. He blamed the US for the tensions and called for diplomacy. Iran's first vice president said Tehran has no choice but to place the strait under its forces' control, and Qatar rejected transit fees.
S20261020-10.t: Hormuz disruption keeps Türkiye's energy import costs and inflation exposed.

S20261020-11.h: Tanker hits mine in Hormuz as attacks on shipping continue
S20261020-11.s: The IRGC Navy said an oil tanker with its identification systems switched off struck a mine south of the strait and caught fire, and warned of a firm response to similar vessels. At least 15 vessels have been struck in the waterway over ten days. The IMO says about 6,000 seafarers are stranded near Hormuz.

S20261020-12.h: Russia fires 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and hits energy sites in 11 regions
S20261020-12.s: Overnight Russian strikes hit Kyiv and Kyiv region, killing several people and damaging a metro station, a mall and a hospital diagnostic centre. Zelensky said 28 energy facilities across 11 regions were hit, leaving about 550,000 households without power. Poland scrambled aircraft.

S20261020-13.h: Zelensky says US gave no warning of Russian missile strike; Rubio denies halting intelligence
S20261020-13.s: Zelensky said Ukraine received no advance warning of the ballistic strike on Kyiv and accused Washington of 'denial of reality'. Rubio rejected claims that intelligence sharing with Kyiv had stopped, and Washington responded to the claim.

S20261020-14.h: Zelensky: US withholding paid-for Patriot interceptors to push Ukraine toward capitulation
S20261020-14.s: Zelensky says the Pentagon is delaying Patriot missiles Ukraine already paid for, including under a NATO initiative. Hegseth has yet to approve the transfer of a significant batch. Zelensky met Lockheed Martin about Patriots and F-16 repairs and hopes to buy ballistic missile interceptors.

S20261020-15.h: Trump says someone other than Zelensky should negotiate; defends Russia sanctions relief
S20261020-15.s: Trump accused Zelensky of never wanting to end the war and said Russia has been 'fine' on Ukraine. He suggested a different Ukrainian negotiator. Rubio said neither side can win outright, a US delegation is to travel to Norway for talks, and Zelensky said he is ready to meet US negotiators.
S20261020-15.t: A US-Ukraine rift and shifting US policy complicate Türkiye's mediation and its Black Sea security interests.

S20261020-16.h: Putin floats Trump-Xi summit on Ukraine; Trump open but wants nuclear talks
S20261020-16.s: The WSJ reports Putin proposed a trilateral meeting with Trump and Xi, possibly at the APEC summit in Shenzhen, without Zelensky. Trump said he is open to it but would focus on denuclearisation. The Kremlin says no concrete proposals were made, and Kyiv says it would only embolden Putin.

S20261020-17.h: White House proposed EU buy more Russian gas; Commission rejects it
S20261020-17.s: The NYT reports Witkoff and Kushner proposed that EU officials buy more Russian gas and have Ukraine resume transit. The European Commission said it has no plans to resume Russian gas imports and still believes in coordinated sanctions. The EU also signalled further visa restrictions on Russians.
S20261020-17.t: Any rerouting of Russian gas toward Europe bears on Türkiye's hub ambitions.

S20261020-18.h: Ukraine launches over 1,000 drones at Russia and hits Bryansk radar
S20261020-18.s: Ukraine's strike on Russian oil facilities involved more than 1,000 drones, one of its largest air strikes. Its General Staff says it also hit a radar station in Bryansk region and ammunition depots in Donetsk region. Netanyahu cited a drop in anti-Israel online activity after Ukrainian strikes on Yandex data centres.

S20261020-19.h: Russian drone kills six including children in Nova Vodolaha park
S20261020-19.s: A Russian drone struck a park near a café in Nova Vodolaha, Kharkiv region, killing six people, including three children, and injuring more than a dozen. Zelensky called it 'pure atrocity' and urged partners not to lift sanctions and to apply the Graham Act. Sybiha called for tougher sanctions on Russia's drone industry.

S20261020-20.h: Ukraine and Russia finalise civilian evacuation from occupied Oleshky; Pope involved
S20261020-20.s: Ukraine and Russia are finalising details of an evacuation of civilians from Oleshky and six nearby settlements. Pope Leo XIV discussed the humanitarian situation with Zelensky days after speaking to Putin. Ukraine also brought back more children from occupied territory.

S20261020-21.h: Ukraine discusses Black Sea shipping protection with Türkiye, Egypt and India
S20261020-21.s: Ukraine is discussing a plan with Türkiye, Egypt and India to protect food shipments through the Black Sea. Kyiv will compensate damaged cargo ships, and Russia rejected its Black Sea proposal.
S20261020-21.t: Türkiye could gain a central role as guarantor of Black Sea trade, but it risks friction with Moscow.

S20261020-22.h: Erdoğan accuses Israel of seeking to destabilise Syria and says Türkiye avoided turmoil
S20261020-22.s: Erdoğan accused Israel of trying to destabilise Syria. He said Türkiye's cautious approach has kept it out of regional conflicts and credited his government for sparing it from turmoil.
S20261020-22.t: Ankara is signalling it sees Israeli activity in Syria as a direct threat while avoiding military involvement.

S20261020-23.h: Damascus fears Israeli-backed Druze offensive in Sweida, condemns IDF incursions
S20261020-23.s: A Syrian official told the Jerusalem Post Damascus fears an imminent Druze offensive in Sweida, claiming Israel is encouraging armed groups. Syria also condemned IDF incursions in Quneitra and Daraa and demanded a pullout from the Golan. A Syrian soldier was killed in an attack in Deir ez-Zor countryside.
S20261020-23.t: Escalation in southern Syria would test Türkiye's backing for Damascus.

S20261020-24.h: Fidan and Saudi counterpart discuss attacks on Saudi Arabia amid Mecca pact test
S20261020-24.s: Hakan Fidan spoke with Faisal bin Farhan about regional security and the attacks on Saudi sovereignty and territory. Analysts say Ankara is balancing Mecca pact obligations against avoiding offensive military action.
S20261020-24.t: Türkiye is trying to show solidarity with Riyadh without being drawn into the Yemen war.

S20261020-25.h: Pakistan's army chief Munir to visit Tehran to revive US-Iran mediation
S20261020-25.s: Field Marshal Asim Munir is due in Tehran on Tuesday as Islamabad seeks to revive stalled negotiations between Washington and Tehran. Pezeshkian told Lavrov Iran welcomes any regional initiative.
S20261020-25.t: Pakistan's mediation overlaps with Ankara's own ambitions as an intermediary.

S20261020-26.h: Gantz quits Israeli election race as polls show no seats
S20261020-26.s: Benny Gantz withdrew eight days before the vote after polls put Blue and White below the threshold. Arab turnout is seen as pivotal, and Israel's opposition is described as even more hawkish on Iran than Netanyahu.

S20261020-27.h: IDF suspends leave and reinforces West Bank ahead of Israeli election
S20261020-27.s: The IDF chief suspended soldiers' leave and is adding troops across units, including in the West Bank. Soldiers' voting starts Tuesday, and officials warn enemies may try to attack on Election Day.

S20261020-28.h: Israel arrests 10 over settler attacks on US journalist and European diplomats
S20261020-28.s: Israeli police detained 10 suspects after settler assaults on a US photojournalist and European diplomats in the West Bank. The UAE condemned the attack. Israel is deploying a new Border Police company, while the UN warns of escalating attacks on olive farmers.

S20261020-29.h: Israel resumes commercial shipments to Gaza as WFP cuts aid to 500,000
S20261020-29.s: Israel said it would resume commercial goods shipments into Gaza after a dispute over Hamas fees. The UN World Food Programme will end monthly aid to 500,000 people because of funding shortfalls. The IDF says it killed three Hamas men in new strikes, and a Palestinian was killed elsewhere in Gaza.

S20261020-30.h: Lebanese president says Israel violates framework deal; Hezbollah funding row grows
S20261020-30.s: Aoun said Israel has failed to comply with the US-mediated framework agreement and that Lebanon stays committed to diplomacy. The Israeli army kept shelling the south. Lebanon found a new tunnel near Beirut, and reported Iranian aid of about $200m to Hezbollah is pressuring Beirut. Qatar plans power plants and an LNG deal for Lebanon.

S20261020-31.h: Macron begins Gulf tour to secure fuel after violent protests in France
S20261020-31.s: Macron arrived in Kuwait and the UAE at the start of a Gulf tour that also covers Bahrain and Qatar, seeking oil and diesel supplies. He refused his interior minister's resignation after protests. Iran warned its citizens against travel to France, Belgium and Italy, and the Kremlin dismissed claims it was involved in the unrest.

S20261020-32.h: Iran summons German ambassador and EU presidency envoy over allegations
S20261020-32.s: Tehran summoned the German ambassador over what it called repeated baseless accusations, and the rotating EU president's envoy over a European statement.

S20261020-33.h: Christodoulides and Erhürman to meet Tuesday under UN auspices
S20261020-33.s: The Greek Cypriot president and the Turkish Cypriot leader will meet on Tuesday on dates proposed by the UN. Erhürman vowed continued diplomacy to end isolation. Cyprus also launched a reporting system for illegal use of Turkish Cypriot properties, and police are probing an alleged attack on a Turkish Cypriot in Limassol.
S20261020-33.t: The meeting bears on Ankara's two-state stance and its EU and Greece relations.

S20261020-34.h: Turkey's capital markets chief resigns amid investment fund scandal
S20261020-34.s: The head of the capital markets regulator resigned citing health reasons. Prosecutors and the regulator are examining trading in 31 companies' shares for suspected manipulation. An opposition lawmaker alleged a $600,000 bribe for a stock market listing.
S20261020-34.t: The scandal weakens market confidence at a time of financial fragility.

S20261020-35.h: Turkey detains opposition Çukurova mayor and 43 others in corruption probe
S20261020-35.s: Gendarmes detained the mayor of Çukurova in Adana and 43 others. Separate raids targeted the Süleymanlılar religious community, with 22 detained, and prosecutors seek up to 50 years for 22 former judges and prosecutors. The İmamoğlu defence in Silivri and divisions among opposition parties over the Halk TV case remain under discussion.
S20261020-35.t: The continued crackdown on opposition municipalities shapes domestic stability and Türkiye's standing with European partners.

S20261020-36.h: Fidan, Çiftçi and Gürlek hold Türkiye-Belgium ministerial in Brussels
S20261020-36.s: The foreign, interior and justice ministers met Belgian counterparts for the 4th Türkiye-Belgium meeting on counterterrorism, judicial and police cooperation, defence industry, visas and migration. Fidan met Maxime Prévot. Türkiye's chief of staff also held talks with his French counterpart.
S20261020-36.t: The talks bear on Gülenist and PKK-linked extradition requests and on visa and migration issues.

S20261020-37.h: Twelve migrants die in Aegean crossings off Lesbos and Samos
S20261020-37.s: Twelve migrants drowned in two incidents, including six who died when a speedboat from Türkiye collided with a Greek coast guard patrol boat off Lesbos. An infant was among the dead. Turkish police also detained 36 over an alleged egg-cell trafficking network linked to Cyprus.

S20261020-38.h: Istanbul and Kocaeli floods kill at least eight
S20261020-38.s: The death toll from flooding in Istanbul and Kocaeli rose to eight as rescuers recovered more bodies.

S20261020-39.h: Erdoğan says Türkiye closed or took over Gülen-linked schools in over 50 countries
S20261020-39.s: Erdoğan said Türkiye has secured the closure or takeover of Gülen-linked schools abroad and vowed to continue. A Turkey-Azerbaijan dispute over school headscarf rules and Baku's Israel ties has exposed differences.

S20261020-40.h: Turkish defence industry set to reach $20bn in new contracts in 2026
S20261020-40.s: Al-Monitor reports Türkiye's defence sector is on course for about $20bn in new contracts, and the industry is also serving as a foreign-policy tool deepening military partnerships.
S20261020-40.t: Defence exports are becoming a lever in Ankara's relations with Gulf and other partners.

S20261020-41.h: Syrian Kurdish YBŞ in talks with Baghdad on joining Iraqi security forces
S20261020-41.s: A YBŞ spokesperson said negotiations with senior Iraqi security and military officials began in February on integration into Iraqi security institutions. Separately, Syrian Kurds are protesting Arabic-language instruction in northeastern schools, and Türkiye's interior minister reaffirmed the 'Terror-free Türkiye' goal.
S20261020-41.t: Kurdish integration moves in Iraq and Syria shape Ankara's process to end PKK violence.

S20261020-42.h: Qatar warns Iran war's energy shock has yet to peak, plans defence partnership
S20261020-42.s: Qatar's deputy PM said global energy shockwaves from the Iran war have not peaked, urged dialogue with Tehran and stressed US defence ties. Doha is preparing a new regional defence partnership.

S20261020-43.h: EU weighs €30bn for Ukraine by late 2026 and a €70bn 2027 gap
S20261020-43.s: The Commission said Ukraine could receive about €30bn by the end of 2026 if reforms proceed. It is also exploring how to cover a €70bn financing gap in 2027, and EU diplomats are to review progress on opening negotiating clusters.

S20261020-44.h: Iran's parliament confirms 'Missile Man' Akhlaqi as defence minister
S20261020-44.s: Iran's parliament voted overwhelmingly to approve Mehrdad Akhlaqi as defence minister.

S20261021-01.h: Hegseth makes unannounced visit to Netanyahu, discusses Iran eight days before Israeli election
S20261021-01.s: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met Netanyahu in Israel on Monday, discussing Iran, according to Axios and Reuters reports. The meeting reportedly took place in southern Israel with Defense Minister Katz present, and the Israeli army chief was excluded. It comes as renewed US-Israeli strikes on Iran are under discussion.
S20261021-01.t: Renewed US-Israeli strikes on Iran would hit Türkiye's border region, energy supply and trade routes.

S20261021-02.h: Netanyahu calls toppling Iran's regime 'primary objective' after US talks
S20261021-02.s: Netanyahu said he discussed 'eliminating' Iran's regime with Trump and called regime change Israel's primary objective. The Jerusalem Post's sources say Trump is 'very close' to renewing strikes, while analysts note Netanyahu may offer to wait until after the 3 November US midterms. Haaretz reports Trump has tied US action on Iran to Netanyahu's re-election, and Netanyahu claims Tehran is trying to interfere in Israel's election.
S20261021-02.t: An explicit Israeli regime-change goal raises the risk of regional destabilisation and refugee and energy shocks on Türkiye's eastern border.

S20261021-03.h: IRGC says tankers hit mines in Hormuz, claims another US MQ-9 shot down
S20261021-03.s: The IRGC Navy says two 'non-compliant' tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the southern Strait of Hormuz, while CENTCOM rejected Iran's account. The IRGC also claims it downed a US MQ-9 drone and warns that undersea internet cables could become targets. Qatar has urged Iran not to target the cables.
S20261021-03.t: Disruption in Hormuz and threats to subsea cables raise Türkiye's energy import costs and risk to Gulf connectivity.

S20261021-04.h: Pakistan's army chief Munir in Tehran as Iran restates conditions for talks with US
S20261021-04.s: Field Marshal Asim Munir met Araghchi, Pezeshkian and Ghalibaf in Tehran as mediator in the US-Iran conflict. Iran told him there would be no talks with Washington until its seven conditions are met, and that the Hormuz reopening depends on past US commitments. Reuters sources say Iran is deliberately prolonging talks to weaken Trump before the midterms.
S20261021-04.t: Pakistan, a partner of Türkiye in the new defence pact, is positioning itself as the main mediator in a crisis affecting Türkiye's neighbourhood.

S20261021-05.h: Iran warns it will answer any US attack and rules out surrendering enriched material
S20261021-05.s: Iranian officials, including the foreign ministry, the UN envoy and Pezeshkian, warned of proportionate retaliation for any renewed US or Israeli aggression. Iran's security chief said no enriched nuclear material will leave the country. Iran's ambassador in Moscow called Trump's new threat unable to break Iranian resolve.
S20261021-05.t: Tehran's hard line on enriched material and retaliation lowers the odds of a negotiated settlement that Ankara favours.

S20261021-06.h: Lavrov in Tehran pledges support as Russia weighs gains from US-Iran crisis
S20261021-06.s: Sergey Lavrov made his first Tehran visit since the war began, meeting Araghchi and Pezeshkian. Araghchi said Iran-Russia ties have never been closer. Analysts note Russia profits from the conflict and seeks to benefit from any US sanctions relief, while Zelensky suggested Russia may have shared intelligence with Iran.
S20261021-06.t: Closer Russia-Iran alignment, and Moscow's gains from higher energy prices, complicate Türkiye's balancing in the Black Sea and Caucasus.

S20261021-07.h: Houthi missiles reach Riyadh as attacks hit Saudi economy; investment forum cancelled
S20261021-07.s: Explosions were heard in the Saudi capital after a civil defence alert, and the coalition intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh. Saudi Arabia cancelled its 2026 investment conference and ordered government staff to work from home. The coalition also targeted a Houthi weapons-smuggling operation off Yemen's coast.
S20261021-07.t: Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia raise pressure on Ankara to act under the pact it has just sent to parliament.

S20261021-08.h: Barrack questions US intervention against Houthis as Saudi allies set limits on support
S20261021-08.s: US envoy Tom Barrack said Washington is giving logistical support but questioned intervention against the Houthis, urging regional alliances. Haaretz reports Egypt and the UAE back Riyadh but draw strict lines on military backing. Qatar, the UAE and Türkiye have condemned the Houthi attacks.
S20261021-08.t: Turkish foreign minister Fidan has joined the UAE in condemning the attacks, and Ankara is weighing how far to back Riyadh.

S20261021-09.h: UK to deploy RAF Typhoons for defensive missions over Saudi Arabia
S20261021-09.s: Britain announced RAF Typhoon fighters will fly defensive missions to protect Saudi cities and critical national infrastructure from Houthi missiles and drones. It is an extension of UK support for Riyadh.
S20261021-09.t: Western air cover for Riyadh frames what Türkiye's own limited contribution could look like.

S20261021-10.h: Houthi missile strike on Shabwa training camp kills 73
S20261021-10.s: The death toll from the Houthi attack on a government security forces training camp in Shabwa province has risen to 73, with 14 missing. The governor earlier reported 58 dead and more than 200 injured.

S20261021-11.h: Houthis tighten siege on Taiz as Yemen displacement tops 250,000
S20261021-11.s: The UN says more than 250,000 people have fled renewed fighting and demands aid access to besieged Taiz. The Yemeni army claims 129 Houthis were killed in Taiz, and Houthis fired missiles at Marib and attacked in Lahj. Analysts discuss how Saudi Arabia is now paying the price of the UAE's exit from Yemen.

S20261021-12.h: Turkey submits Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan to parliament
S20261021-12.s: A bill ratifying the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement was sent to the Turkish parliament. Reports say it binds the three countries to mutual defence for at least 10 years. AK Party and Ankara stress it is not an alternative to NATO, and Turkish help to Riyadh against the Houthis is expected to be limited.
S20261021-12.t: This is Türkiye's biggest new security commitment in years and could drag it into the Yemen war while straining NATO and Israel relations.

S20261021-13.h: Türkiye, Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia to sign defence industry cooperation MoU
S20261021-13.s: The four countries are to sign a memorandum in Doha on joint production, technology transfer and supply chains. Turkish Defence Minister Güler will travel to Qatar for it, and the cooperation is to be institutionalised in a multilateral structure.
S20261021-13.t: It widens the market for Turkish defence exports and builds a bloc of Muslim-majority partners.

S20261021-14.h: Eastern Libya parliament approves Turkey maritime deal; Ankara moves to consolidate
S20261021-14.s: The Benghazi-based House of Representatives approved the 2019 Türkiye-Libya maritime jurisdiction memorandum, reversing years of opposition. Fidan phoned Dbeibah and Saddam Haftar, and intelligence chief Kalın held talks in Tripoli on unifying Libya's rival institutions. Greece rejects the move.
S20261021-14.t: It strengthens Türkiye's legal case in the Eastern Mediterranean against Greece and Cyprus and gives Ankara leverage with both Libyan camps.

S20261021-15.h: Costa and von der Leyen offer 'solidarity' to Greece and Cyprus over Turkey-Libya deal
S20261021-15.s: The European Council and Commission presidents backed Athens and Nicosia after the Libyan vote. Cyprus's foreign ministry had already declared the maritime agreement illegal.
S20261021-15.t: Expect an EU-Türkiye dispute over Eastern Mediterranean maritime rights to sharpen.

S20261021-16.h: Güler: Turkish troops stay in Syria and Iraq until borders are secured
S20261021-16.s: Defence Minister Yaşar Güler told AFP Türkiye will keep its forces in Syria and Iraq until border security is fully ensured, and that they may stay longer.
S20261021-16.t: It signals the PKK peace process will not lead to a quick withdrawal from northern Iraq or Syria.

S20261021-17.h: Israeli tanks advance into Quneitra countryside as Barrack urges halt to operations
S20261021-17.s: Israeli forces advanced with tanks into northern Quneitra and raided a home in Taranja village. Damascus condemned escalating incursions, and US envoy Tom Barrack called on Israel to halt its military operations in Syria.
S20261021-17.t: Israeli pressure on southern Syria undermines the Damascus government that Ankara backs.

S20261021-18.h: Erdoğan warns of 'ring of fire' around Türkiye, accuses Israel of destabilising Syria
S20261021-18.s: Erdoğan said Israel is undermining stability in Syria and that Türkiye is surrounded by a 'ring of fire'. Daily Sabah says Netanyahu is using enmity toward Türkiye in his election campaign.
S20261021-18.t: Turkish-Israeli rhetoric is escalating into campaign themes on both sides.

S20261021-19.h: DEM and PKK press Ankara for concrete steps in stalled peace process
S20261021-19.s: DEM co-chair Tuncer Bakırhan said peace cannot be kept 'in a waiting room' and urged an end to trustee appointments, prisoner releases and a peace body. PKK official Duran Kalkan said the process is largely rhetorical and asked for action on Öcalan's status. A commentary asks whether Israel opposes the process.
S20261021-19.t: The process lacks legal steps, which risks stalling it just as Ankara keeps troops in Syria and Iraq.

S20261021-20.h: Iran says Iraq agreed to expel Kurdish opposition groups; IRGC officer killed
S20261021-20.s: Iran's ambassador to Iraq said Tehran and Baghdad agreed to expel or hand over Iranian Kurdish separatist groups from the Kurdistan region. An IRGC officer was killed in the border mountains as fighting with Kurdish opposition intensifies.
S20261021-20.t: Pressure on Kurdish groups in northern Iraq feeds into Türkiye's own regional Kurdish policy.

S20261021-21.h: Fund crisis dominates Turkish politics as Bahçeli and opposition clash
S20261021-21.s: Opposition leader Özel attacked Erdoğan over the investment fund crisis, while the justice minister says all who profited from market abuses are identified. Bahçeli called the probes an opportunity for 'purification' and criticised municipal interest ties. Commentators also discuss the trustee appointed to Halk TV.
S20261021-21.t: The crisis is a domestic stress test for the governing alliance.

S20261021-22.h: S&P warns energy shock could add 7 points to Turkish inflation
S20261021-22.s: S&P says higher energy prices from the Middle East conflict could raise Turkey's inflation by up to 7 percentage points this year. A think tank urges the central bank to hold its rate at 37 percent amid the fund crisis.
S20261021-22.t: A Gulf war energy shock hits the Turkish economy directly while confidence is already shaken.

S20261021-23.h: Cemalettin Kani Torun joins AK Party, raising its seat count
S20261021-23.s: The former ambassador to Somalia left the New Path Party and joined AK Party, shifting the seat distribution in parliament. Reports had said he would join DEM.
S20261021-23.t: Small shift in parliamentary arithmetic as ratification votes on defence pacts approach.

S20261021-24.h: Court orders opposition leader Özel to pay justice minister 750,000 lira
S20261021-24.s: A Turkish court ordered CHP leader Özgür Özel to pay Justice Minister Akın Gürlek 750,000 lira over allegations of unexplained wealth.
S20261021-24.t: Another sign of legal pressure on the main opposition.

S20261021-25.h: Azerbaijan issues arrest warrants for seven Turks including pro-Erdoğan pundit
S20261021-25.s: Baku issued warrants for seven Turkish citizens living in Türkiye, including commentator Fatih Tezcan. An opinion piece links the friction to Erdoğan's remarks on headscarf bans.
S20261021-25.t: Unusual public friction with Türkiye's closest Caucasus ally.

S20261021-26.h: Fidan in Brussels: meets Rutte, Belgian counterparts; presses Belgium on terror groups
S20261021-26.s: Foreign Minister Fidan met NATO chief Rutte and addressed the European Policy Centre. Turkish ministers asked Belgium for stronger judicial cooperation and extraditions against FETÖ and PKK-linked groups. Belgium called Türkiye indispensable to European security.
S20261021-26.t: A chance to press Türkiye's case on defence, security and extraditions in the EU.

S20261021-27.h: Canadian PM Carney visits Ankara to sign defence and energy declaration
S20261021-27.s: Carney arrives Wednesday for a three-day visit, the first bilateral trip, and is set to sign a joint declaration deepening defence and energy ties. The two aim for a $10 billion trade target and launching free trade talks.
S20261021-27.t: Opens a defence-industrial and energy partnership with a NATO ally.

S20261021-28.h: Cyprus leaders meet again next week as Bahçeli rejects federation
S20261021-28.s: Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Erhürman met in Nicosia and will meet again next week before a UN envoy's visit. MHP's Bahçeli called a federal settlement a fantasy.
S20261021-28.t: Ankara's governing ally rules out federation, limiting room for a UN-led deal.

S20261021-29.h: Israeli firms reportedly close to €150m naval deal with Cyprus
S20261021-29.s: Israel Shipyards and Rafael are reportedly nearing a €150 million deal to supply naval vessels to Cyprus. Cyprus is also courting Israeli investors, and commentators describe it as Israel's economic backyard.
S20261021-29.t: Cyprus-Israel military ties add to Ankara's Eastern Mediterranean concerns.

S20261021-30.h: NATO adds Black Sea assets as Russian attacks hit grain ships
S20261021-30.s: NATO is sending extra surveillance, reconnaissance and forensic support after attacks on vessels carrying grain. Kallas backs a naval mission and a moratorium on Black Sea strikes, though the EU is unlikely to send one. Russia says it hit four cargo ships at Odesa.
S20261021-30.t: Türkiye, the Montreux guardian, faces more risk and demands on its shipping and Black Sea security role.

S20261021-31.h: Witkoff holds Oslo talks with Zelensky, then flies to Moscow
S20261021-31.s: US envoy Witkoff met Zelensky, European allies, the EU and NATO in Oslo and travels to Moscow on 21 October with proposals including ceasefire and security guarantees. Lavrov says Moscow will listen but make no political concessions, and Zelensky says Ukraine is not losing the war.
S20261021-31.t: A new US-Russia track could reshape the Black Sea balance, and Türkiye has offered mediation venues in the past.

S20261021-32.h: Trump rebukes Zelensky, open to meeting Putin and Xi without Kyiv
S20261021-32.s: Trump said Zelensky does not want to end the war and that it's time for someone else to negotiate. He is willing to meet Putin and Xi on Ukraine, while Zelensky says Ukraine must be present. Republicans have pushed back on a sanctions pause.
S20261021-32.t: Washington's shift toward Moscow raises the risk of a settlement over Kyiv's head, with Black Sea consequences.

S20261021-33.h: Vance: Ukraine a partner 'in a sense', should stop striking Russian refineries and not join NATO
S20261021-33.s: Vice President JD Vance said the US has no formal alliance with Kyiv and that Ukraine should halt strikes on Russian oil refineries. He also said Ukraine should not join NATO.
S20261021-33.t: A US line against Ukrainian NATO membership shifts the alliance's eastern agenda.

S20261021-34.h: US resumes intelligence warnings to Ukraine amid Patriot delivery dispute
S20261021-34.s: Zelensky says Ukraine is receiving US early-warning intelligence again after a suspension, and accuses the US of delaying interceptors. Rubio said Patriot deliveries may not have arrived and the delay was not political.

S20261021-35.h: Kallas accuses US negotiators of pushing Ukraine toward surrender
S20261021-35.s: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said US negotiators have pushed Ukraine towards surrender for about 18 months, and that European support is the only reason Kyiv still resists.

S20261021-36.h: Europe prepares for direct talks with Putin, FT reports
S20261021-36.s: European leaders are rethinking their Kremlin approach, with one reported idea: Russia gets Donbas, Ukraine gets NATO membership.

S20261021-37.h: Russian drone and missile attacks kill civilians in Kyiv and Odesa regions
S20261021-37.s: Overnight Russia launched 165 drones, 115 shot down, and strikes hit Kyiv, a highway near Fastiv, a cardiology institute and an industrial site. At least 16 people were killed across Ukraine in the past day, including children in a park. Energy sites in Odesa and Ternopil were also damaged.

S20261021-38.h: Ukraine strikes Russian depots, Yandex data centres and Druzhba pipeline facility
S20261021-38.s: Ukraine's General Staff reports hits on command posts and warehouses, and Ukrainian drones reportedly hit Tambov infrastructure on the Druzhba pipeline. Moscow says it downed 136 drones. HUR claims 108 Russian soldiers killed in Sumy.

S20261021-39.h: EU Arctic strategy targets shadow fleet and dual-use capabilities; Kremlin pushes back
S20261021-39.s: The Commission unveiled a more militarised Arctic strategy, with Kallas seeking to challenge Russia and China over the Northern Sea Route. Peskov told the EU to settle its position on Arctic dialogue.

S20261021-40.h: Hungary blocks opening of two EU accession clusters for Ukraine
S20261021-40.s: Hungary refused to approve screening results for Clusters 4 and 5 in Ukraine's accession talks.

S20261021-41.h: Israel and Lebanon hold military talks in Florida under US mediation
S20261021-41.s: Israeli and Lebanese delegations met at CENTCOM's Tampa headquarters to discuss a framework agreement and pilot areas for Israeli withdrawal from south Lebanon. President Aoun confirmed Lebanon's participation.

S20261021-42.h: Israel keeps striking south Lebanon; Katz says 200,000 civilians displaced
S20261021-42.s: Israeli air strikes continued in south Lebanon despite the ceasefire and framework deal. Defence Minister Katz said about 200,000 civilians were expelled from the occupied 700 sq km area, and the IDF accused the Lebanese army of lying about Hezbollah weapons enforcement.

S20261021-43.h: Israeli fire kills at least four Palestinians in Gaza despite ceasefire
S20261021-43.s: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four people in Gaza City and Khan Younis, including a married couple and a 17-year-old.

S20261021-44.h: Israeli election campaign: Ben-Gvir surges, settler violence becomes Netanyahu liability
S20261021-44.s: Netanyahu promised Ben-Gvir a senior post as Likud was fined again for using IDF footage. Attacks on a US journalist and European diplomats in the West Bank are hurting Netanyahu, and Ben-Gvir posted a video mocking Gaza's destruction. Vance avoided endorsing Netanyahu.
S20261021-44.t: The result will shape Israel's posture toward Iran, Syria and Türkiye.

S20261022-01.h: US orders non-essential diplomats and families out of Saudi Arabia amid Houthi strikes
S20261022-01.s: The State Department ordered non-essential embassy staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia as Houthi attacks on the kingdom escalate. Reuters first reported that similar departures were being prepared for other Gulf missions. A State Department deputy spokesperson later said the order applies only to the Saudi mission.
S20261022-01.t: A US drawdown in Riyadh raises the risk profile of the Saudi theatre just as Ankara prepares to deploy personnel there under the Mecca defence pact.

S20261022-02.h: Türkiye submits Mecca defence pact to parliament, seeks mandate to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia
S20261022-02.s: A bill to ratify the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan has been sent to the Turkish parliament. A ruling-party official says Ankara will also seek a mandate to send military personnel to Saudi Arabia. The pact pledges mutual support for sovereignty and territorial integrity, and its full text has been published.
S20261022-02.t: Ratification and a deployment mandate would put Turkish forces in the Saudi-Houthi conflict zone and turn the pact into an operational commitment.

S20261022-03.h: Houthis hit Aden airport with ballistic missile as Saudi-led coalition reports strikes and intercepts
S20261022-03.s: The Houthis claimed a ballistic missile attack on a Saudi military camp near Aden airport, and a blast and smoke were reported. Yemeni state media reported airstrikes on Houthi positions east of Mokha, and the coalition said it intercepted drones aimed at Saudi Arabia, including near Medina. The Houthis denied launching drones at Medina. Yemen held a mass funeral for 75 recruits killed in an earlier Houthi missile strike on a training camp.
S20261022-03.t: The intensifying Saudi-Houthi war is the theatre where Turkish personnel may soon deploy.

S20261022-04.h: Macron makes surprise 'solidarity' visit to Riyadh, first Western leader since Houthi escalation
S20261022-04.s: French President Emmanuel Macron met Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Riyadh on a Gulf tour that earlier took in Kuwait, the UAE and Qatar. He secured extra diesel supplies, and in Qatar winter LNG supplies and defence talks. The visit signals Western backing for Riyadh.
S20261022-04.t: European security engagement in the Gulf competes with and complements Turkey's own defence tie-up with Riyadh.

S20261022-05.h: Sisi: Egypt would defend Saudi territory but will not attack Yemen
S20261022-05.s: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said Egypt's military support for Saudi Arabia is limited to defending Saudi territory and borders. He ruled out offensive action against Yemen. A commentary notes the Houthis invoked Egypt's 1960s Yemen war as a warning.
S20261022-05.t: Cairo's defensive-only line sets a benchmark for how far Ankara's Saudi deployment may be read as offensive.

S20261022-06.h: Israeli report: Syria and Saudi Arabia discuss Syrian deployment to Yemen
S20261022-06.s: Israel's i24NEWS reported that Damascus and Riyadh are in advanced talks on a Syrian role in the Yemen campaign. An analysis asks whether Syria should join, given how much its post-Assad economy depends on Saudi support.
S20261022-06.t: Syrian involvement alongside Saudi Arabia would shift Ankara's partner calculus in Damascus.

S20261022-07.h: Britain, France, Jordan and Kuwait line up behind Riyadh against Houthi attacks
S20261022-07.s: Jordan and Saudi Arabia upgraded their coordination council as Amman condemned the Houthi attacks. The Saudi and Kuwaiti foreign ministers also condemned the attacks. Analysts say UK and French support, including British jets, is billed as defensive but may draw them into the conflict.
S20261022-07.t: A widening coalition around Riyadh shapes the diplomatic context for Turkey's own Saudi commitments.

S20261022-08.h: Besieged Taiz faces water and food crisis as fighting displaces 260,000
S20261022-08.s: Aid workers warn Taiz is near an 'unmanageable' crisis, with water, gas and fresh food running out after Houthi advances cut supply routes. The UN says about 260,000 people have been displaced since early August, and fierce clashes continue around the city. A Yemeni official said Taiz will not be held hostage to the Houthis.

S20261022-09.h: Pakistan's army chief presses Tehran on Houthi attacks in latest Iran visit
S20261022-09.s: Field Marshal Asim Munir reportedly urged Iran to persuade the Houthis to halt attacks on Saudi Arabia. He also discussed differences over the US-Iran track, which Amwaj describes as a last-ditch bid to revive diplomacy. Reports say Tehran stonewalled him.
S20261022-09.t: Pakistan is Turkey's partner in the Mecca pact and in Bedir, and is also mediating with Iran.

S20261022-10.h: Iraq closes Shaib border crossing with Iran amid US pressure and Saudi pipeline attack
S20261022-10.s: Baghdad shut the southern crossing with Iran. Baghdad cites technical upgrades, while other reports link it to Iran-linked drone strikes on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and to US pressure on Iraq. Iraq denies hosting Houthi bases and says its territory will not be used to threaten neighbours. More closures were reported.
S20261022-10.t: Iraq's rebalancing away from Iran affects Turkey's border, trade and anti-PKK coordination with Baghdad.

S20261022-11.h: Libyan eastern parliament ratifies Turkey maritime deal; Ankara hails it as legitimate
S20261022-11.s: Libya's eastern House of Representatives approved the 2019 maritime jurisdiction memorandum with Türkiye. Erdoğan, Fidan, Speaker Kurtulmuş and MHP leader Bahçeli welcomed it, with Fidan calling it legally and politically legitimate and not open to debate. Turkish parties defended it, and Ankara's disinformation centre denied claims about it.
S20261022-11.t: The vote strengthens Ankara's Eastern Mediterranean claims and its ties with eastern Libya.

S20261022-12.h: EU, Greece, Egypt and Israel condemn Turkey-Libya maritime deal as invalid
S20261022-12.s: All 27 EU member states backed a statement calling the memorandum null and void, and Kallas told Fidan it infringes on third states' rights. Greece said it remains invalid, and Egypt rejected the ratification. Israel also condemned the vote, and analysts called it troubling for Israeli security.
S20261022-12.t: A united EU, Greek, Egyptian and Israeli front sets up friction over Eastern Mediterranean maritime claims.

S20261022-13.h: Fidan in Brussels meets Kallas; presses Belgium on Gülenists and PKK
S20261022-13.s: Fidan met EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas and Belgian business representatives during a visit for the 4th Turkey-Belgium foreign, justice and interior ministers meeting. Türkiye pressed Belgium to extradite people linked to the Gülen movement, close its institutions and act against the PKK.
S20261022-13.t: The visit is a chance to press security demands on the EU even as the Libya deal strains relations.

S20261022-14.h: Türkiye, Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia sign 'Bedir' defence industry cooperation MoU in Doha
S20261022-14.s: The four defence ministries signed a multilateral memorandum on weapons and defence-industry cooperation, exercises, training and joint projects. Defence Minister Yaşar Güler met his Qatari counterpart there. Türkiye is expected to take the largest share of joint projects.
S20261022-14.t: Bedir builds a Turkey-centred defence-industrial bloc across the Muslim world and expands export opportunities.

S20261022-15.h: Netanyahu says he ordered IDF and Mossad to overthrow Iran's regime
S20261022-15.s: Speaking at a military graduation ceremony, Netanyahu said he directed the IDF and Mossad to bring down Iran's regime, and told the Jerusalem Post that Iran is plotting to influence the election. The army declined to broadcast the speech over electioneering concerns. Analysts see regime change as a personal promise tied to the election.
S20261022-15.t: A new Israeli drive against Tehran would again threaten regional stability on Türkiye's eastern border.

S20261022-16.h: Israeli jets flew close to Iranian border, possibly hoping to provoke a response
S20261022-16.s: Axios and Channel 12 report dozens of Israeli aircraft flew as far as the Iranian border in a sortie on 19 October. Some sources called it routine deterrence, while US officials said Israel may have hoped Iran would fire first and provide justification.
S20261022-16.t: Risk of renewed Israel-Iran war directly affects Türkiye's security environment.

S20261022-17.h: Report: Trump blocked Netanyahu's early October Iran strike plan; Israel weighs action before election
S20261022-17.s: The FT reported Israel planned strikes on Iranian power plants, nuclear and regime targets that Trump opposed. The Jerusalem Post says the IDF was not planning to strike on 10 October. Haaretz and Reuters analysts say Netanyahu is keeping renewed war on the table, and officials warn Israel may act as Iran rebuilds.
S20261022-17.t: US-Israeli friction over Iran timing shapes the risk of a regional war near Türkiye.

S20261022-18.h: Iran says US accepted its seven-day Hormuz plan but added terms; Qatar reports progress
S20261022-18.s: Araghchi said Washington agreed to the conditions in Iran's seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz but sought additional terms. Qatar reported progress, while Tehran said it does not trust Washington. Pezeshkian says Iran will not bow to pressure but does not seek war, and Araghchi warned the US of a greater strategic defeat if it chooses war.
S20261022-18.t: Success or collapse of US-Iran talks decides whether war returns on Türkiye's border and whether energy routes reopen.

S20261022-19.h: Hormuz tensions: tankers hit mines, explosions heard, IRGC claims operational control
S20261022-19.s: Iran says two tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and state media reported explosions nearby. An IRGC commander said Iran's armed forces control the battlefield there, and Araghchi said Iran has unparalleled leverage over the waterway. Iran says it is preparing for resumed US-Israeli bombing.
S20261022-19.t: Disruption in Hormuz hits energy prices and trade that Türkiye depends on.

S20261022-20.h: Iran's parliament speaker meets unseen Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei
S20261022-20.s: Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf met Mojtaba Khamenei, who has not appeared in public since late February after the US-Israeli strikes. The rare meeting followed earlier reported talks between the president and the leader, amid tensions with the US and Israel.

S20261022-21.h: Putin offers Russian help to resolve Iran-US dispute
S20261022-21.s: Putin told Witkoff Russia is ready to help resolve the Iran-US dispute. A Russian diplomat said Moscow will mediate if both sides want it, noting its nuclear proposals have not received support. Trump says Russia and China could have done more on Iran.
S20261022-21.t: Russian mediation competes with Türkiye's own bid for a role in Iran diplomacy.

S20261022-22.h: US sanctions Greece- and Panama-based law firm over help to Iranian shipping
S20261022-22.s: The US Treasury sanctioned Karnakis & Karnakis for assisting Iranian shipping.

S20261022-23.h: Putin tells Witkoff Russia ready to resume trilateral talks in early November
S20261022-23.s: After meeting Putin in St Petersburg, Witkoff said US-Russia-Ukraine talks will continue at technical level. Kremlin aide Ushakov said Moscow is ready in principle, around 10 November, with Abu Dhabi mentioned as a venue. Kyiv backs a quick meeting, and the Kremlin says a full settlement is impossible without Kyiv and that EU and Ukrainian proposals are of little use.
S20261022-23.t: Türkiye, host of earlier Russia-Ukraine contacts, is watching a revived US-led track that could reshape the Black Sea order.

S20261022-24.h: Russia frees US citizen Stephen Hubbard; Witkoff calls Putin 'humanitarian'
S20261022-24.s: Putin ordered the release of Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old American convicted of mercenary activity for fighting for Ukraine, after a US request. Witkoff praised Putin as a 'humanitarian', and a Guardian analysis criticised his flattery.

S20261022-25.h: Zelensky says Ukraine ready to freeze front line, rejects surrendering Donbas
S20261022-25.s: Zelensky backed freezing the conflict along the current line as a first step to a ceasefire and diplomacy. He rejected ceding Donbas and wants a seat at talks and security guarantees from Washington and Europe.
S20261022-25.t: A ceasefire on current lines would shape Black Sea security and Türkiye's mediation role.

S20261022-26.h: Trump reportedly wants Ukraine deal by December G20, pressing Kyiv on refinery strikes
S20261022-26.s: The Atlantic reports Trump wants a Russia-Ukraine peace agreement signed at the December G20 summit and may increase pressure on Kyiv. Axios says Jared Kushner urged Ukraine in Oslo to stop striking Russian oil refineries. Trump says the sides are closer than ever.
S20261022-26.t: US pressure for a deal by year-end raises the stakes for Black Sea and NATO-flank planning.

S20261022-27.h: US-Russia diesel supply deal moves forward; first Russian tanker to leave for US
S20261022-27.s: Moscow says the first tanker with 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel departs for the US on Thursday and contracts are being finalised. The Kremlin says the deal will stabilise fuel markets, though analysts doubt Russia has the spare fuel.
S20261022-27.t: Russian diesel flows to the US shift energy-market and Black Sea trade dynamics.

S20261022-28.h: Russian missile and drone barrage hits Kyiv and energy sites in several regions
S20261022-28.s: Russia launched Iskander-K missiles and 186 drones overnight, and Ukraine downed or jammed 150. Kyiv and several oblasts suffered deaths and injuries and power outages, with energy sites hit in Kyiv, Volyn and Odesa regions. Three universities were also damaged. Heavy fighting continues on the Pokrovsk axis.

S20261022-29.h: Ukraine strikes Russian command posts, depots and energy sites; Black Sea ports crippled
S20261022-29.s: Ukraine's forces hit Russian command posts and logistics depots in Luhansk, Donetsk and Crimea, and energy infrastructure in occupied Donetsk. A Russian newspaper says Ukrainian drone attacks have paralysed Black Sea and Azov ports at a cost of about $2.5bn a month. NATO is adding patrol aircraft and drones in the Black Sea after attacks on commercial ships.
S20261022-29.t: Attacks on Black Sea ports and shipping, and NATO's added presence, bear on Türkiye's maritime security and the Straits.

S20261022-30.h: EU seeks partners to fill €70bn Ukraine funding gap for 2027
S20261022-30.s: Brussels is pressing the UK, Canada, Japan and others to help close the shortfall. Costa says up to €17bn in budget support could come this year subject to reforms, and a special European Council on 26-27 November will discuss funding. Belgium's premier says the Commission will not reopen the frozen Russian assets debate.

S20261022-31.h: Poland suspends major arms shipment to Ukraine over Lviv tribute to UPA
S20261022-31.s: Poland reportedly halted delivery of a large weapons package after Lviv authorities moved to honour the WWII Ukrainian Insurgent Army. Tusk called the move 'suicidal tactics'.

S20261022-32.h: Israel detains US candidate Brad Lander and dozens of volunteers in West Bank
S20261022-32.s: Israeli forces held about 80 US, Israeli and British volunteers near Nahalin during an olive harvest, among them Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander. Mamdani and Jewish organisations criticised the detentions.

S20261022-33.h: Settler violence, raids and demolitions continue across West Bank
S20261022-33.s: The Palestinian commission reported 23 attacks on olive farmers in 12 hours. Israeli forces demolished a building housing 35 people near Qalandia, and an Israeli minister called for settling the entire West Bank. Church leaders say lack of accountability fuels the attacks.

S20261022-34.h: IDF steps up Gaza operations as Israeli strikes kill Palestinians despite ceasefire
S20261022-34.s: The IDF says it killed Hamas operatives, including one linked to the Shani Louk abduction and one involved in a September 2025 tank attack. Israeli strikes killed several Palestinians, including students, and a Resistance Committees commander in Khan Younis, despite the ceasefire.

S20261022-35.h: Hezbollah rebuilding as Israel strikes south Lebanon despite ceasefire
S20261022-35.s: Israeli security officials say Hezbollah is rebuilding capabilities in Beirut and the IDF is preparing for possible renewed fighting. Israel struck areas of south Lebanon despite the ceasefire and framework agreement.

S20261022-36.h: Israeli election run-up: Netanyahu bloc slips in poll as right-wing rivalries and Trump endorsement shape race
S20261022-36.s: A poll puts Netanyahu's bloc at 51 seats against 55 for Eisenkot's. Smotrich offered a far-right rival a post to quit the race, and Netanyahu said the next defence minister should be from Likud. Vance declined to endorse Netanyahu, while Trump has endorsed him, and soldiers began voting.
S20261022-36.t: The election outcome will shape Israel's posture toward Iran, Syria and Türkiye.

S20261022-37.h: Öcalan moves into new İmralı residence as PKK process stalls
S20261022-37.s: Jailed PKK founder Abdullah Öcalan reportedly moved into a newly built residence on İmralı island. Analyst Ruşen Çakır says the peace process is paused, with Kandil watching İmralı and İmralı watching Ankara.
S20261022-37.t: The pause in the process to end PKK violence puts a central domestic-security project in doubt.

S20261022-38.h: Iraq says it is working with Türkiye to expel PKK from its territory
S20261022-38.s: An Iraqi government spokesman said Baghdad is coordinating closely with Ankara to remove the PKK from Iraqi territory.
S20261022-38.t: Baghdad's cooperation supports Türkiye's push to end the PKK presence in northern Iraq.

S20261022-39.h: Prosecutor seeks punishment for İmamoğlu in CHP congress case; fund probe detains 26
S20261022-39.s: In the CHP 38th congress case, the prosecutor sought a penalty for jailed Istanbul mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu and acquittal for Cemil Tugay, who joined the AKP. Police separately detained 26 people, including a former Finance Ministry official, in an investment-fund probe, and Erdoğan vowed accountability. An opposition mayor was sentenced to over seven years.
S20261022-39.t: Judicial pressure on the opposition shapes Turkey's domestic politics and its image with Western partners.

S20261022-40.h: Azerbaijan bars 31 Turkish nationals as headscarf dispute with Türkiye deepens
S20261022-40.s: Azerbaijan banned 31 Turkish citizens, including opposition figures, amid a row over school headscarf restrictions. Erdoğan and Aliyev held a phone call and Erdoğan invited Aliyev to the Organization of Turkic States summit in Ankara, as Ankara tries to contain the dispute.
S20261022-40.t: A rift with Baku ahead of the Turkic States summit tests Ankara's closest regional alliance.

S20261022-41.h: Erdoğan confirms upcoming Damascus visit; Barrack meets al-Sharaa
S20261022-41.s: Erdoğan said he will soon visit Damascus, his first trip since the fall of Assad. US envoy Thomas Barrack discussed Syria and regional stability with President al-Sharaa. Two Syrian soldiers were hurt in a landmine blast in Raqqa.
S20261022-41.t: The visit would cement Türkiye's position as Damascus's main patron.

S20261022-42.h: Canada's Carney visits Ankara to elevate ties and deepen defence, energy cooperation
S20261022-42.s: Canadian PM Mark Carney meets Erdoğan on 22-23 October. The two NATO allies are expected to sign a joint declaration on closer defence and energy cooperation and elevate ties to a strategic partnership.
S20261022-42.t: Opens the way for defence-industry and energy cooperation with a NATO partner.

S20261022-43.h: Cyprus talks: Erhürman rejects Varosha proposal; Fidan allows GSI surveys with notification
S20261022-43.s: Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhürman rejected Christodoulides' Varosha proposal. Greek Cypriot negotiator Menelaou said the Pyroi crossing dispute is resolved apart from Louroujina. Fidan said Türkiye will not object to Great Sea Interconnector seabed surveys if given written notification.
S20261022-43.t: Ankara signals conditional flexibility on GSI surveys while the Cyprus track and Libya deal sharpen Eastern Mediterranean disputes.

S20261022-44.h: Turkish press groups call nationwide protests over censorship as Halk TV X account blocked
S20261022-44.s: Press organisations urged journalists and the public to demonstrate on Saturday against the media crackdown. Halk TV's X account, run under a trustee, was made invisible in Türkiye, and another journalist's account was blocked.
S20261022-44.t: Media restrictions deepen criticism from European partners.

S20261022-45.h: Türkiye and Iran hold border security meeting in Maku
S20261022-45.s: Turkish and Iranian officials met in Maku, Iran, for a routine meeting on border security.
S20261022-45.t: Border cooperation matters as Iran faces war risk and Kurdish militancy near the frontier.

S20261023-01.h: IRGC Navy says seven vessels hit near Hormuz, warns US of wider response
S20261023-01.s: Iran's IRGC Navy said four oil-carrying ships were hit and set on fire in the northern Gulf, and three others struck mines west of Hormuz. It warned the US of a wider response and threatened US bases if tankers keep using what it calls illegal routes. Oil prices reached a five-month high, and seafarers say Hormuz traffic is down about 90%.
S20261023-01.t: Disrupted Hormuz traffic and higher oil prices hit Türkiye's energy import bill and widen the risk of a regional war on its borders.

S20261023-02.h: US orders diplomats out of Saudi Arabia citing Houthi threat
S20261023-02.s: The State Department ordered some diplomats and family members to leave Saudi Arabia, saying the Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against the kingdom. Reports suggest similar withdrawals in the UAE, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain amid fears of a return to conflict with Iran.
S20261023-02.t: A US drawdown from Gulf posts signals expected escalation just as Ankara commits to a new Saudi defence arrangement.

S20261023-03.h: Houthi strikes hit Saudi airport and energy sites; Aramco evacuates Dhahran HQ
S20261023-03.s: An attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed two people and injured eight. Aramco reportedly ordered its Dhahran headquarters evacuated. Yemen's Houthi-run forces claim ballistic missile and drone strikes on the Riyadh defence ministry, Yanbu and Abha. Saudi forces intercepted a missile aimed at Najran and a drone over the Riyadh region.
S20261023-03.t: The attacks on the kingdom come as Türkiye prepares to ratify a defence pact that could send Turkish troops to Saudi Arabia.

S20261023-04.h: Pakistan-Saudi-Türkiye Mecca defence pact text revealed; Ankara to seek troop authorisation
S20261023-04.s: The pact text provides for a permanent secretariat, rotating leadership and new members. Türkiye's parliamentary Foreign Affairs Committee will debate the ratification bill on 27 October, and Ankara will seek authorisation to send troops to Saudi Arabia. A Turkish column criticises the risks for regional balances and the Yemen link.
S20261023-04.t: Ratification could commit Turkish forces to defending Saudi Arabia amid the Houthi escalation and Iran tensions.

S20261023-05.h: Fidan hosts first R4+E3 foreign ministers' meeting in Istanbul
S20261023-05.s: Fidan will host the foreign ministers of Germany, the UK, France, Egypt, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia on Friday. They will discuss regional conflicts and Russia-Ukraine in a combined R4/R4+E3 format.
S20261023-05.t: The meeting puts Ankara at the centre of a new Europe-Middle East diplomatic format during the Iran and Yemen crises.

S20261023-06.h: Reports of US-Israeli plan for 72-hour Iran strike campaign after midterms
S20261023-06.s: NYT and FT-based reports say Israel and the US are weighing renewed strikes on Iran after the 3 November midterms, with a drafted 72-hour campaign. The White House says the US will not attack before the elections. A US official says Trump called off planned strikes seven times at the last minute, and Gulf states are bracing.
S20261023-06.t: A renewed Iran war would again threaten Türkiye with border instability, refugee flows and energy shocks.

S20261023-07.h: Iran threatens Gulf oil, AI facilities and undersea cables if war resumes
S20261023-07.s: Iran threatened to strike oil and AI facilities across the Gulf and US regional assets if attacks resume. The IRGC also threatened to cut key internet cables. Parliament speaker Ghalibaf and other officials warned of painful consequences, and the Army chief said drone capabilities were strengthened.
S20261023-07.t: Threats to Gulf infrastructure and communications cables raise regional risk for Turkish trade and energy supply.

S20261023-08.h: Iran sets seven conditions for reopening Hormuz and says it is ready for attrition
S20261023-08.s: Tehran set seven conditions for reopening the Strait and resuming talks. SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Iran is ready for a war of attrition. Its foreign ministry blamed US broken promises for the stalled negotiations.
S20261023-08.t: A prolonged Hormuz standoff keeps pressure on Turkish energy costs and on Ankara's mediation options.

S20261023-09.h: Trump says US 'knocked the hell out of' Iran, accuses Tehran of lifting oil prices
S20261023-09.s: Trump said the US could go further against Iran after inflicting serious damage. He accused Iran of driving up oil prices before the 3 November midterms, claiming fake hits and mines.

S20261023-10.h: Netanyahu orders IDF and Mossad to topple Iran's regime, denies planned attack reports
S20261023-10.s: After a report that Trump blocked an Israeli attack on Iran, Netanyahu told graduating officers that Iran is developing weapons of death and that the regime should be toppled. He also rejected reports that Israel had planned an attack and asked for time to finish the job. Analysts doubt Israel can topple the government, and Israeli officials debate the election context.
S20261023-10.t: Israeli regime-change rhetoric toward Iran raises the odds of a regional war on Türkiye's border.

S20261023-11.h: Egypt weighs military support for Saudi Arabia, limited to defence
S20261023-11.s: Egypt's parliament is preparing a vote on authorising military support to Saudi Arabia against the Houthis. Sisi said support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and borders, not attacking Yemen. The foreign minister called for a diplomatic solution.
S20261023-11.t: Egypt's limited stance contrasts with Ankara's planned troop authorisation and shapes how the Saudi pact is read.

S20261023-12.h: Arab states and Iraq condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
S20261023-12.s: Qatar, the UAE, Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, Yemen, Egypt and Al-Azhar condemned the drone attack on Dammam airport, and India condemned the deadly attacks. Iraq rejected use of its territory to target Saudi Arabia. The European Parliament called for listing the Houthis as terrorists.

S20261023-13.h: Yemeni government forces strike Houthi positions in Taiz
S20261023-13.s: Yemen's army says it carried out 780 strikes in 24 hours and killed 512 Houthi fighters. Airstrikes hit missile launchers, depots and radars. The government warned Houthi recruitment gatherings are legitimate targets.

S20261023-14.h: Yemen fighting displaces 260,000; Taiz faces shortages under Houthi blockade
S20261023-14.s: The WHO reports 1,574 killed and 6,939 injured since August. The UN verified 251 civilian casualties and 260,000 displaced. Taiz residents face food and water shortages after a Houthi blockade cut a supply route.

S20261023-15.h: Libya's eastern parliament ratifies Turkey maritime deal, EU and Egypt object
S20261023-15.s: Eastern Libya's House of Representatives backed the maritime delimitation memorandum with Ankara. Türkiye's Defence Ministry welcomed it and rejected Greek and EU objections. Greece and Egypt are reportedly discussing extending their maritime zone toward Cyprus.
S20261023-15.t: The ratification strengthens Türkiye's Eastern Mediterranean claims but deepens friction with Greece, Cyprus, Egypt and the EU.

S20261023-16.h: Türkiye and Canada upgrade ties to strategic partnership, sign defence agreements
S20261023-16.s: After Erdoğan-Carney talks in Ankara, the two countries signed three agreements on defence industry, air transport and energy. They launched a three-year action plan and will start free trade talks. Erdoğan aims to raise trade from about $3 billion to $5 billion.
S20261023-16.t: The deal adds a defence-industry and financing partner at a time of strained arms access with other allies.

S20261023-17.h: Turkish central bank cuts policy rate 100 points to 36%
S20261023-17.s: The central bank cut its one-week repo rate to 36% from 37%. This is its first cut after five consecutive holds, citing easing inflation.
S20261023-17.t: Easing signals confidence on disinflation but leaves the economy exposed to oil shocks from the Gulf war.

S20261023-18.h: Türkiye awaits Qatar's sales contract for second-hand Eurofighters
S20261023-18.s: Ankara says the Qatar Eurofighter purchase remains on track despite the Iran war and awaits a draft contract from Doha. Qatar and Oman can supply some jets under the UK deal.
S20261023-18.t: The jets are a stopgap for Türkiye's air force modernisation.

S20261023-19.h: Novatek says it is negotiating LNG supplies to Türkiye
S20261023-19.s: The Russian gas firm's CEO said talks are underway on LNG supplies to Türkiye, which he described as careful about energy security.
S20261023-19.t: Adds a Russian LNG option to Ankara's energy diversification during Hormuz disruption.

S20261023-20.h: Kurtulmuş says 'Terror-free Türkiye' process progressing smoothly
S20261023-20.s: Parliament speaker Numan Kurtulmuş said the process is advancing without problems and called on all parties to fulfil their responsibilities.
S20261023-20.t: The process to end PKK violence is central to Türkiye's security and domestic politics.

S20261023-21.h: Iraqi PM reportedly proposes closing Iran border crossings at US request
S20261023-21.s: Prime Minister al-Zaidi reportedly raised closing Iran crossings with the Coordination Framework. The US urged him to honour commitments made to Trump.
S20261023-21.t: Iraq's alignment affects Iran's trade routes and border-region security that Ankara watches.

S20261023-22.h: Russia strikes Kyiv with missiles and drones hours after Witkoff-Putin talks
S20261023-22.s: Russia launched three waves of missiles and drones, including ballistic missiles with cluster warheads, killing at least nine and injuring dozens across Ukraine. Zelenskyy said Moscow struck Kyiv immediately after talks. Kyiv historic sites were damaged and Ukraine intercepted 181 drones.

S20261023-23.h: Witkoff meets Putin; trilateral talks may resume, Abu Dhabi floated as venue
S20261023-23.s: Witkoff met Putin in St Petersburg after presenting proposals in Oslo. Putin said he is ready to resume trilateral talks, and Zelensky confirmed discussions for November. The Kremlin says Abu Dhabi is under consideration.
S20261023-23.t: A new talks venue in Abu Dhabi cuts against Istanbul's hosting ambitions.

S20261023-24.h: Trump suspension of Russian diesel sanctions draws Zelensky and Czech criticism
S20261023-24.s: Zelensky said suspending sanctions would strengthen Putin and called Trump's blame for diesel prices unfair. Czech President Pavel said a truce was close until the diesel decision. Dmitriev says a diesel deal with the US takes effect Friday.

S20261023-25.h: Trump asks Musk to lift Starlink limits on Ukraine's military service
S20261023-25.s: The WSJ reported that Trump asked Musk to lift restrictions on the military version of Starlink. Trump said access was restored, but a Ukrainian official says the speed cap remains. Vance said the decision rests on US policy.

S20261023-26.h: Donetsk makes child evacuation mandatory around Kramatorsk and Sloviansk
S20261023-26.s: Authorities extended mandatory evacuation of families with children to all settlements in the Kramatorsk and Sloviansk communities. Ukraine is reportedly organising Azov-veteran-led groupings to hold the approaches against a Russian push.

S20261023-27.h: Ukraine's Khartiia Corps says Veles pipeline raid advanced behind Russian lines at Kupiansk
S20261023-27.s: Ukrainian troops reportedly moved up to 15 km through underground gas pipelines under the Oskil River. They say they blocked Russian access to the right bank.

S20261023-28.h: Ukraine gains access to NATO procurement agency for weapons
S20261023-28.s: Ukraine will buy weapons and ammunition through the NATO Support and Procurement Agency, according to FT-based reports. Estonia added €10 million to PURL, and Patriot supplies were discussed with NATO.

S20261023-29.h: EU searches for envoy to talk with Putin; Merz demands European role
S20261023-29.s: European diplomats are discussing who should represent the EU in talks, with Stubb, Meloni and Pavel named. Merz and Czech leaders say Europe must take part in negotiations.

S20261023-30.h: European Parliament urges Black Sea naval operation; Moscow cites contacts with Türkiye
S20261023-30.s: MEPs urged the EU to consider a naval mission after attacks on civilian ships. Russian diplomat Grushko said Moscow is in contact with Türkiye on Black Sea security and blamed Ukraine for the escalation.
S20261023-30.t: A European naval role in the Black Sea would test Türkiye's control under the Montreux Convention.

S20261023-31.h: Russia and Ukraine trade accusations over Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant
S20261023-31.s: Rosatom warned that Ukrainian strikes on the plant and Energodar could cause a regional catastrophe. Moscow claims Ukraine blocked staff transit and mined roads, days after Russia took control of the plant.

S20261023-32.h: Ukrainian drones hit Moscow region as Russia reports 163 intercepted
S20261023-32.s: Hundreds of Ukrainian drones targeted the Moscow region, including a military plant, injuring two in Moscow and one in Lipetsk. Atesh claimed communications sabotage near a Moscow data centre.

S20261023-33.h: Belousov says NATO buildup requires Russia-Belarus response
S20261023-33.s: Belousov called for a prompt response to NATO's buildup. Russia and Belarus set a 160-activity cooperation plan, announced the Union Shield 2027 exercise and discussed deterrence.

S20261023-34.h: Syrian troops deploy to Sweida front as Israel moves hardware in
S20261023-34.s: Syrian government troops deployed to the Sweida front line while Israel moved military hardware into the area. A Druze source denied reports Israel plans a base in rural Sweida.
S20261023-34.t: Israeli-Syrian friction in the south limits Ankara's room in Syria.

S20261023-35.h: Israeli raids in southern Syria kill civilian, block UNDOF patrol
S20261023-35.s: Israeli forces killed a disabled man in Jamla, Daraa. Syria's foreign ministry and the UN condemned it. Israel also blocked a UNDOF patrol and blew up a house in Quneitra. Jordan's king rejected Israeli attacks in talks with Shaibani.

S20261023-36.h: Israeli strikes continue in southern Lebanon despite ceasefire
S20261023-36.s: Israeli air and artillery strikes hit southern Lebanon, with about 20 troops and four tanks advancing toward Habbariyeh. Aoun warned of wider escalation. Lebanon's justice minister said a Hezbollah explosives shipment breached security.

S20261023-37.h: Israeli fire kills Palestinians in Gaza as ceasefire erodes
S20261023-37.s: Israeli strikes and gunfire killed at least four people in Gaza. IDF intelligence reportedly says Hamas can only be dismantled by renewed fighting, and the IDF killed a Hamas commando.

S20261023-38.h: Gaza faces bakery closures and hospital fuel crisis
S20261023-38.s: Most bakeries stopped after Israel blocked flour. Seven WFP-supported bakeries could close within 48 hours. Hospitals are near collapse as generator fuel and parts run out.

S20261023-39.h: West Bank settler violence surges during olive harvest
S20261023-39.s: Israel and settlers carried out 409 attacks during the harvest. Israel released most suspects in two settler attacks after US calls. Guterres said the situation is out of control.

S20261023-40.h: Israel heads to 27 October election with Netanyahu courting right
S20261023-40.s: Netanyahu faces rivals including Eisenkot and Bennett. Reuters says both reject a Palestinian state, so policy is unlikely to change. Likud is using a voter-tracking app, and families plan Election Day protests.
S20261023-40.t: A new Israeli government or a re-elected Netanyahu will shape Israeli-Turkish tension in Syria and the Eastern Mediterranean.

S20261023-41.h: Russia frees US veteran Stephen Hubbard after Trump-Putin deal
S20261023-41.s: Putin announced the release of Hubbard, 74, held for over four years, during the Witkoff visit.

S20261023-42.h: Germany arrests Ukrainian suspected of spying for Russia
S20261023-42.s: The suspect allegedly gathered information on armoured vehicle and ammunition production and a Bundeswehr brigade. The military raised its sabotage threat level.

S20261023-43.h: Turkish Cypriot leader offers talks if rotating presidency accepted
S20261023-43.s: Erhürman said he would immediately accept formal negotiations if Christodoulides accepts a rotating presidency. Cyprus separately asked the EU to restore its mutual defence clause.
S20261023-43.t: Cyprus talks affect Ankara's EU relations and Eastern Mediterranean positions.

S20261023-44.h: Turkish journalism pressure grows as trustee named at Halk TV
S20261023-44.s: Halk TV's programme director discussed the appointment of a trustee at the channel. Jailed mayor İmamoğlu urged the public to buy newspapers amid the crackdown.
S20261023-44.t: Media pressure affects Türkiye's domestic politics and its standing with European partners.

S20261023-45.h: MKE unveils TOLGA close-range air defence system
S20261023-45.s: The system's twin 20 mm revolver gun fires 3,200 rounds per minute against drones and kamikaze boats.
S20261023-45.t: Expands Türkiye's indigenous counter-drone defence portfolio.

S20261024-01.h: Trump and envoy Barrack signal possible new US strikes on Iran within days
S20261024-01.s: US ambassador Tom Barrack said a strike on Iran could 'absolutely' happen this weekend, while Washington says it is open to a deal and seeks no regime change. Trump spoke of another 'little Epic Fury' unless Iran agrees terms, and also said he knew nothing about the envoy's remark. Al-Monitor reports signs the US is preparing to resume large-scale strikes, and Trump is weighing a quick end to the war against letting it fade.
S20261024-01.t: A renewed US-Iran escalation would hit Türkiye's border region, energy supply and trade, and Ankara is lobbying publicly against it.

S20261024-02.h: IRGC says two supertankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz and were abandoned
S20261024-02.s: The IRGC said two supertankers carrying over 4.5 million barrels of crude struck naval mines in or south of the Strait of Hormuz, followed by an explosion. Trump accused Iran of fabricating tanker attack reports to raise oil prices before the US midterms. October saw the most recorded ship attacks in the strait and nearby waters since monitoring began in 2017.
S20261024-02.t: Disrupted Hormuz traffic raises Türkiye's energy import costs and strengthens the case for the Istanbul diplomatic track.

S20261024-03.h: Iran sets seven conditions for talks and Hormuz reopening, threatens Gulf cables
S20261024-03.s: Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary said Tehran will neither resume talks nor reopen Hormuz until seven conditions are met. Iranian security officials told Reuters that Tehran has detailed plans to hit Gulf undersea internet cables and US-linked data centres if the US and Israel attack again.
S20261024-03.t: Attacks on Gulf cables and data centres would disrupt regional connectivity and trade routes that Türkiye relies on.

S20261024-04.h: Istanbul talks: eight countries warn new attack on Iran would widen regional war
S20261024-04.s: After the R4+E3 meeting, Hakan Fidan said participants agree a new military attack on Iran would escalate regional conflicts and that diplomacy is the only solution. The Guardian and Al Jazeera report the ministers urged the US and Israel not to resume strikes and to pursue US-Iran diplomacy.
S20261024-04.t: Ankara is positioning itself as the convenor of a diplomatic alternative to war on Iran.

S20261024-05.h: Türkiye hosts first R4+E3 foreign ministers' meeting in Istanbul
S20261024-05.s: Foreign ministers of Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Pakistan (R4) met their counterparts from the E3 and Italy, chaired by Hakan Fidan. The agenda covered Hormuz, Palestine, Yemen, Bab al-Mandab security and Ukraine. Haaretz reports Qatar offered Tehran a non-aggression pact.
