S20261024-05.t: The format puts Türkiye at the centre of Europe-Middle East diplomacy on the Iran war and Hormuz.

S20261024-06.h: Wadephul: Istanbul E4+R4 format to meet regularly, Germany hosts next round
S20261024-06.s: German FM Wadephul said the first E4+R4 meeting surpassed expectations and the ministers agreed to meet regularly. Italy's Tajani described it as a Turkish diplomatic initiative to return to crisis-mitigation diplomacy, and France's Barrot said the eight committed to joint action.
S20261024-06.t: A standing mechanism gives Ankara lasting access to European and regional decision-making.

S20261024-07.h: Türkiye, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan blame Israeli occupation for regional instability
S20261024-07.s: The four R4 foreign ministers issued a joint statement in Istanbul calling Israel's occupation of Palestinian territories the main source of regional instability. Fidan separately said Israeli violations of the Gaza ceasefire undermine trust in the international system and called for aid access.
S20261024-07.t: Ankara is building a joint Muslim-majority position against Israeli policy with Riyadh, Cairo and Islamabad.

S20261024-08.h: Erdoğan receives visiting ministers; Fidan holds bilaterals on Istanbul meeting sidelines
S20261024-08.s: Erdoğan received foreign ministers from Germany, Italy, France, Egypt, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia at Dolmabahçe. Fidan held separate meetings with the British, French, Pakistani, Italian and German ministers and the GCC Secretary-General. He said Ankara will keep taking responsibility for regional issues.
S20261024-08.t: The meetings show Türkiye's attempt to turn the Istanbul format into a lasting mediation mechanism.

S20261024-09.h: US says it is ready for prolonged Iran standoff, keeps port blockade
S20261024-09.s: Mike Waltz said the war will continue until a nuclear deal is struck and Iran's enriched stockpile is eliminated, and that strikes, blockade and sanctions are meant to force concessions. Bessent said Kharg Island oil shipping is near standstill. Iranian exports to China are reported collapsing, while Tehran Times argues the blockade violates the UN Charter.
S20261024-09.t: A long blockade keeps Iranian energy off the market and prolongs the price and border-security pressure on Türkiye.

S20261024-10.h: Iran orders army to top readiness; reports of tighter internal security
S20261024-10.s: Iran's army ordered ground forces to maintain the highest combat readiness. The IRGC Navy commander said US forces moved 600-700 km from Hormuz, and the Foreign Ministry warned against underestimating Iran's defences. Witnesses report more armed patrols, checkpoints and degraded internet, suggesting fear of unrest.
S20261024-10.t: Heightened Iranian alert and internal tension raise the risk of instability on Türkiye's eastern border.

S20261024-11.h: Brent hits $116 on fears of renewed Iran strikes; stocks and gas supply stressed
S20261024-11.s: Brent crude rose to its highest since June 2022 on fears of renewed US strikes on Iran and Iranian threats to Gulf oil facilities. Global markets fell. Analysts warn emergency oil stocks are at multi-decade lows, and the IEA says the EU enters winter with record-low gas reserves.
S20261024-11.t: Higher energy prices strain Türkiye's import bill and inflation fight.

S20261024-12.h: Houthi missiles and drones hit Saudi Arabia; Sanaa reportedly struck
S20261024-12.s: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted 11 drones and a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh, Medina, the Eastern Province, Najran and the south. The Arab League condemned Houthi attacks on Dammam Airport and the Shaybah field, and the UN chief voiced concern. IRNA reports explosions in Sanaa attributed to Saudi airstrikes.
S20261024-12.t: Türkiye is a defence partner of Riyadh and is being drawn into the question of its role against the Houthis.

S20261024-13.h: Egypt weighs troops for Saudi Arabia; Türkiye rules out fighting Houthis
S20261024-13.s: Egypt's security body pledged necessary support to Saudi Arabia while parliament weighs authorising troop deployment. Defence Minister Güler said Türkiye will not fight the Houthis under its trilateral defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.
S20261024-13.t: Ankara is setting limits on its commitments under the pact with Riyadh and Islamabad.

S20261024-14.h: Houthi siege of Taiz cuts off 800,000 from aid, UN warns
S20261024-14.s: The UN says over 800,000 people in Taiz have been cut off from aid since Houthi forces encircled the city in early October. OCHA reports road closures sharply cutting fuel, food and supplies.

S20261024-15.h: Saudi Arabia expands ballistic missile plant, raising regional arms-race risk
S20261024-15.s: Satellite image analysis suggests Saudi Arabia is expanding a ballistic missile plant to produce larger solid-fuel missiles. A study says this could deter Iran and the Houthis but risks a regional missile race.
S20261024-15.t: Saudi missile growth shifts the Gulf military balance and could open defence-cooperation opportunities for Ankara.

S20261024-16.h: Two Israeli soldiers killed near Hebron; Netanyahu vows largest West Bank operation since 1967
S20261024-16.s: Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded others at a Hebron checkpoint, and both attackers died. Netanyahu announced an operation on a scale not seen since 1967. Smotrich called for a comprehensive campaign, days before Israel's election.
S20261024-16.t: A major West Bank offensive would inflame regional opinion and sharpen Ankara's criticism of Israel.

S20261024-17.h: Israel locks down West Bank and raids Hebron after shooting
S20261024-17.s: Netanyahu ordered a full West Bank lockdown and closure of Hebron, with forces sealing entrances. The IDF and Shin Bet began a multi-day search operation for weapons and militant infrastructure. Ben-Gvir ordered demolitions, and the UN chief voiced concern over closures and rising violence.
S20261024-17.t: The closures add to the Palestinian grievances Ankara is raising in diplomatic forums.

S20261024-18.h: Final Israeli polls show opposition ahead of Netanyahu days before 27 October vote
S20261024-18.s: Final polls give Gadi Eisenkot's bloc 54 seats against Netanyahu's 48, with neither reaching a majority. Netanyahu campaigns as the only candidate able to ensure security, and tensions are rising before the election.
S20261024-18.t: A post-election change in Israel's government would affect Ankara's Gaza, Syria and Eastern Mediterranean calculations.

S20261024-19.h: Analysts: Netanyahu could strike Iran after election to force unity government
S20261024-19.s: Analysts say the election result could shape the timing of renewed war with Iran, and that Netanyahu might strike afterwards to pressure rivals into a wartime coalition. The army reportedly doubts regime change is feasible. Netanyahu warned Iran against attacking Israel.
S20261024-19.t: Israeli action against Iran after the vote would pull Türkiye into a wider regional crisis.

S20261024-20.h: Netanyahu warns of banking sanctions and end of US aid
S20261024-20.s: Netanyahu said Israel must prepare for banking sanctions and floated crypto and blockchain alternatives. He also doubted US military aid will continue.
S20261024-20.t: Growing Israeli isolation shapes the diplomatic space Ankara uses against Israel.

S20261024-21.h: Israeli incursions in southern Syria continue as Damascus deploys 1,000 troops
S20261024-21.s: Israeli forces advanced near Saida al-Hanout in Quneitra, shelled Quneitra outskirts and killed a civilian in Jamla, Daraa, which the UN condemned. Hundreds of Syrians protested the incursions. Syria deployed 1,000 troops to its south, with officials saying neither side wants escalation.
S20261024-21.t: Israeli pressure in southern Syria challenges the Damascus government that Türkiye backs.

S20261024-22.h: Gunmen kill at least seven at Karak church funeral in Jordan
S20261024-22.s: Two masked gunmen opened fire on a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, killing six to seven people and wounding dozens. King Abdullah II called it terrorism and vowed retaliation, and a manhunt is under way. The EU, UAE and Syria condemned the attack.
S20261024-22.t: A rare attack on Christians in Jordan points to a new regional terrorism risk.

S20261024-23.h: Cargo ship sinks off Romania after drone strike; Bucharest blames Russia
S20261024-23.s: The Comoros-flagged Khoryv, with Ukrainian and Azerbaijani crew, sank near Romanian waters, killing one sailor with three missing. Romania's president called it Russian escalation on NATO's flank, and von der Leyen condemned it. The European Parliament asked the EU to consider a Black Sea naval operation.
S20261024-23.t: The strike is near Black Sea waters where Türkiye, a NATO member and Montreux guardian, bears responsibility for shipping safety.

S20261024-24.h: Trilateral Ukraine-US-Russia talks set for early November in Abu Dhabi
S20261024-24.s: Zelensky and the Kremlin said negotiating teams will meet in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi, with Witkoff and Kushner involved. Putin said Russia wants a final security settlement, not temporary ceasefires. Whether the EU takes part is under discussion.
S20261024-24.t: Abu Dhabi hosting instead of Istanbul puts Türkiye's mediation role in this war at risk.

S20261024-25.h: Reported US peace plan: Donbas demilitarised zone, no NATO for Ukraine, sanctions relief
S20261024-25.s: Reports say US officials drafted a plan with a demilitarised Donbas, Ukraine dropping its NATO bid and eased sanctions for Russia. The Economist says it also offers EU membership and Nord Stream restart, and calls it dangerous for Ukraine and Europe.
S20261024-25.t: Terms on Black Sea security and NATO enlargement would directly affect Türkiye's strategic environment.

S20261024-26.h: Melania Trump brokers local ceasefire for Oleshky from 29 October
S20261024-26.s: The White House says Melania Trump secured a localised ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky, Kherson, to allow aid and civilian evacuation. The Kremlin confirmed military officials are arranging it, and Ukraine confirmed a humanitarian operation. Some reports give 27 October, and Al Jazeera said neither side had confirmed.

S20261024-27.h: First Russian diesel tanker sails for US under Trump-Putin sanctions-easing deal
S20261024-27.s: The tanker Agioi Fanendes left Primorsk for New York with about 35,000-40,000 tonnes of diesel, the first cargo under the deal. The Kremlin says regular shipments will follow, and Novak says three tankers are heading to the US East Coast. Kyiv sources say fertiliser sanctions relief may be next.
S20261024-27.t: US-Russia energy deals reshape Black Sea and Mediterranean trade flows and Türkiye's leverage as a transit hub.

S20261024-28.h: Ukrainian drones close Moscow airports and hit Russian data centres
S20261024-28.s: Ukrainian drones and balloons closed all four Moscow airports and prompted an evacuation of a Moscow-City tower. Ukrainian drones reportedly hit Yandex, Sber and VKontakte facilities across five regions, causing payment and cloud outages, and a tax service data centre.

S20261024-29.h: Russia and Ukraine swap 270 prisoners each in UAE-mediated exchange
S20261024-29.s: Zelensky announced 270 Ukrainians returned, including Azov fighters and nine civilians. The exchange ran via Belarus, with the US and UAE credited as facilitators. Erdoğan separately cited Türkiye's role in such swaps.

S20261024-30.h: Russian strikes halt DTEK plant and cut power to hundreds of thousands
S20261024-30.s: Overnight attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure left over 500,000 without electricity and stopped a DTEK thermal plant. A drone strike in Lviv region cut power to 175 settlements. Eight people were reported killed.

S20261024-31.h: Russian strikes hit Dnipro, Chernihiv, Kharkiv and Zaporizhia, killing civilians
S20261024-31.s: Russian attacks killed one and injured others in Dnipro, one and injured sixteen in Chernihiv, and three in Zaporizhia. Kharkiv and nearby towns were also hit.

S20261024-32.h: Zelensky: Starlink limits persist and interceptor deliveries are delayed
S20261024-32.s: Zelensky confirmed speed caps on Starlink and Starshield remain despite Trump's claim that Musk restored full service. Kyiv is considering sovereign satellites from ICEYE and Nokia. Rubio is due to revisit the restrictions.

S20261024-33.h: Ukraine seeks interceptors as Russia pushes ballistic attacks
S20261024-33.s: Zelensky warned Russia will intensify ballistic strikes amid a Patriot interceptor shortage, saying Europe holds PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles. Ukraine's defence minister discussed interceptors, NASAMS and F-16 ammunition with Norway.

S20261024-34.h: Moldova expels Russian diplomat after drone with explosives lands near homes
S20261024-34.s: A Russian Geran drone carrying explosives fell near family homes and an energy facility in Chistelnita, Moldova. President Sandu condemned it and Moldova declared a Russian Embassy employee persona non grata.

S20261024-35.h: Austria expels four Russian diplomats over suspected espionage
S20261024-35.s: Austria expelled four Russian diplomats, including an OSCE military security delegate, after intelligence services flagged conduct incompatible with diplomatic rules. Moscow vowed a response.

S20261024-36.h: Kyiv and European intelligence warn of Russian hybrid campaign against EU
S20261024-36.s: Zelensky said Russia is using drone attacks and hybrid war to weaken European support for Ukraine. Ukrainian intelligence claims Russia is intensifying destabilisation and preparing false-flag operations in Europe.

S20261024-37.h: Libya's parliament ratifies Türkiye maritime boundary deal, angering Greece, Cyprus and Israel
S20261024-37.s: Libya's House of Representatives approved the 2019 maritime delimitation memorandum with Türkiye, which the TRNC welcomed. Cyprus's foreign minister said Nicosia is ready to delimit its boundary with Greece. Al-Monitor says it advances Türkiye's push to broker Libyan reunification, though rival interests may limit its influence.
S20261024-37.t: The ratification strengthens Türkiye's Eastern Mediterranean maritime claims and its influence in Libya.

S20261024-38.h: Canada and Türkiye form strategic partnership covering defence, energy and trade
S20261024-38.s: Carney's Ankara visit upgraded ties, launched free trade talks starting 30 November, and produced an Eximbank-EDC credit deal. Carney said Canada is open to buying Turkish military capabilities and will study SSB as a model. His team also raised LGBTQ+ rights concerns.
S20261024-38.t: A NATO partner seeking Turkish defence goods boosts Ankara's export prospects and Western standing.

S20261024-39.h: Grossi says IAEA is ready to verify Iran's nuclear activity, urges deal
S20261024-39.s: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi said the agency has largely prepared to verify Iran's nuclear activities and called for a swift return of inspectors. He said no lasting solution is possible without a diplomatic deal. Iran urged the IAEA to end what it calls selective application of its statute.
S20261024-39.t: A verified nuclear arrangement is what Türkiye's diplomacy aims for to head off further war.

S20261024-40.h: Iraq pledges to disarm militias by 30 June as Baghdad fears joining US-Iran war
S20261024-40.s: PM Ali al-Zaidi said armed groups will hand weapons to the state by 30 June and Iraq will not join regional wars. Washington reportedly asked Baghdad to close Iran border crossings and disarm groups, and an adviser accused Iran of undermining Iraq's security.
S20261024-40.t: Iraqi militia behaviour and stability affect Türkiye's border security and the Development Road project.

S20261024-41.h: Tanker struck by projectile near Oman; UAE battles oil spill
S20261024-41.s: A tanker was hit by an unknown projectile near Oman's Limah but continued its voyage. Another struck off the UAE coast caused a fire and an oil spill on Umm Al Quwain beaches. Gulf oil spills have grown since the war began on 28 February.
S20261024-41.p: Strait of Hormuz and UAE coast

S20261024-42.h: Israeli strikes hit southern Lebanon near Nabatieh as drones overfly Beirut
S20261024-42.s: Israeli airstrikes and artillery hit southern Lebanon near Nabatieh while drones overflew Beirut and Tyre at low altitude.

S20261024-43.h: Iran-linked plots in Britain: bomb manual and Yom Kippur trial
S20261024-43.s: Reports say Iran sent a bomb-making manual and organised plots in the UK. Two Iranians will stand trial over an alleged plot to bomb a Jewish community in northern England on Yom Kippur.

S20261024-44.h: Erdoğan stresses mediation, citing Russia-Ukraine prisoner swaps
S20261024-44.s: Erdoğan reaffirmed Türkiye's commitment to mediation and diplomacy, pointing to its role in Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchanges and mediation efforts in Africa.
S20261024-44.t: Erdoğan is projecting Türkiye as an indispensable mediator.

S20261024-45.s: ASELSAN signed a $442.5 million export contract with an international customer.
S20261024-45.t: The deal adds to Türkiye's defence export growth.

S20261024-46.h: Turkish police arrest 34 including Çukurova mayors in bribery probe
S20261024-46.s: Authorities arrested 34 suspects, including current and former mayors of Adana's Çukurova district, in a bribery and procurement investigation. Mayor Emrah Kozay was among those arrested.
S20261024-46.t: Another operation against opposition municipalities feeds the domestic political polarisation.

S20261025-01.h: Pentagon presents Trump options for new Iran strikes; Trump says strike or deal 'tomorrow'
S20261025-01.s: The Pentagon has reportedly given Trump options for fresh strikes on Iranian nuclear sites and infrastructure while more US warships head to the region. Trump says he may have to finish what he started and that the US could strike tomorrow or reach a 'big, beautiful' deal. He also denied knowing of weekend strike plans, after envoy Tom Barrack said action could occur, and Istanbul diplomacy produced no breakthrough.
S20261025-01.t: Renewed US-Iran war would hit Türkiye's border region, energy and trade, and undercut Ankara's mediation and Istanbul diplomacy.

S20261025-02.h: US intelligence warns Iranian plots against Americans are advanced; embassy staff cut region-wide
S20261025-02.s: A US intelligence memo, reported by Axios and others, says Iran has sharply stepped up plots to target US personnel in the Middle East, some at advanced stages. The State Department is reducing embassy staff and evacuating diplomats and families from missions. US forces are reportedly also moving standoff missiles, bunker-busters and an amphibious assault ship.
S20261025-02.t: US drawdowns and plot warnings point to an imminent escalation near Türkiye and raise risks for US-linked sites and diplomats in the region.

S20261025-03.h: Iran vows to bar US warships from the Gulf, IRGC threatens multiplied response
S20261025-03.s: Iran's armed forces chief said US warships will never be allowed into the Persian Gulf. IRGC spokesman Mohebbi warned that any enemy mistake or limited strike would be answered several times over. Officials also threatened regional infrastructure and Israel, and analysts sense war is closer.
S20261025-03.t: Threats to Gulf shipping and regional infrastructure endanger Türkiye's energy supply and trade routes.

S20261025-04.h: Tehran blames US for failed interim deal as Pezeshkian urges new attempt
S20261025-04.s: President Pezeshkian and other Iranian officials blamed Washington for the collapse of an interim deal and called for a new attempt at talks. He also urged an end to the 'neither war nor peace' limbo. Analysts say the lack of progress keeps the risk of renewed war alive, and France warned escalation would hurt both sides and raise oil prices.
S20261025-04.t: Ankara hosted recent diplomacy and benefits from a revived US-Iran track that lowers escalation risk.

S20261025-05.h: Reported Iranian offer to reopen Hormuz for lifting US blockade; Iranian media deny it
S20261025-05.s: TASS reported that Iran proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz in return for the US lifting its naval blockade, relayed through Pakistani mediators. Iranian media denied that a new offer was sent. Pakistan is separately mediating while deploying troops to defend Saudi Arabia against Iran-aligned groups.
S20261025-05.t: Reopening Hormuz would ease the oil and trade shock on Türkiye, and Pakistan's mediation role overlaps with Ankara's own diplomacy.

S20261025-06.h: Two supertankers disabled by sea mines near Hormuz, IRGC says
S20261025-06.s: The IRGC says two supertankers carrying more than 4.5 million barrels were disabled by sea mines on an unauthorised route south of Hormuz. Gulf News also reports tankers striking mines near the strait.
S20261025-06.t: Mining of the strait prolongs the oil-price and shipping disruption that weighs on Türkiye's economy.

S20261025-07.h: Houthis declare Riyadh's King Khalid Airport a target; missiles intercepted over capital
S20261025-07.s: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saria declared King Khalid Airport a military target and warned airlines. The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting a ballistic missile fired at Riyadh, and the airport is now operating from two terminals. Civil defence alerts were issued in several areas.
S20261025-07.t: Houthi escalation against Saudi Arabia, Ankara's defence-pact partner, raises pressure on Türkiye's Gulf security posture.

S20261025-08.h: Houthi missiles and drones hit across Saudi Arabia, including Mecca area, Yanbu and Aramco sites
S20261025-08.s: Saudi forces intercepted multiple Houthi missiles aimed at Taif, Yanbu, Jeddah, Mecca and Medina, with debris falling on several cities. The Houthis claim strikes on Aramco facilities and Dammam airport in retaliation for Saudi airstrikes on Yemen. Flight disruptions were reported.
S20261025-08.t: Strikes on Saudi oil and holy cities test the Türkiye-Saudi-Pakistan security framework and endanger energy markets.

S20261025-09.h: Houthis claim missile strikes on Aden; Saudi airstrikes reported on Sanaa and Mokha
S20261025-09.s: The Houthis claimed ballistic missile strikes on Aden's airport, port and coast guard base, and said Saudi airstrikes hit Sanaa and Mokha. Explosions were heard in Aden, with causes unclear, and Riyadh did not respond immediately.

S20261025-10.h: Saudi, Turkish, Egyptian, Pakistani ministers meet in Istanbul, urge Hormuz reopening and diplomacy
S20261025-10.s: Foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, Egypt and Pakistan met in Istanbul. They called for reopening Hormuz, said the Iran-Israel-US conflict can only be solved by diplomacy, and urged the Houthis to stop attacks on Saudi Arabia. Türkiye ruled out combat against the Houthis under its defence pact.
S20261025-10.t: Ankara positions itself as convenor of a regional diplomatic bloc while limiting military exposure in the Houthi conflict.

S20261025-11.h: Pakistan ratifies Mecca pact with Türkiye and Saudi Arabia
S20261025-11.s: Pakistan announced ratification of the Mecca pact signed with Türkiye and Saudi Arabia. Operational matters remain under trilateral discussion.
S20261025-11.t: The ratification advances a trilateral security architecture with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

S20261025-12.h: Fidan meets Yemen's foreign minister, to call Houthi attacks on civilians unacceptable
S20261025-12.s: Hakan Fidan met Yemen's foreign minister in Istanbul to discuss ties and ending the conflict. Turkish officials planned to say Houthi attacks on civilians are unacceptable and urge dialogue. Yemen's minister said operations against the Houthis will continue until goals are met.
S20261025-12.t: Türkiye is courting the Yemeni government and signalling alignment with Riyadh without military involvement.

S20261025-13.h: US issues Gulf, Israel and Iraq travel warnings over Houthi and Iranian threats
S20261025-13.s: Washington urged citizens to reconsider travel to Saudi Arabia and the UAE and updated advisories for Israel, citing Iran and Houthi threats. It warned attacks could escalate rapidly and renewed a Do Not Travel notice for Iraq. The State Department said the advisories do not indicate new Houthi capabilities.

S20261025-14.h: Israel displaces thousands in Hebron, levels neighbourhood after soldiers' deaths
S20261025-14.s: After two soldiers were killed, the IDF removed an estimated 250 Palestinian families from Hebron and demolished buildings across about 35 hectares. Estimates of those displaced range from about 1,200 to 2,500, with more evictions planned. Netanyahu called it the largest West Bank operation since 1967.
S20261025-14.t: The operation feeds Turkish criticism of Israel and the legal and diplomatic campaign against Netanyahu.

S20261025-15.h: Two Israeli soldiers killed at Hebron checkpoint by Palestinian gunmen
S20261025-15.s: Two Palestinian fighters killed two Israeli soldiers at the Farsh al-Hawa checkpoint after a roughly 20-minute confrontation. The attack, days before Israel's election, triggered the Hebron operation.

S20261025-16.h: Israel locks down West Bank, bans workers, raids dozens of towns before election
S20261025-16.s: The Israeli army began a full lockdown of the West Bank, with raids in at least 15 northern towns. The military will bar Palestinian workers' movement and close land crossings on Election Day.

S20261025-17.h: Israel votes Tuesday with no bloc projected to reach a majority
S20261025-17.s: Final polls show Netanyahu's bloc around 50 seats versus 52 for the opposition, with Eisenkot leading. Opposition and Arab parties weigh a coalition or minority government. Tens of thousands rallied in Tel Aviv for an October 7 inquiry, and the army is on highest alert.
S20261025-17.t: The result shapes Israel's posture toward Türkiye, Syria and Gaza, and the prospect of a US-Israel strike on Iran.

S20261025-18.h: Trump advisers reportedly frustrated with Netanyahu; Netanyahu says US aid will end
S20261025-18.s: Axios reports most of Trump's close advisers opposed his decision to back Netanyahu in Israel's election, and see opportunities if he loses. Netanyahu said the end of US military aid is a matter of time and ordered preparations for possible financial sanctions.
S20261025-18.t: A weakened Netanyahu-Trump link could shift US-Israel regional coordination that bears on Türkiye.

S20261025-19.h: Turkish court opens trial of Netanyahu and 34 Israelis over flotilla interception
S20261025-19.s: A Turkish court opened the trial in absentia of Netanyahu and 34 other Israelis over the interception of the Gaza-bound Sumud flotilla. It upheld their arrest warrants.
S20261025-19.t: The case is a legal instrument of Ankara's pressure on Israel and adds friction in bilateral relations.

S20261025-20.h: Gunmen kill eight at Greek Orthodox funeral in Jordan; King orders 'iron fist'
S20261025-20.s: Gunmen attacked a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak, killing at least eight and wounding about 27 to 40. The attackers remain at large and no link to known groups has been established. King Abdullah ordered a harsh response and Jordan tightened security at malls and embassies.
S20261025-20.t: Türkiye condemned the attack; instability in Jordan adds to the regional security burden.

S20261025-21.h: Hezbollah renews pledge not to intervene militarily for Tehran
S20261025-21.s: Hezbollah repeated that it will not intervene militarily in support of Iran in a new confrontation with the US.

S20261025-22.h: Israel holds 700 sq km of south Lebanon, keeps striking; Tampa talks stall
S20261025-22.s: Israel occupies about 700 square kilometres of southern Lebanon as a security belt and struck the south despite a ceasefire. US-hosted Lebanon-Israel talks in Tampa ended without breakthrough as Israel refused to leave pilot zones. A poll finds 66% of Lebanese Shi'ites back transferring Hezbollah's weapons to the state.

S20261025-23.h: Baghdad suspects Israel hit Chinese air defences held by Iraqi factions
S20261025-23.s: Iraq reportedly believes Israel struck militia weapons supplied by Iran, including Chinese-made air defence systems, in mid-October. The Jerusalem Post says the report's escalation claims are questionable.

S20261025-24.h: Iraqi militias cite 171 US airspace violations; Iraqi PM says no US troops remain
S20261025-24.s: Iraq's Islamic Resistance claims 171 US airspace violations in under a month, and the US embassy warns of rising terror risk. Iraq's PM says no US troops remain in Iraq and aims to bring all weapons under state control by next June.

S20261025-25.h: Dozens of Russian-linked hybrid incidents across Europe; Merz warns of destabilisation
S20261025-25.s: Officials linked at least 52 incidents in 17 European countries between April and October to Russian or Belarusian hybrid operations. Chancellor Merz said Russia seeks daily to destabilise Germany through cyberattacks, sabotage and threats to infrastructure.

S20261025-26.h: Drone debris found in Latvia's Alūksne district
S20261025-26.s: Latvian forces found debris of an unidentified foreign drone in Alūksne district, and military and police opened an investigation.

S20261025-27.h: Fidan hints rival Libyan administrations near reunification; Greek lobby targets Turkey-Libya deal
S20261025-27.s: Fidan suggested Libya's eastern and western administrations may be nearing reunification, hinting at an imminent Ankara announcement. A Greek-American group urged Rubio to reject the Turkey-Libya maritime memorandum.
S20261025-27.t: A unified Libya would consolidate Ankara's influence and the maritime memorandum underpinning its Mediterranean claims.

S20261025-28.h: Ankara protests Greece's appointment of muftis in Western Thrace
S20261025-28.s: The Turkish Foreign Ministry, parliament speaker and AK Party officials accused Greece of violating Turkish minority rights by appointing muftis in Komotini and Xanthi. They called on Athens to honour Lausanne obligations and recognise elected muftis.
S20261025-28.t: The dispute adds to Turkish-Greek friction over minority rights and Lausanne commitments.

S20261025-29.h: AKSUNGUR drone conducts first submarine-detection sortie during TURNAs-26
S20261025-29.s: TUSAŞ's AKSUNGUR UAV deployed three ASELBUOY buoys off Antalya in the Navy's TURNAs-26 exercise and collected acoustic data. This is a first for the platform.
S20261025-29.t: It extends Turkish anti-submarine warfare reach with indigenous UAVs.

S20261025-30.h: Syrians protest Israeli raids as Amnesty accuses Israel of unlawful destruction
S20261025-30.s: Protests spread across Syria, including near the Golan Heights, after a disabled man died in an Israeli raid. Amnesty accused Israel of unlawful destruction of civilian property and deadly attacks in Syria.
S20261025-30.t: Israeli activity in southern Syria collides with Türkiye's interests in Syria.

S20261025-31.h: US envoy Barrack distances Washington from Druze leader, alleges drug trafficking
S20261025-31.s: Tom Barrack said the US does not back a Druze religious leader in southern Syria and accused unnamed local actors of drug trafficking.
S20261025-31.t: Washington's distancing from Druze separatism aligns with Ankara's preference for a unified Syria.

S20261025-32.h: Ukraine strikes Russian plants and airfield, from Tolyatti to Omsk
S20261025-32.s: Ukraine's General Staff says it hit the Proton-Elektrotex plant in Orel, the Tolyattikauchuk plant in Tolyatti and an aircraft at Yeysk airfield. Drones also hit a chemical plant in Omsk, about 2,500 km from the border. Three people were reportedly killed in Oryol.

S20261025-33.h: Blackout hits all of occupied Crimea after Taman substation attack
S20261025-33.s: An overnight attack damaged the Taman substation in Krasnodar Krai, causing mass blackouts across occupied Crimea.

S20261025-34.h: Russia, Ukraine and US agree local Oleshky ceasefire for humanitarian operation
S20261025-34.s: A localised ceasefire in occupied Oleshky runs from 27 October to allow a humanitarian operation. Zelensky says Ukraine will comply and hopes for US mediation, and MEP Picierno ended her hunger strike.

S20261025-35.h: Starlink and Starshield speeds restored for Ukrainian forces after a week of limits
S20261025-35.s: Ukraine's defence ministry says Starshield speeds are back above 400 km/h after restrictions that disrupted drone and frontline operations. The episode strained US-Ukraine ties.

S20261025-36.h: Reports reveal US asked SpaceX to toggle Starlink; senators press Hegseth
S20261025-36.s: Reuters-based reports say successive US administrations asked SpaceX to enable or disable Starlink in Ukraine, Iran and elsewhere. US senators threaten to block appointments until Ukrainian access is secured, and the UK PM asked Trump to ensure full access.

S20261025-37.h: Zelensky ready to freeze front line; new US-Russia-Ukraine talks eyed for Abu Dhabi
S20261025-37.s: Zelensky says Ukraine is ready to freeze fighting along the current line without territorial concessions. US sources say talks could be held in Abu Dhabi or Switzerland. Rubio calls Donbas the central issue, Trump floats 200% tariffs on both sides, and US envoys again met Putin.
S20261025-37.t: A Black Sea settlement would affect Türkiye's trade and mediation role.

S20261025-38.h: Ukraine received only 24 Patriot interceptors in three months
S20261025-38.s: Zelensky said Ukraine got just 24 Patriot missiles from the US over three months against a need near 350 a month. The Atlantic reports CIA Director Ratcliffe would not block Trump from cutting intelligence sharing, though early warnings continue.

S20261025-39.h: Russian drones and missiles kill civilians across Ukraine; Moscow claims 616 drones downed
S20261025-39.s: Russian attacks killed several civilians in Dnipropetrovsk, Sumy, Kharkiv, Chernihiv and Donetsk regions, with 126 drones launched overnight. Russia's Defence Ministry says it destroyed 616 Ukrainian drones and claims strikes in Chornomorsk.

S20261025-40.h: Twelve states including Iran, Russia, China and Pakistan condemn attacks on nuclear sites
S20261025-40.s: Twelve countries issued a joint statement at the UN General Assembly First Committee that safeguarded nuclear facilities must never be attacked. Iran's UN envoy condemned US and Israeli attacks and called for impartial IAEA reporting.

S20261025-41.h: Pezeshkian to visit Moscow; Russia denies Bushehr staff evacuation
S20261025-41.s: Pezeshkian will travel to Moscow for talks with Putin. Russia's embassy denied reports it is evacuating staff from the Bushehr plant. Al-Monitor reports Putin prioritises Trump over Iran in mediation.

S20261025-42.h: Gaza ceasefire strained by Israeli strikes and food shortages
S20261025-42.s: Israeli attacks killed Palestinians in Gaza despite the ceasefire. Bakeries are closing for lack of flour, and calls are growing for the WFP to end its Palantir contract.

S20261025-43.h: Turkish press groups march over trustees at Halk TV and TELE1
S20261025-43.s: Journalists marched in Istanbul and Gebze for press freedom, protesting arrests, trustee appointments and access bans.
S20261025-43.t: Pressure on opposition media is a domestic political stress for the government.

S20261025-44.h: Germany in talks to buy Ukrainian jet-powered Bars drones
S20261025-44.s: Germany is reportedly negotiating to buy Ukrainian jet-powered drones with a range of about 1,000 km as it rebuilds precision munitions stocks.

S20261025-45.h: Kurtulmuş says Terror-Free Türkiye process goes beyond PKK disarmament
S20261025-45.s: Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş said the Terror-Free Türkiye process paves the way for unity and brotherhood beyond the PKK's disarmament.
S20261025-45.t: It signals the government's framing of the PKK process as a broader national settlement.

S20261027-01.h: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials hold first high-level talks with Iran in Tehran
S20261027-01.s: Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalın travelled to Tehran under the Mecca defence pact. They met President Pezeshkian and held a quadrilateral meeting to head off renewed US-Israeli war with Iran. It is the first high-level contact since the conflict reached Saudi Arabia and Yemen. Qatar's mediation also features, and Saudi Arabia says the visit seeks dialogue.
S20261027-01.t: Türkiye, through MIT chief Kalın, is a co-guarantor in a new Saudi-Pakistani-Turkish track that puts Ankara at the centre of de-escalation with Iran.

S20261027-02.h: Tehran talks end with pledge on regional security without foreign interference
S20261027-02.s: The four delegations pledged continued security cooperation and agreed that regional states should maintain regional security without foreign interference. Topics included Israeli activity, Palestine and Lebanon. Iran's security council secretary spoke of a positive atmosphere, and Pezeshkian said Tehran backs any understanding that unifies Islamic countries.
S20261027-02.t: Ankara gains a formal framework with Riyadh, Islamabad and Tehran to shape regional security while Israeli and US pressure on Iran grows.

S20261027-03.h: Reports: US ready to strike Iran within 96 hours of a Trump order
S20261027-03.s: CNN-sourced reports say US forces could launch large-scale strikes on Iran within 96 hours of an order, and Washington has drawn up a target list covering nuclear, oil and military sites. Trump has held back and no final decision is reported. European gas prices hit a four-year high, and analysts see possible strikes after the US midterms or earlier.
S20261027-03.t: A renewed US-Iran war would hit Türkiye's border region, energy prices and its mediation role.

S20261027-04.h: Netanyahu pressed military for pre-election Iran operation; Zamir and Mossad resisted
S20261027-04.s: Reports say Netanyahu pushed for a swift Iran operation before the election, opposed by IDF chief Zamir and senior Mossad officials who feared political motives. Netanyahu and Katz deny any plan to attack before the vote or to dismiss Zamir. Lieberman asked for a treason probe, and TASS says Trump was not persuaded.
S20261027-04.t: It shows Israeli electoral politics may drive escalation against Iran, a risk Ankara is trying to contain.

S20261027-05.h: Houthis hit Riyadh airport and Saudi East-West pipeline sites in new attacks
S20261027-05.s: The Houthis claimed a ballistic missile attack on Riyadh's King Khalid airport and drone strikes on East-West pipeline pumping stations. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted missiles and drones, and debris fell on Khamis Mushait. Around 86-90% of Riyadh flights were cancelled in October, with limited resumption. Arab interior ministers condemned attacks on the Makkah and Madinah regions.
S20261027-05.t: Houthi pressure on Saudi Arabia drives the Mecca pact's cohesion, in which Türkiye is a partner.

S20261027-06.h: Saudi-led coalition strikes Houthi launchers and missile tunnels in Yemen
S20261027-06.s: The coalition said it destroyed missile launchers in Sanaa, one used in a recent Riyadh attack, plus storage tunnels, launch platforms and a missile facility. This is the Saudi counter-strike after the Houthi escalation.

S20261027-07.h: Egypt's parliament authorises military support for Saudi Arabia against Houthis
S20261027-07.s: Parliament authorised Sisi to send military support, including possible troop deployment, if Riyadh requests it. The support is described as defensive and limited to Saudi territory and borders. Cairo ruled out strikes on Yemen and has not joined the Mecca pact.
S20261027-07.t: Egyptian backing widens the Saudi-led camp that Türkiye and Pakistan also belong to.

S20261027-08.h: Jordan strikes southern Syria after church attack; Damascus closes border crossing
S20261027-08.s: Jordanian air strikes in southern Syria (Daraa) killed five to seven people, including children, after a church attack in Karak that killed nine. Jordan arrested three suspects, and no group has claimed the attack. Syria says the strikes were not coordinated and closed its crossing with Jordan, while saying contacts continue.
S20261027-08.t: A Jordan-Syria rupture adds instability in southern Syria, where Türkiye backs Damascus.

S20261027-09.h: Israel votes in tight election; Eisenkot's party narrowly ahead of Netanyahu's Likud
S20261027-09.s: Israel holds its first election since 7 October, with no clear governing majority projected and Netanyahu fighting for survival. Likud is split over turnout and reportedly weighing a 'rigged election' narrative if it loses. Arab turnout and possible unity or post-election scenarios are widely discussed. Ben-Gvir raided Al-Aqsa on the eve of the vote.
S20261027-09.t: The outcome shapes Israel's posture toward Iran, Syria and Gaza, all files that touch Turkish interests.

S20261027-10.h: Netanyahu closes campaign warning of Iranian threat, hinting at restarting war
S20261027-10.s: Netanyahu said he and Trump could restart the war on Iran if he wins, and warned of potential annihilation if rivals win. The Washington Post reports he told US officials Eisenkot would be his best partner if hostilities resume. His adviser argued the Trump-Netanyahu partnership could help remove Iran's leadership.
S20261027-10.t: Election rhetoric signals continued Israeli appetite for confrontation with Iran.

S20261027-11.h: Libya's parliament ratifies Turkey-Libya maritime deal; Greece, Egypt and others reject it
S20261027-11.s: Libya's parliament ratified the 2019 maritime memorandum with Türkiye, reviving eastern Mediterranean tensions. Greece, Cyprus, Egypt, the UAE, Bahrain and others declared it null and void, and Greece and Egypt agreed to pursue extending their EEZ deal eastward. The US State Department first called the deal unconstructive and provocative, then corrected its statement.
S20261027-11.t: The ratification strengthens Ankara's maritime claims but draws a united front of Greece, Cyprus, Egypt and Gulf states.

S20261027-12.h: Erdoğan defends Libya maritime deal, vows to confront expansionist actors
S20261027-12.s: Erdoğan urged respect for the Türkiye-Libya joint will on maritime jurisdiction, saying Ankara only protects its rights. He also vowed to confront actors fuelling regional conflict and said Türkiye's compass is its national interest.
S20261027-12.t: Sets Ankara's public line as eastern Mediterranean opposition builds.

S20261027-13.h: Türkiye extends seabed survey NAVTEX for gas pipeline to northern Cyprus
S20261027-13.s: Türkiye issued and extended navtex warnings through 31 December for seabed surveys between its southern coast and Cyprus ahead of a planned gas pipeline to the island.
S20261027-13.t: Advances a Turkey-northern Cyprus energy link amid fresh Mediterranean friction.

S20261027-14.h: Israel to supply Cyprus with new offshore patrol vessel
S20261027-14.s: Israel agreed to supply the Greek Cypriot administration with a new offshore patrol vessel and upgrade systems on an existing one.
S20261027-14.t: Israeli-Cypriot defence ties add to Ankara's eastern Mediterranean concerns.

S20261027-15.h: PKK-linked Sinjar units disarm and join Iraqi security forces
S20261027-15.s: Iraq announced that the Sinjar Protection Units (YBS) are handing over weapons and joining state forces, about 4,000 members under the Interior Ministry and Hashd al-Shaabi. Iraqi forces took over positions in Sinjar. Daily Sabah ties it to the YPG's dissolution announcement two months earlier.
S20261027-15.t: It advances the end-of-PKK process and removes an armed PKK affiliate from Türkiye's southern border region.

S20261027-16.h: Kurtulmuş warns provocateurs may try to derail Terror-Free Türkiye process
S20261027-16.s: Parliament Speaker Kurtulmuş urged careful language and actions, warning that provocateurs may try to derail the process.
S20261027-16.t: The process to end PKK violence remains politically sensitive at home.

S20261027-17.h: Iran says it controls Hormuz as US touts role in Gulf oil exports
S20261027-17.s: Iran's armed forces chief said Hormuz remains under Iranian control and warned vessels violating its protocols. The US says the strait is free of mines, and CENTCOM claims it helped export 1.5 billion barrels. Britain and France would deploy mine-hunting drones only once fighting stops.
S20261027-17.t: Hormuz disruption affects Turkish energy costs and trade.

S20261027-18.h: Iran says US not serious on negotiations, sets seven conditions
S20261027-18.s: Iran's Foreign Ministry said the US is not serious about talks and rejected claims about its nuclear programme. An Iranian official said Washington must accept Tehran's seven conditions first. A ship caught fire off Iraq's coast.
S20261027-18.t: Stalled US-Iran diplomacy raises the stakes of Ankara's mediation.

S20261027-19.h: Iranian hardliners attack Pezeshkian and Tehran's outreach to Saudi, Turkish, Pakistani officials
S20261027-19.s: Anti-negotiation hardliners turned against Pezeshkian over talks with the US. Kayhan warned the Saudi-Turkish-Pakistani initiative could weaken Tehran's leverage.
S20261027-19.t: Internal Iranian resistance could limit what the Tehran diplomacy delivers.

S20261027-20.h: Reports: Hezbollah rearming with Iranian funds, preparing for new war
S20261027-20.s: Sources say Hezbollah has used a lull to buy explosives and drones and rebuild command structures with Iranian money.
S20261027-20.t: A renewed Israel-Hezbollah war would further destabilise the Levant.

S20261027-21.h: Berri says Hezbollah will not fight alongside Iran if war resumes
S20261027-21.s: Lebanese Speaker Nabih Berri conveyed to President Aoun that Hezbollah would not fight on Iran's side if war resumes.

S20261027-22.h: Israel strikes southern Lebanon despite ceasefire
S20261027-22.s: Israeli forces carried out air and artillery strikes and blasts in southern Lebanon, including near Qantara and Zawtar al-Sharqiya, despite a ceasefire and framework agreement.

S20261027-23.h: UN commission accuses Israel of crimes against humanity in West Bank, genocide in Gaza
S20261027-23.s: A UN commission says Israel committed war crimes and crimes against humanity in the occupied territories and continued 'genocidal acts' in Gaza after the ceasefire. Israel rejected the report as misinformation.
S20261027-23.t: Adds to the international legal pressure on Israel that Ankara has championed.

S20261027-24.h: Israeli operation in Hebron displaces thousands; UN warns of ethnic cleansing
S20261027-24.s: Israel's operation in Hebron, after a gun attack killed two Israeli soldiers, displaced roughly 2,000-3,200 Palestinians. The UN rights chief warned of possible ethnic cleansing and urged an end to disproportionate force.

S20261027-25.h: Russia says talks won't pause fighting; Ukraine seeks to bring trilateral talks forward
S20261027-25.s: The Kremlin said resuming US-backed trilateral talks places no limits on military operations. Zelensky expects negotiators to meet in early November, and Kyiv wants to move the Abu Dhabi round up by a week and involve the EU.
S20261027-25.t: Türkiye has offered itself as a venue and mediator in Ukraine diplomacy.

S20261027-26.h: Telegraph: Putin may demand NATO cut presence near Russia to 1997 levels
S20261027-26.s: The Telegraph reports Russia plans to use the new talks to demand NATO reduce forces in Poland, the Baltics and Finland to 1997 levels.
S20261027-26.t: Any NATO force-posture bargain would involve Türkiye as an ally.

S20261027-27.h: Local ceasefire in Oleshky allows civilian evacuation, brokered with Melania Trump's help
S20261027-27.s: Russia and Ukraine announced a local ceasefire in occupied Oleshky from 27 October for a humanitarian corridor, with Moscow preparing convoys for residents.

S20261027-28.h: Ukraine hits Energia plant in Yelets, Russia's glide-bomb battery maker
S20261027-28.s: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed strikes on the Energia plant in Yelets, which produces batteries for aerial bomb guidance systems and Iskander-M power sources. OSINT shows at least seven hits and serious damage.

S20261027-29.h: Ukrainian drones hit Voronezh industrial sites, killing two
S20261027-29.s: Overnight Ukrainian drone and missile attacks struck Voronezh, including an aircraft production association and a petrochemical plant. Two died and 17 were injured, with fires in the city; Russia says it shot down 113 drones.

S20261027-30.h: Zelensky: US holding up Patriot and NASAMS missiles awaiting Hegseth's approval
S20261027-30.s: Zelensky said Ukraine has waited nearly a month for US approval of a large batch of air defence missiles and told officials to press Washington again.

S20261027-31.h: UN inquiry: Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy are crimes against humanity
S20261027-31.s: The UN Commission of Inquiry found Russian attacks on energy infrastructure constitute war crimes and crimes against humanity, and that foreign nationals were trafficked into its military.

S20261027-32.h: EU releases €4.9bn from European Peace Facility for Ukraine
S20261027-32.s: The EU Council mobilised about €4.9bn, mostly to reimburse member states for past aid and the rest for a training mission.

S20261027-33.h: Germany prepares to buy Ukrainian Bars cruise missiles
S20261027-33.s: Germany plans to buy an initial batch of Ukrainian-German Bars missiles for Bundeswehr testing, with an agreement expected within weeks pending technical tests.

S20261027-34.h: Serbia's student-led opposition defeats Vučić's party, ending his 14-year rule
S20261027-34.s: The Student List won Serbia's 25 October parliamentary election and Vučić conceded. The winners say they will not impose sanctions on Russia.

S20261027-35.h: Romania says Russian sabotage network behind fire near weapons factory
S20261027-35.s: Romanian intelligence identified a Russian-run sabotage network allegedly behind a September industrial fire. President Dan said Russia sharply escalated attacks on NATO's eastern flank this month.

S20261027-36.h: European defence ministers: Putin not seeking peace; E5 names Russia top threat
S20261027-36.s: E5 defence ministers meeting in Paris reaffirmed support for Ukraine, said Putin is playing for time and Kallas warned of a brutal winter. Their joint assessment will name Russia the greatest threat. Kallas also warned of serious risk of renewed US-Iran escalation.

S20261027-37.h: ASELSAN signs €523m contract for new-generation air and missile defence
S20261027-37.s: ASELSAN signed a €523 million contract with the SSB to develop a new-generation air and missile defence system.
S20261027-37.t: Strengthens domestic air defence, a priority amid regional escalation.

S20261027-38.h: Türkiye, Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia prepare joint defence training and R&D project
S20261027-38.s: The four states are preparing to announce a joint defence training and R&D project under the recently signed Badr deal.
S20261027-38.t: Extends Türkiye's defence-cooperation network among Muslim-majority states.

S20261027-39.h: Presidential chief adviser Oktay Saral resigns over remarks on Azerbaijan
S20261027-39.s: Oktay Saral resigned after remarks he made about Azerbaijan.
S20261027-39.t: Touches Ankara-Baku ties, a core relationship for Türkiye.

S20261027-40.h: Car bomb and drone strike reported on Damascus-Homs highway
S20261027-40.s: A deadly car bomb on the Damascus-Homs highway was followed by a drone reportedly targeting commander Abu Abdulrahman al-Libi in Qara.

S20261027-41.h: Iraq closes al-Shib crossing with Iran; Maysan leader threatens protests
S20261027-41.s: Baghdad closed the crossing citing smuggling concerns, while Iraqi politicians blame US pressure. A court ordered the arrest of the Maysan council chief who threatened blockades, and PM al-Zaidi ordered an inquiry.

S20261027-42.h: Oman calls for security framework and non-aggression pact among eight Gulf states including Iran
S20261027-42.s: Oman proposed a security framework and non-aggression pact among eight Gulf states including Iran.

S20261027-43.h: Iran watching reports of Ukrainian drone bases near its borders
S20261027-43.s: Iran's foreign minister said armed forces will act decisively against threats to its borders, responding to reports of Ukrainian drone bases nearby and drones in Iraqi Kurdistan.

S20261027-44.h: Pezeshkian in Moscow for gas forum, meeting Putin
S20261027-44.s: Pezeshkian arrived to address the Gas Exporting Countries Forum and meet Putin and Qatar's emir. He called for multilateralism against US unilateralism.

S20261028-01.h: Israel exit polls show deadlock between Netanyahu and Eisenkot blocs
S20261028-01.s: Exit polls after Israel's election put Netanyahu's bloc at about 50-51 seats and Eisenkot's opposition bloc at 52-53, with Arab parties on 17-18. Neither side reaches the 61 seats needed. Likud is the largest single party, and official results are due November 4.
S20261028-01.t: A hung Knesset and a possible end to Netanyahu's rule would reshape Israel's posture on Iran, Gaza and Syria, all of which affect Ankara.

S20261028-02.h: Turkish parliament committee approves Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan
S20261028-02.s: The Foreign Affairs Committee of the Turkish parliament approved the bill ratifying the Mecca Joint Defense Alliance among Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia after a debate. The bill now goes to the full legislature.
S20261028-02.t: Ratification would formally commit Türkiye to a collective defence arrangement with Riyadh and Islamabad while Saudi Arabia is under Houthi fire.

S20261028-03.h: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani security chiefs meet Iranian leaders in Tehran
S20261028-03.s: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye, including MİT chief Kalın, met Iranian leaders in Tehran. This was reportedly the first meeting with all three Mecca Pact members since the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia escalated. Topics included Hormuz, Yemen, Lebanon and US-Iran talks. Iran's SNSC chief Rezaei said regional security must come from within the region, while Gulf News reported the talks faltering.
S20261028-03.t: Türkiye is acting as a direct interlocutor in the Gulf security architecture and a channel between Tehran and its Mecca Pact partners.

S20261028-04.h: Houthis claim missile and drone strikes on Saudi targets including Ras Tanura
S20261028-04.s: The Houthis claimed ballistic missile and drone attacks on Saudi sites, including the Defense Ministry in Riyadh, Abha airport and the Ras Tanura refinery, where they claimed a fire. Riyadh has not confirmed damage. The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh, the Eastern Province and the south, and debris damaged buildings in Riyadh.
S20261028-04.t: The attacks test the Mecca Defence Pact Türkiye is about to ratify and raise questions about its ability to protect the kingdom.
S20261028-04.p: Riyadh and Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia

S20261028-05.h: US warns Gulf allies Iran war could resume; Trump disparages ceasefire
S20261028-05.s: Reports say the US told Gulf states a short, intense war with Iran could follow the midterms. Asharq Al-Awsat says US forces are ready to act within 96 hours of an order. Trump called the summer ceasefire a waste of time, claimed Iran was weeks from a nuclear missile and said a naval blockade has halted Iranian shipping. Al Jazeera reports hints of strikes on civilian infrastructure.
S20261028-05.t: Renewed US-Iran war would hit Türkiye's border region, energy supplies and the Hormuz trade routes just as Ankara is mediating.

S20261028-06.h: Netanyahu reportedly pushed for pre-election Iran strike; army chief resisted
S20261028-06.s: The New York Times reportedly says Netanyahu pushed for an Iran strike before the October 27 vote, but chief of staff Eyal Zamir objected to the timing and urgency. Israeli defence officials say political motives drove the push, and the opposition vowed to block a last-minute strike. Haaretz commentary warns he could try to ignite another war if he loses.
S20261028-06.t: An Israeli-Iranian escalation outside any US framework would spread instability across Türkiye's neighbourhood.

S20261028-07.h: Qatar urges Iran to show goodwill, end Gulf threats and reopen Hormuz
S20261028-07.s: Qatar's foreign ministry said Iran must show good intentions for its US-coordinated mediation to succeed. It also said Saudi-led and Mecca Coalition efforts complement its mediation with Pakistan. Regional powers are demanding that Hormuz reopen, threats to Gulf states stop and nuclear inspections proceed.
S20261028-07.t: Türkiye's own contacts with Tehran run in parallel with Qatari and Saudi mediation, so Ankara's role depends on this coordination.

S20261028-08.h: US orders non-emergency staff out of Saudi Arabia over Houthi threat
S20261028-08.s: The US State Department ordered non-emergency government employees and families to leave Saudi Arabia, citing security threats from Houthi attacks.
S20261028-08.t: A US drawdown signals how seriously Washington takes the Houthi threat as Türkiye prepares to join a Saudi defence pact.

S20261028-09.h: Egypt's parliament approves military support for Saudi Arabia if requested
S20261028-09.s: Egypt's parliament approved military support for Riyadh if requested, as Houthi attacks threaten the kingdom and Red Sea shipping. Kurdistan24 reports the Houthis warned Egypt against backing Riyadh.
S20261028-09.t: Egypt's move adds another regional military alignment around Saudi security alongside the Mecca Pact.

S20261028-10.h: Fighting near Bab el-Mandeb as Yemeni forces advance against Houthis
S20261028-10.s: Yemeni government forces pressed an advance against the Houthis near Bab al-Mandeb and in Taiz, and say they neutralised about 440 fighters. The Houthis claim they repelled a pro-Saudi advance. Houthi attacks have displaced about 270,000 Yemenis in two months.
S20261028-10.t: A ground push near Bab el-Mandeb threatens Red Sea shipping lanes that matter for Turkish trade.

S20261028-11.h: Mojtaba Khamenei sets conditions for ending the war, stresses Hormuz control
S20261028-11.s: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei met SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei after the Tehran talks with Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani envoys. He said ending the war must secure the rights of the Iranian people and stressed managing the Strait of Hormuz. Parliament's speaker said he is healthy and in full control despite heavy losses.
S20261028-11.t: Tehran's hard conditions limit the room for the Turkish and Saudi mediation effort.

S20261028-12.h: Iranian navy says tanker hit mine east of Strait of Hormuz
S20261028-12.s: Iran's navy said an oil tanker struck a naval mine east of the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire after switching off its tracking systems.
S20261028-12.t: Mines and fires in Hormuz raise risks for energy flows on which Türkiye depends.

S20261028-13.h: Iran threatens legal action against South Korean shipper Sinokor over Hormuz
S20261028-13.s: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority said Sinokor vessels will face legal action from November 1 over passage through Hormuz.
S20261028-13.t: Iran asserting legal control of Hormuz traffic sets a precedent for commercial shipping that matters to Türkiye.

S20261028-14.h: IAEA's Grossi presses Iran for access to verify 440 kg of enriched uranium
S20261028-14.s: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi, speaking at the UN Security Council, urged Iran to grant immediate access to nuclear sites to verify its declared 440 kg of highly enriched uranium.
S20261028-14.t: The unverified uranium stockpile is a key trigger for renewed strikes on Iran and thus for regional escalation.

S20261028-15.h: Pentagon data: US has spent over $47 billion on Iran war
S20261028-15.s: Pentagon data obtained by Reuters shows US spending on the Iran war has passed $47 billion, more than 25% above the July estimate. Hegseth is also due to face questions at an ASEAN meeting on US Indo-Pacific commitment amid the strain.
S20261028-15.t: The cost may shape Washington's appetite for a renewed round and its demands on regional partners.

S20261028-16.h: Jordan strikes southern Syria after church attack, killing civilians per Damascus
S20261028-16.s: Jordan says airstrikes in southern Syria killed over 20 ISIS militants and destroyed a weapons depot after a church attack in Jordan. Jordan's interior minister said the attackers were Jordanian nationals with no foreign link. Syria says six to seven civilians, including three children, died in Daraa, and relatives deny links to the attack. The UN called for civilian protection.
S20261028-16.t: Cross-border strikes on Syrian soil test al-Sharaa's government, with which Ankara is closely aligned.

S20261028-17.h: Syria and Jordan move to contain crisis with joint committee and talks
S20261028-17.s: Syria closed the Nasib crossing after the strikes, opened direct talks with Amman and announced it would reopen on Tuesday morning. The two sides agreed a joint security committee to review the strikes and pledged to restore ties. Syria says Jordan did not coordinate with Damascus beforehand.
S20261028-17.t: A rapid Syrian-Jordanian de-escalation preserves stability on Syria's southern front.

S20261028-18.h: Iraqi PM al-Zaidi to visit Damascus for energy and security talks
S20261028-18.s: Iraq's prime minister al-Zaidi will visit Damascus with a senior federal delegation to meet President al-Sharaa. The visit was delayed by security developments in Jordan.
S20261028-18.t: Iraq-Syria energy and security links bear on Türkiye's Iraq Development Road and Kurdish-related security concerns.

S20261028-19.h: Egypt, UAE and Bahrain join Greece and Cyprus against Turkey-Libya maritime deal
S20261028-19.s: Egypt, Bahrain and the UAE joined Greece and Cyprus in a UN statement condemning Türkiye's maritime agreement with Libya as violating international law. Erdoğan said Türkiye is pursuing its own interests, not trying to score against rivals. Euractiv says the deal may push the EU to defend a Greek energy project.
S20261028-19.t: The deal has drawn Arab Gulf and Egyptian states into the Greek-Cypriot camp, widening diplomatic pressure on Ankara in the Eastern Mediterranean.

S20261028-20.h: Ankara denies Aegean policy shift after reported Fidan interview in Greek paper
S20261028-20.s: Türkiye's Foreign Ministry says its Aegean and Eastern Mediterranean policy is unchanged. It rejects claims that Foreign Minister Fidan gave a controversial interview to a Greek newspaper and says it will protect its rights without concession.
S20261028-20.t: Ankara is guarding against any perception of softening toward Athens.

S20261028-21.h: Cypriot leaders to meet ahead of UN envoy Holguin's visit
S20261028-21.s: Christodoulides and Turkish Cypriot leader Erhürman agreed to make no further substantive statements before UN envoy Holguin visits. Christodoulides proposed UN-administered repopulation of Varosha and EU control of Famagusta port.
S20261028-21.t: Proposals on Varosha and Famagusta port touch directly on Turkish positions on the island.

S20261028-22.h: Pezeshkian meets Putin in Moscow at gas forum, urges energy cooperation
S20261028-22.s: Iranian President Pezeshkian met Putin on the sidelines of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum, discussing oil and gas projects and bilateral trade up 10.4%. He said regional states can solve problems without the US, and warned the US blockade and military presence threaten energy markets.
S20261028-22.t: Iran-Russia energy plans, including a gas swap via Azerbaijan, bear on Türkiye's own energy corridors.

S20261028-23.h: Qatar's emir meets Putin and Pezeshkian in Moscow over Hormuz and energy
S20261028-23.s: Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim met Putin and Iran's president in Moscow on the sidelines of the GECF summit. They discussed Hormuz security, de-escalation and energy cooperation. Putin said Russia has sought diplomatic solutions since the conflict began.
S20261028-23.t: Moscow is positioning itself in the Gulf-Iran mediation effort alongside Türkiye.

S20261028-24.h: Israeli Arab parties surge in exit polls, becoming potential kingmakers
S20261028-24.s: Exit polls show Arab parties winning 16-18 seats, nearly double their previous total, on record Arab turnout of about 80%. Netanyahu and Smotrich attacked reliance on Arab parties, while Odeh and Joint List leaders said they cannot be ignored. The opposition must decide whether to work with them.
S20261028-24.t: The rise of Arab parties could alter Israeli coalition options and policy on Gaza and the Palestinians.

S20261028-25.h: Israeli parties jockey over coalition after exit polls leave no majority
S20261028-25.s: Netanyahu claimed a mandate for a right-wing government, while Eisenkot claimed victory and vowed a Zionist government. Lieberman urged Netanyahu's MKs to revolt, a Shas official did not rule out joining Eisenkot, and Bennett and Lapid floated options. Herzog must decide who gets the first chance to form a government. Ben-Gvir attacked Netanyahu over a reported plan to form a government without him.
S20261028-25.t: Who governs Israel will determine its line on Iran, Syria and Türkiye.

S20261028-26.h: Israelis vote in record numbers in first election since 7 October
S20261028-26.s: Turnout reached a record 74.3% by 8 pm, the highest in decades, and the Elections Committee rejected a Likud request to extend voting hours. The vote was widely framed as a referendum on Netanyahu after the Gaza and Iran wars. The Shin Bet warned of foreign influence networks, and an Iran-linked group sent bouquets to polling sites.
S20261028-26.t: The outcome will shape Israel's posture toward Iran, Gaza and Syria, all of which bear on Türkiye.

S20261028-27.h: Finnish and Norwegian leaders hold rare call with Putin on ending Ukraine war
S20261028-27.s: Finland's Stubb and Norway's Støre spoke with Putin for about 90 minutes, the first direct European leader contact in over a year. Putin reportedly told them Russia will not compromise on taking all of Donbas, and agreed to keep direct contacts. Stubb said the call was coordinated with Kyiv and US negotiators, and Zelensky discussed it with them afterwards.
S20261028-27.t: European outreach to Moscow changes the diplomatic field in which Türkiye has long sought a mediating role.

S20261028-28.h: Danish PM criticises Nordic leaders' Putin call, exposing European rift
S20261028-28.s: Denmark's Frederiksen criticised the uncoordinated call, saying she sees no sign Russia wants peace with Europe. Støre responded that Nordic allies had been informed in advance.
S20261028-28.t: Divisions among European allies on engaging Moscow affect NATO cohesion.

S20261028-29.h: Trilateral Ukraine-Russia-US talks tentatively set for Abu Dhabi on November 4
S20261028-29.s: Polish PM Tusk said leader-level trilateral talks are tentatively set for Abu Dhabi on November 4. Kyiv has not confirmed them, though Zelensky expects November talks and wants Europe involved. Putin welcomed resumed talks in the first half of November.
S20261028-29.t: Abu Dhabi rather than Istanbul as the venue shows Türkiye is not hosting the process.

S20261028-30.h: Putin invites Zelensky to Moscow, Kyiv says it needs a leaders' meeting
S20261028-30.s: Kremlin aide Ushakov said Putin invited Zelensky to Moscow and promised his safety, after the Finnish and Norwegian leaders conveyed his interest in talks. Ukrainian FM Sybiha said a Zelensky-Putin meeting is needed on the most sensitive peace issues.
S20261028-30.t: A leaders' meeting would revive the Türkiye-style mediation idea, though the venue Moscow cuts against it.

S20261028-31.h: Local ceasefire takes effect in Oleshky for humanitarian evacuation
S20261028-31.s: A US-backed localised ceasefire began on October 27 in Oleshky, Kherson region, announced by Melania Trump, and runs to November 1. A humanitarian mission has begun and Ukraine's rights commissioner found no violations. The zone was extended beyond the town, though civilians may be taken to Russia first.
S20261028-31.t: A small US-brokered truce shows the format of the peace process, run without Türkiye.

S20261028-32.h: Russia hits Kyiv with ballistic missiles, damaging Southern Bridge
S20261028-32.s: Russian ballistic missiles and drones struck Kyiv, hitting the Southern Bridge, closing it and suspending metro service. At least one person died, and strikes also hit energy infrastructure in eight regions. Kyiv approved alternative Dnipro crossings.
S20261028-32.t: Escalating Russian strikes shape the Black Sea and Ukraine-war environment on Türkiye's northern flank.

S20261028-33.h: Zelensky says Ukraine lacks Patriot missiles; asks E5 for 10% of stocks
S20261028-33.s: Zelensky said Russia fired over 100 ballistic missiles at Kyiv in two weeks, linking the strikes to delays in Patriot and NASAMS deliveries. Ukraine's defence minister asked E5 countries to transfer 10% of their Patriot and IRIS-T stocks.
S20261028-33.t: Allied air-defence shortages raise pressure on NATO members' own stockpiles.

S20261028-34.h: Trump administration weighs lifting sanctions on Russia's RDIF
S20261028-34.s: The New York Times reported, citing an unnamed US official, that Trump is considering lifting sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund, tied to the US-Russia diesel deal. Novak said three tankers of Russian diesel have departed and a fourth will sail, routed to the US.
S20261028-34.t: US-Russia economic normalisation affects Black Sea and energy dynamics around Türkiye.

S20261028-35.h: Romania says Russian-coordinated sabotage network behind fire near defence site
S20261028-35.s: Romanian intelligence says it uncovered a Russian-coordinated sabotage network behind a September fire near a defence facility. President Dan condemned it as part of a hybrid war against European security.
S20261028-35.t: Hybrid attacks on a Black Sea NATO neighbour bear on Türkiye's own regional security.

S20261028-36.h: France and ten European states reportedly plan nuclear-capable jets deployment
S20261028-36.s: France and ten European countries reportedly plan to deploy nuclear-capable French jets in a new deterrence framework aimed at Russia.
S20261028-36.t: A European nuclear deterrence arrangement outside the US umbrella affects NATO's burden-sharing and Türkiye's place in it.

S20261028-37.h: UK-Poland defence pact and E5 ministers pledge Ukraine support against Russia
S20261028-37.s: The UK and Poland signed a defence agreement including joint air-defence missile development. Defence ministers of the UK, Germany, Italy, Poland and France met in Paris on Ukraine support, naming Russia the main threat. The five reaffirmed readiness to give security guarantees after a ceasefire.
S20261028-37.t: European defence-industrial integration is a competitive and cooperative field for Turkish industry.

S20261028-38.h: Black Sea states step up security cooperation after drone attacks on ships
S20261028-38.s: Türkiye, Romania and Bulgaria are deepening Black Sea security cooperation after a surge in drone attacks on commercial vessels near Bulgaria and Romania.
S20261028-38.t: Türkiye is positioned as a core littoral security provider as commercial shipping is attacked.

S20261028-39.h: Hebron offensive displaces thousands as Israel seals West Bank on election day
S20261028-39.s: The Israeli army operation in Hebron entered a fifth day with 4,969 Palestinians displaced, per Anadolu, after an attack on two IDF soldiers. Israeli forces dispersed protests, and the IDF blockaded West Bank cities on Election Day.
S20261028-39.t: Escalation in the West Bank feeds Ankara's criticism of Israel and regional tensions.

S20261028-40.h: Israeli strikes kill six in Gaza despite ceasefire; Hamas hopes for Netanyahu defeat
S20261028-40.s: Israeli strikes killed six Palestinians in Gaza in 24 hours despite the ceasefire. Hamas hopes a Netanyahu defeat would unlock the ceasefire plan, and UN-commissioned experts say Israel continues committing genocide.
S20261028-40.t: Ankara is a Gaza ceasefire guarantor and critic of Israeli policy, so developments there matter.

S20261028-41.h: Police detain dozens in corruption probe of CHP-run Bakırköy and in Denizli
S20261028-41.s: Police detained 56 people, including five deputy mayors, in a corruption probe into the CHP-run Bakırköy municipality, with detention orders issued for 68. Police also detained YENİ Parti Merkezefendi mayor Şeniz Doğan and at least 16 others in Denizli.
S20261028-41.t: The crackdown deepens domestic political polarisation with possible effects on Türkiye's international standing.

S20261028-42.h: CHP splits: mayors join YENİ Parti as party fights Özel leadership ruling
S20261028-42.s: Four Istanbul district mayors resigned from the CHP and joined the new YENİ Parti, which is preparing its founding congress. The CHP is preparing a European Court of Human Rights application against a ruling that removed Özgür Özel from the party leadership.
S20261028-42.t: The fragmentation of the main opposition reshapes the domestic political balance in Türkiye.

S20261028-43.h: Özel rejects sending Turkish troops to Yemen under Mecca pact
S20261028-43.s: Özgür Özel rejected sending Turkish troops to Yemen under the Mecca pact and said his party would challenge the funding law at the Constitutional Court.
S20261028-43.t: Domestic opposition to deployment under the pact could constrain how Ankara implements it.

S20261028-44.h: Türkiye unveils Digital Sovereignty Strategy to cut reliance on foreign technology
S20261028-44.s: The Cyber Security Board was presented a Digital Sovereignty Strategy aimed at strengthening cybersecurity and reducing dependence on foreign technologies in critical areas.
S20261028-44.t: The strategy aims to cut exposure to foreign tech suppliers in critical sectors.

S20261028-45.h: Turkish raids over alleged links to Starlink sabotage in Poland
S20261028-45.s: Turkish authorities detained dozens in raids across Türkiye over alleged links to the sabotage of Starlink in Poland, after two suspects were arrested there.
S20261028-45.t: The case shows Turkish-European security cooperation on sabotage and a Turkish-linked network.

S20261028-46.h: PKK withdrawal raises questions over Turkish bases in Iraq; KRG courts Ankara
S20261028-46.s: Analysis says the PKK's October withdrawal from Türkiye and border areas of Iraqi Kurdistan raises questions about Turkish bases in Iraq. KRG PM Masrour Barzani pledged expanded trade with Türkiye and the Development Road, and discussed forming a new cabinet with Türkiye's ambassador.
S20261028-46.t: The process to end PKK violence may shift Türkiye's military footprint in northern Iraq and its economic ties with the KRG.

S20261028-47.h: US gives Iraq until June 2027 to disarm armed groups or face sanctions
S20261028-47.s: The US gave Iraq until June 2027 to disarm armed groups or face sanctions, a deadline an Iraqi analyst says could bring severe penalties. Separately, Iraq's prime minister dismissed Shatri as intelligence head.
S20261028-47.t: Pressure on Iraqi militias bears on Türkiye's security interests in Iraq.

S20261028-48.h: British men charged over alleged Iranian plot at RAF Fairford
S20261028-48.s: Two British men were charged under the National Security Act over an incident at RAF Fairford, a base used by US bombers against Iran. One is accused of aiding Iranian intelligence, and a prosecutor said they helped plan attacks on Iran International journalists.
S20261028-48.t: It shows Iranian intelligence reach inside NATO states during the war.

S20261028-49.h: Kuwait sentences three to death for Iran and Hezbollah assassination plot
S20261028-49.s: A Kuwaiti court sentenced three people to death for collaborating with Iran and Hezbollah in a plot to assassinate senior officials, including the interior minister.
S20261028-49.t: Iranian networks targeting Gulf states form part of the threat environment shaping the Mecca Pact.

S20261029-01.h: Iran rejects Qatari draft deal as it weighs seven-day Hormuz reopening plan
S20261029-01.s: Qatari mediators gave Tehran a new draft to end the war with the US and Israel, with about seven days to address US concerns. A senior Iranian official called it unacceptable, while Araghchi says Iran is in close contact with mediators on a seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz. Iran's response is expected by the end of the week and its forces say they are ready to defend the country.
S20261029-01.t: A collapse of the talks would revive war risk and Hormuz disruption on Türkiye's border and energy routes.

S20261029-02.h: US reportedly warns Gulf states of short, intense strike on Iran after midterms
S20261029-02.s: The WSJ reports Washington told Gulf states to prepare for a brief but intense campaign against Iran after the 3 November midterms. Forces are being repositioned and a Patriot system is reportedly moving to Israel, and Trump said a post-election attack is possible. The UN said diplomacy, not military action, is needed.
S20261029-02.t: Renewed US-Israeli strikes on Iran would hit Türkiye's neighbourhood with refugee, energy and security fallout.

S20261029-03.h: Mediators propose IAEA inspectors' return and Iran-US meeting in Türkiye before November 4
S20261029-03.s: Qatar-led mediators, backed by Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Egypt, are pushing a package to restart US-Iran talks and prevent renewed war. It reportedly includes UN inspectors returning to Iranian nuclear sites in exchange for sanctions relief. Gulf states are also drafting a wider deal covering Hormuz, sanctions and a Houthi withdrawal in Yemen.
S20261029-03.t: Türkiye could host a US-Iran meeting, raising its mediation profile.

S20261029-04.h: Vance writes to Iran's security chief; Trump denies tasking him with talks
S20261029-04.s: Vance sent a letter to Iran's security chief saying negotiations must cover the nuclear issue, the highest-level US outreach in months. Reports say it was at Trump's direction. Trump denied tasking Vance with restarting talks, saying Vance only helped secure medical supplies for Iran.

S20261029-05.h: Iran's supreme leader orders end to 'neither war nor peace' state
S20261029-05.s: Iran's supreme leader reportedly ordered an end to the 'neither war nor peace' situation, though Tehran's demands toward Washington are unchanged. President Pezeshkian pledged to implement the directive.

S20261029-06.h: Netanyahu and Katz signal possible renewed strike on Iran as vote count continues
S20261029-06.s: During the vote count Defence Minister Katz sent a message of possible attack on Iran. Netanyahu said he could work with Trump to eliminate the Iran threat and warned against distractions. Iran warned any Israeli-led attack would devastate global markets, and analysts say he may use renewed war to push for a unity government.

S20261029-07.h: Iran, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye meet in Tehran on regional security
S20261029-07.s: The four countries agreed to continue consultations and that regional security requires no foreign military presence. Araghchi briefed the cabinet on the meeting. Egypt separately stressed coordination within a four-way mechanism with Türkiye and Pakistan in calls with Saudi and Emirati counterparts.
S20261029-07.t: Türkiye is a full member of an emerging regional security format with Iran, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

S20261029-08.h: Erdoğan tells Trump Türkiye seeks diplomatic fix for Hormuz and Yemen crises
S20261029-08.s: In a phone call Erdoğan said Türkiye is pursuing diplomacy on Hormuz and Yemen, and that the Mecca Joint Defence Alliance is monitoring both. The call also covered bilateral ties and Ukraine.
S20261029-08.t: Ankara is positioning itself as a mediator and security partner of Gulf states under the Mecca pact.

S20261029-09.h: Türkiye, Bulgaria and Romania warn against Black Sea ship attacks
