S20261029-09.s: After a Sofia meeting, Guler urged Russia and Ukraine to halt attacks on commercial ships following sea-drone strikes on a ship off Bulgaria. Türkiye reserves legal rights over strikes on Turkish-linked vessels. The three defence ministers stressed Montreux compliance and their capacity to secure the Black Sea, and Ankara will keep restricting warship passage.
S20261029-09.t: Ankara asserts its role as Black Sea guardian under Montreux and threatens legal steps over Turkish-linked ships.

S20261029-10.h: US blockade of Iranian ports keeps Hormuz risk 'severe'; oil and gas prices climb
S20261029-10.s: UKMTO rates the regional threat level 'severe' as the US enforces a blockade of Iranian ports. The US military rejected Iranian claims of a mine strike and says transit lanes are clear. Oil rose on Houthi strikes and war threats, European gas topped €100/MWh, and a tanker spill reached UAE beaches.
S20261029-10.t: Higher energy prices and shipping risk hit Türkiye's import bill.

S20261029-11.h: Pentagon: Iran war cost tops $47 billion, over 25% above July estimate
S20261029-11.s: Pentagon data obtained by Reuters show costs above $47 billion, with more than $29 billion going to replace munitions. CENTCOM's figure excludes base repairs.

S20261029-12.h: Houthis strike Aden airport twice with ballistic missiles after evacuation warning
S20261029-12.s: The Houthis told people to evacuate Aden airport, alleging a Saudi military cargo plane carrying weapons was there. Yemen's government says the airport was hit twice within hours, and a missile landed at Al-Nasr camp. The Yemeni army claimed heavy Houthi losses.

S20261029-13.h: Houthi missiles aimed at Taif and eastern Saudi Arabia intercepted
S20261029-13.s: The coalition intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles launched toward Taif and eastern Saudi Arabia. Houthis claimed multiple targets, China urged dialogue, and Saudi Arabia and Kuwait called for a firm international stance.

S20261029-14.h: Russian satellites reportedly helped Houthis target Saudi energy and military sites
S20261029-14.s: An AP report and a geospatial firm found Russian satellites converged over about 40 Saudi targets days before Houthi and Iraqi militia strikes between July and October.

S20261029-15.h: Kuwait summons Iran's ambassador over alleged plot against interior minister
S20261029-15.s: Kuwait summoned Iran's ambassador after the Iranian embassy rejected allegations that an Iranian citizen took part in a plot against Kuwait's interior minister.

S20261029-16.h: Oman and UAE push restraint and a Gulf-Iran security pact; analysts sceptical
S20261029-16.s: Oman called for an economic and security pact between Iran and Gulf states. UAE's Gargash said wars only lead to more crises, while analysts doubt GCC diplomacy with Iran will produce a lasting pact.

S20261029-17.h: Israel's election ends in deadlock; Netanyahu's bloc short of 61 seats
S20261029-17.s: With nearly all votes counted, Netanyahu's bloc has roughly 53 to 55 seats and Eisenkot's about 48 to 50, with neither near a majority. Record turnout was the highest since 1999. Absentee and soldier ballots could shift the outcome, with final results due Thursday.
S20261029-17.t: A weakened or caretaker Netanyahu affects Israeli policy on Syria, Iran and Gaza that Ankara tracks.

S20261029-18.h: Arab parties emerge as kingmakers after record turnout in Israeli election
S20261029-18.s: Arab parties won about 19 seats. The Joint List offered to work with Eisenkot's bloc to oust Netanyahu, and Ra'am's Mansour Abbas signalled willingness to join a government. Opposition parties disagree on relying on them, and hundreds protested for a Jewish-Arab government.

S20261029-19.h: Herzog to decide who forms government; scenarios include unity deal or new vote
S20261029-19.s: President Herzog urged leaders to avoid another election and will consult factions, then give a candidate 28 days. Channel 14 reported a rotation deal under which Netanyahu would serve two years before Eisenkot, which the president's office denied. BBC analysis sees new elections as the most likely outcome.

S20261029-20.h: Trump claims credit for Netanyahu's showing, opposes Ben-Gvir and Smotrich in government
S20261029-20.s: Trump said his endorsement lifted Netanyahu and that he would look at helping form a unity government. US sources say he opposes Ben-Gvir and Smotrich joining, wanting a government that advances his goals in Gaza, Syria and Lebanon. Smotrich pledged settlement expansion and no withdrawals from Lebanon and Syria.
S20261029-20.t: A Netanyahu-led or caretaker government shapes Israeli posture toward Syria, where Türkiye is also active.

S20261029-21.h: Likud accuses Arab parties of stealing the election and files complaints
S20261029-21.s: Likud said it will submit hundreds of testimonies to police, Shin Bet and the Central Elections Committee alleging the election was stolen by Arab parties after they reached record seats.

S20261029-22.h: Attacker killed outside Israeli embassy in Belgrade; Serbia raises terror alert
S20261029-22.s: Serbian police shot dead a teenage knife attacker who assaulted a guard outside the Israeli embassy. Serbia said he was an ISIS supporter and raised its terror threat level to maximum.

S20261029-23.h: Syria and Jordan form joint security committee after deadly Jordanian air strikes in Daraa
S20261029-23.s: Jordanian air strikes in southern Syria killed at least seven people, including children, and Damascus summoned Jordan's ambassador. The two states agreed to a joint probe and security committee and reopened a border crossing, and Amman expressed regret over civilian deaths.

S20261029-24.h: Iraqi PM al-Zaidi visits Damascus, meets al-Sharaa on oil pipeline and security
S20261029-24.s: On the first such visit since Assad's fall, Iraqi PM Ali al-Zaidi discussed trade and reviving the Baniyas oil pipeline with Ahmed al-Sharaa. Sharaa backed Iraq's efforts to place weapons under state control.
S20261029-24.t: Reviving the Baniyas pipeline and Iraq-Syria ties affects regional energy routes that Türkiye also eyes.

S20261029-25.h: French fighter killed in Idlib clash with Syrian security forces
S20261029-25.s: A French national was killed and a Syrian civilian injured when an Internal Security Forces patrol clashed with an armed group near a camp housing French fighters. The Syrian government confirmed a French extremist died in a shootout.

S20261029-26.h: Israeli forces raid Quneitra village, detain five residents
S20261029-26.s: Israeli forces entered al-Muallaqa in southern Quneitra with seven vehicles, searched homes and detained five residents.
S20261029-26.t: Israeli activity in southern Syria bears on Türkiye's Syria policy.

S20261029-27.h: Türkiye hosts Libya east-west reunification talks; no deal yet
S20261029-27.s: A senior Turkish official confirmed Türkiye hosted talks between Libya's eastern and western administrations last week, focused on military unification. No agreement emerged.
S20261029-27.t: Türkiye strengthens its role as broker in Libya, where it has military and maritime interests.

S20261029-28.h: Ankara ready to sign maritime delimitation deal with Egypt, rivalling Greece's
S20261029-28.s: Türkiye's defence ministry said it is ready to sign a maritime jurisdiction deal with Egypt, claiming Cairo would gain over 15,000 km² more than under Greece's deal. It welcomed Libya's House of Representatives ratifying the maritime memorandum.
S20261029-28.t: Ankara is courting Egypt to counter Greek and Cypriot Eastern Mediterranean claims.

S20261029-29.h: Kremlin: Abu Dhabi talks with US and Ukraine after Nov 4, Europe not invited
S20261029-29.s: The Kremlin says trilateral talks will proceed after 4 November without European representatives, though dates are not set. Zelensky expects a meeting on 6 to 10 November covering energy, a maritime ceasefire, prisoner swaps and security guarantees. Trump says a Putin-Zelensky summit could come soon.
S20261029-29.t: Türkiye has sought to host Ukraine talks; Abu Dhabi as venue sidelines Ankara.

S20261029-30.h: US-Russia economic package and diesel deal raise sanctions-relief fears
S20261029-30.s: US and Russia are reportedly discussing a package covering energy, pipelines and nuclear cooperation, and Washington is weighing lifting sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund. Critics say the diesel deal gives Moscow cash. The EU ruled out resuming Russian gas and fears broader contacts.

S20261029-31.h: US proposes demilitarized zones in Donbas and Kinburn Spit; Kyiv shifts on guarantees
S20261029-31.s: Zelensky said the US proposed demilitarized and buffer zones in Donbas and the Kinburn Spit within peace talks. The FT reports Kyiv is shifting its stance on security guarantees, fearing a full US withdrawal.

S20261029-32.h: Possible Putin-Trump-Xi summit unconfirmed; Zelensky fears Yalta-style deal
S20261029-32.s: The Kremlin says no final agreement exists on a Putin-Trump-Xi meeting on the APEC sidelines. Zelensky warned of a superpower division of influence and opposes closer Russia-US economic ties.

S20261029-33.h: Finland and Norway leaders call Putin, drawing European criticism
S20261029-33.s: Finland's and Norway's leaders held a rare call with Putin to influence the Abu Dhabi talks. The FT says Putin spoke mostly about Slavic history. The EU called for a united message, and Moscow hopes to keep contact with Helsinki and Oslo.

S20261029-34.h: UK pledges £10bn and Netherlands €500m in military aid for Ukraine
S20261029-34.s: Britain will provide £10 billion over three years including £3 billion for arms exports. The Netherlands announced €500 million in military aid plus €1.2 billion in non-military aid, and a joint air defence project.

S20261029-35.h: Ukraine gets only 12 Patriot missiles a month against need of 150
S20261029-35.s: Zelensky said the US supplies about 12 Patriot interceptors a month in 2026 against roughly 150 needed, citing Middle East demand, and he is seeking more from allies. A temporary Starshield restriction also halted 2,000 interceptor drones.

S20261029-36.h: Ukraine strikes Russian air defences and plants; Russia builds new Geran launch site
S20261029-36.s: Ukraine's General Staff reported hits on three Russian air defence elements and a Donetsk depot, and drones hit the Azot plant in Novomoskovsk. Ukrainian intelligence says a new Geran site near Millerovo can launch 100 drones daily. Russian refineries have raised throughput about 25% since refinery strikes paused.

S20261029-37.h: Dozens of drones downed over Moscow region; flights restricted
S20261029-37.s: Nearly 60 drones were reportedly shot down over Moscow Oblast in 90 minutes, with flights restricted at three of four main airports. The mayor reported 15 more downed.

S20261029-38.h: Russia hits Ukraine with ballistic missile and 88 drones amid Oleshky local ceasefire
S20261029-38.s: Russia launched 88 Shahed-type drones and an Iskander-M/S-400 missile overnight. Meanwhile a local ceasefire holds in Oleshky, with demining and evacuation planning for residents.

S20261029-39.h: Israel keeps striking Lebanon despite ceasefire; Aoun says US mediation yields nothing
S20261029-39.s: Israeli forces continued artillery strikes on southern Lebanese villages. Lebanese President Aoun said Israeli attacks obstruct an agreement, and Hezbollah's Qassem demanded Israeli troops leave. Lebanon's judiciary named seven suspects in a Hezbollah explosives case.

S20261029-40.h: Gaza strikes continue under ceasefire; Hebron siege enters sixth day
S20261029-40.s: Israeli strikes killed several Palestinians in Gaza despite the ceasefire. A lockdown of Hebron drew UN concern about ethnic cleansing, and settlers attacked foreign journalists. The WFP called hunger in Gaza unacceptable.

S20261029-41.h: Turkish peace process stalls as PKK members surrender and Speaker warns of hidden motives
S20261029-41.s: Turkish defence ministry says two more PKK members surrendered last week. Analysts assess why the process has gone quiet, and Speaker Kurtulmuş warned against seeking political gain from it. The KRG rejected Baghdad's 2027 budget draft, and the PUK reportedly discussed a similar process with Iran's Kurdish opponents.
S20261029-41.t: The Terror-Free Türkiye process faces delays that could affect Ankara's domestic and Iraqi Kurdish strategy.

S20261029-42.h: Ankara hosts Turkic states summit as Erdoğan meets Kazakhstan's Tokayev
S20261029-42.s: Erdoğan held talks with Tokayev ahead of the 13th Organization of Turkic States summit on 29-30 October. Türkiye and Kazakhstan agreed to deepen defence industry and Middle Corridor cooperation. Reports say Aliyev's attendance was in doubt over a row with an Erdoğan adviser.
S20261029-42.t: The summit advances Ankara's Turkic-world agenda, defence exports and Middle Corridor logistics.

S20261029-43.h: Putin hosts Pezeshkian, promises Russian support for Bushehr and reactors
S20261029-43.s: Putin told Pezeshkian Russia will honour joint projects including Bushehr. Rosatom is raising Bushehr staff to 200 in November after cutting it from 700 to 20, and a small modular reactor protocol is due to be signed.

S20261029-44.h: IRGC-linked media push NPT withdrawal as IAEA sees no repair of nuclear sites
S20261029-44.s: Tasnim argued Iran should leave the NPT and Fars promoted calls for a bomb. Grossi said there are no signs Iran has tried to repair facilities damaged in US strikes.

S20261029-45.h: EU Israel sanctions talks frozen until new government forms
S20261029-45.s: EUobserver reports EU discussions on sanctions against Israel are on hold until a new Israeli government is formed, amid concerns about Netanyahu's election support.

S20261030-01.h: US weighs renewed Iran strikes after midterms as aircraft reach Israel
S20261030-01.s: Reports say CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper briefed Trump on options for resuming attacks on Iran. Ten US military aircraft reportedly landed at Israel's Ovda and Nevatim bases, and Washington has warned Gulf allies to prepare for Iranian retaliation against energy and infrastructure. Reports describe a short, intense campaign of about a week after the 3 November midterms, with Israel reportedly seeking US permission to hit Iranian energy sites.
S20261030-01.t: A resumed US-Israel air campaign on Iran would threaten Türkiye's southern neighbourhood with energy shocks, refugee and security spillover.

S20261030-02.h: Vance letter to Iran's Rezaei offers to restart talks; Tehran yet to reply
S20261030-02.s: Reports say VP JD Vance wrote to Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei after Qatari-mediated contacts. A senior Iranian source confirmed receipt but said there has been no response. Trump confirmed the outreach and said Washington is weighing a week-long campaign after the midterms, while also describing the letter as about medical supplies.
S20261030-02.t: A US-Iran diplomatic track, with Qatar mediating, would reduce the risk of a regional war on Türkiye's border.

S20261030-03.h: Mediators struggle to bridge US-Iran gap as Tehran rejects Qatari draft
S20261030-03.s: A US envoy said a deal is 'very close' and credited Qatar and Pakistan. A senior Iranian official said Qatar's latest draft contained only unacceptable ideas, and Iranian leaders insisted talks can progress only on Iran's conditions. Saudis reportedly asked Trump to try diplomacy first and asked Tehran to spare key oil facilities.
S20261030-03.t: Prolonged deadlock raises the odds of renewed war and prolonged Hormuz disruption that hits Türkiye's energy costs.

S20261030-04.h: Tankers hit mines in Hormuz; IRGC blames use of unauthorised routes
S20261030-04.s: The IRGC Navy said three tankers hit mines within 24 hours after switching off navigation systems and using a prohibited route. UKMTO reported fires on vessels off Khasab, Oman. Iran closed the strait to uncoordinated transits and challenged CENTCOM's claim that US forces had cleared the mines.
S20261030-04.t: Hormuz disruption pushes up energy prices and trade costs for Türkiye.

S20261030-05.h: Iran claims downing of US MQ-1 drone and capture of another near Hormuz
S20261030-05.s: The IRGC and Iran's army said they shot down a US MQ-1 drone east of Hormuz off Sirik. The IRGC Navy also said it captured a US reconnaissance and decoy drone intact. Iranian media also reported interceptions of hostile aircraft near Qeshm and Kish.

S20261030-06.h: Houthis fire missiles at Saudi cities and oil sites; Saudi air defences respond
S20261030-06.s: Houthis claimed six attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities, which Riyadh has not confirmed. The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed several ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh and the Eastern Region, and civil defence alerts sounded in Riyadh, Al-Kharj and Najran. A Saudi citizen was injured by debris.
S20261030-06.t: Escalation against Saudi Arabia tests the new Mecca pact and Gulf stability that matter to Ankara's regional diplomacy.

S20261030-07.h: Israeli election leaves no bloc with majority; coalition talks begin
S20261030-07.s: The final count gave Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats and the opposition 48, with Likud the largest party. Neither side reaches 61 without Arab parties, which won a record 19 seats. Gadi Eisenkot is expected to get the president's mandate, though most of his bloc's parties reject reliance on Arab parties.
S20261030-07.t: Netanyahu's weakened position shapes Israeli policy on Gaza, Syria and Iran that Ankara is contesting.

S20261030-08.h: Netanyahu and Likud allege Arab-party election fraud; police and Shin Bet push back
S20261030-08.s: Netanyahu accused Arab parties of foreign-backed election theft after his coalition lost its majority. Eisenkot accused him of an organised campaign to delegitimise the result. A senior police official and Shin Bet said fraud complaints were fewer than in past elections and the probe does not implicate a group of voters.

S20261030-09.h: Israel probes alleged Qatari and Turkish election funding; Doha and Ankara deny
S20261030-09.s: Israel's Central Elections Committee asked Shin Bet to investigate suspected Qatari and Turkish funding to lift Arab turnout. Qatar called the claims disinformation and Türkiye's Communications Directorate rejected them as a deliberate disinformation campaign. Ben-Gvir called for arrests of Arab party leaders, and Haaretz said initial suspicions were narrower than publicly presented.
S20261030-09.t: Israeli accusations of Turkish interference add a new strand to Ankara-Israel hostility.

S20261030-10.h: Israeli election seen raising prospect of attack on Iran; Iran meddling alleged
S20261030-10.s: The National reads the Israeli results as raising the prospect of a new Israeli attack on Iran, and Ahmad Tibi claims Netanyahu plans war on Iran after the US midterms. Iranian analysts say a weakened Netanyahu is unlikely to change Israel's Iran policy. Reports also allege Iranian cyber and recruitment efforts aimed at Israel's election and the US midterms.

S20261030-11.h: Libya's parliament approves Türkiye maritime deal; Greece calls it void
S20261030-11.s: Libya's House of Representatives approved the long-dormant maritime memorandum with Türkiye, with backing from former adversaries. Greek PM Mitsotakis called the deal null and void. Türkiye also renewed its offer to Egypt for a maritime boundaries agreement.
S20261030-11.t: Eastern Libyan ratification consolidates Türkiye's Eastern Mediterranean maritime claims against Greece and Cyprus.

S20261030-12.h: Naval drones sink Greek container ship off Bulgaria in Black Sea
S20261030-12.s: A Greek container ship, reportedly ZIM-chartered, sank after drone strikes off Bulgaria, the latest in a series of attacks on ships in the western Black Sea. Ukraine blames Russia, which denies involvement, and Bulgaria's defence chief said the drones came from the east. Mitsotakis urged a global maritime truce and NATO's Black Sea states voiced concern.
S20261030-12.t: Türkiye, as the Black Sea gatekeeper, faces rising risk to commercial shipping and spillover near NATO waters.

S20261030-13.h: Trump calls Erdoğan during Turkic summit; Erdoğan offers help on Ukraine-Russia talks
S20261030-13.s: Trump phoned Erdoğan at the Republic Day dinner for Turkic leaders and wished the Organization of Turkic States summit success. Erdoğan said Türkiye is ready to help restore Ukraine-Russia talks. US Ambassador Barrack said the Turkic partnership is central to both leaders' vision.
S20261030-13.t: The call signals Washington's backing for Ankara's Turkic outreach and a mediation role on Ukraine.

S20261030-14.h: Ankara hosts 13th Organization of Turkic States summit; Aliyev sends FM instead
S20261030-14.s: Foreign ministers met under Hakan Fidan ahead of the 29-30 October summit. Erdoğan spoke of Turkic unity and a 'Century of Türkiye', and Kyrgyz President Japarov received a Turkic World order. Aliyev skipped the summit and sent Foreign Minister Bayramov amid tensions over Türkiye's criticism of headscarf restrictions.
S20261030-14.t: The summit showcases Ankara's Turkic leadership, but Azerbaijan's low-level attendance exposes friction with a key partner.

S20261030-15.h: Türkiye and Uzbekistan sign five agreements including defence
S20261030-15.s: Erdoğan and Mirziyoyev signed five bilateral agreements covering trade, investment, mining, transport, social security and defence. Türkiye aims to lift trade from $3.1 billion in 2025 to $5 billion, and a customs data protocol was also signed.
S20261030-15.t: Deepens economic and defence ties in Central Asia.

S20261030-16.h: Senior PKK figure says peace process with Türkiye is frozen
S20261030-16.s: A senior PKK figure said the process is frozen, blaming the government for insufficient political and legal steps. A Kurdish community group in Germany separately said Türkiye is barring Kurdish visitors from returning to Germany.
S20261030-16.t: A stall in the process to end PKK violence threatens the government's flagship domestic-security initiative.

S20261030-17.h: Fidan to attend G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta
S20261030-17.s: Hakan Fidan will attend the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta on 30-31 October to discuss regional crises and energy security. He is expected to press for more international pressure on Israel.
S20261030-17.t: A chance for Ankara to engage Washington directly and push its line on Israel and regional crises.

S20261030-18.h: Russian drone strike on Dnipro train station kills at least 14
S20261030-18.s: A Russian jet-powered drone hit a train at Dnipro's main station despite an air raid alert, killing 13-14 people and wounding more. Dnipro declared a day of mourning. The EU and UN condemned the strike and EU leaders pledged continued support to Ukraine.

S20261030-19.h: Russian strikes hit Kremenchuk, Chernihiv and Kyiv; Zelensky warns of more ballistic attacks
S20261030-19.s: Russian attacks killed people in Kremenchuk and Chernihiv, including two teenage girls, and injured dozens. Ballistic missiles hit Kyiv overnight, and Russia launched 112 drones. Zelensky said intelligence indicates new ballistic strikes are planned and called for air defence support.

S20261030-20.h: Temporary Oleshky ceasefire holds as humanitarian convoy prepares to enter
S20261030-20.s: Russia and Ukraine have observed a halt to hostilities around occupied Oleshky since 27 October, and sappers have cleared routes. A Ukraine-US-Russia delegation reached the aid hub ahead of the planned delivery, with residents allowed to leave. Zelensky said Russia was still striking civilians elsewhere.

S20261030-21.h: Ukraine peace diplomacy: Abu Dhabi trilateral talks, Zelensky offers territory discussion
S20261030-21.s: Ukraine's foreign minister said Zelensky told Putin he is ready to discuss territory in person. Kyiv lowered expectations for the 4 November Abu Dhabi talks, hoping for an energy truce. Ushakov said the battlefield will determine when talks begin and ruled out Europe in Abu Dhabi, while Peskov said the war 'must continue'.
S20261030-21.t: Türkiye's offer to help restore talks competes with the Abu Dhabi track.

S20261030-22.h: Ukraine launches huge drone raid on Moscow and Russian regions
S20261030-22.s: Russia's Defence Ministry said it destroyed 1,214 Ukrainian drones across 19 regions, and Moscow's mayor said 613 flew toward the Moscow region. Three airports restricted flights and debris fell at a Sterlitamak chemical site. A separate strike on the Taman substation caused power outages across occupied Crimea.

S20261030-23.h: Ukrainian Neptune missiles destroy two Russian Su-34 jets at Marinovka airfield
S20261030-23.s: Ukraine's Navy said Neptune missiles destroyed two Su-34 bombers at Marinovka airfield in Volgograd Oblast. Zelensky also cited a hit on an Iskander launcher, and intelligence puts Su-34 losses at 43.

S20261030-24.h: Putin says Russia ready for war with Europe but does not want one
S20261030-24.s: After calls with Finnish and Norwegian leaders, Putin said there would be no winners in a Russia-Europe war and that Moscow wants to avoid a Hormuz-style crisis in the Baltic. Denmark and Sweden publicly rebuked the Finland-Norway call.

S20261030-25.h: NATO pushes Patriot interceptors for Ukraine as US delays PAC-3 deliveries
S20261030-25.s: NATO's deputy secretary general urged allies to transfer PAC-2 and PAC-3 interceptors from stockpiles to Ukraine. Partners fear the White House will not approve interceptors before the US congressional vote. PAC-3 deliveries are reportedly delayed while PAC-2s arrive through PURL.

S20261030-26.h: European Commission opens over €20 billion in defence funds, urges joint procurement
S20261030-26.s: The Commission invited member states to use about $23.7 billion in defence funds and apply for SAFE loans for joint procurement and Ukraine support.
S20261030-26.t: EU defence funding rules and procurement preference shape Türkiye's access to European defence markets.

S20261030-27.h: Israel tightens siege of Hebron as thousands displaced
S20261030-27.s: Israeli forces have besieged and raided Hebron for a seventh day, with demolitions and over 3,300 people forced from their homes. The IDF may scale back its presence after evacuating thousands, with Netanyahu possibly more flexible after the election.

S20261030-28.h: Israeli strikes in Gaza continue despite ceasefire
S20261030-28.s: Israeli strikes killed several Palestinians, including at an Economy Ministry post in al-Mawasi, and damaged a UN warehouse. Over 21,000 patients await evacuation for treatment.
S20261030-28.t: Türkiye is positioning itself as Gaza aid provider and critic of Israeli ceasefire violations.

S20261030-29.h: SDF-Damascus integration advances amid Afrin return disputes and US oil takeover
S20261030-29.s: Syrian officials agreed final steps to merge Kobani and Rojava universities. Ilham Ahmed said armed groups in Afrin hinder displaced residents' return. US firm HKN plans to double output at northeastern fields taken from Kurdish-run operations, and UN rights chief Türk pledged minority protection support.
S20261030-29.t: The pace and terms of SDF integration affect Ankara's security demands and the PKK process.

S20261030-30.h: Iraqi PM visits Damascus in first such trip since Assad's fall
S20261030-30.s: Iraqi PM Ali Al-Zaidi met Syrian President Ahmed Al-Sharaa, drawing domestic praise and criticism. Separately, Damascus and Amman gave contradictory accounts of an attack in southern Syria that killed a family.
S20261030-30.t: Iraq-Syria rapprochement shifts regional alignments around Türkiye's neighbours.

S20261030-31.h: Pentagon fires Joint Staff planner Sylvia amid Iran war preparations
S20261030-31.s: Hegseth fired Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia, head of strategy and plans on the Joint Staff, reportedly over leaks on Iran and Ukraine, as Trump appears poised to resume large strikes.

S20261030-32.h: Iran war costs US $47bn as Pentagon eyes $400bn budget cut
S20261030-32.s: The Pentagon says the Iran war has cost $47bn, days before the midterms. It is also reportedly preparing a $400bn cut to the requested defence budget, which could slow restocking.

S20261030-33.h: Reuters: Iran imported $2bn in military supplies despite US blockade
S20261030-33.s: Iran reportedly imported at least $2bn in military supplies since January 2025 through a network of more than 5,000 agencies, despite the US naval blockade.

S20261030-34.h: Iran repression: executions after January protests, arrests of alleged US-Israel cells
S20261030-34.s: A UN rapporteur reported at least 34 executions over January protests and thousands detained. Iran separately arrested 16 people it links to US- and Israel-linked cells, and a protester was sentenced to death twice.

S20261030-35.h: Hormuz disruption forces energy scramble: QatarEnergy buys LNG, EU releases oil
S20261030-35.s: QatarEnergy plans overseas LNG purchases and signed a deal with Woodside as force majeure on Hormuz shipping continues. EU states pledged to release 42.6 million barrels of oil, and EU energy prices are at four-year highs.
S20261030-35.t: Higher energy prices and supply disruption weigh on Türkiye's import bill and its role as a transit corridor.

S20261030-36.h: Yemen fighting: heavy casualties, strikes on Houthis and toxic-shell allegations
S20261030-36.s: WHO says Yemen fighting has killed nearly 1,700 since August. Intensive strikes targeted the Houthis amid suspicions of toxic shells in Taiz, and the Yemeni army claimed 324 Houthis neutralised in 24 hours.

S20261030-37.h: Abu Dhabi court jails eight for life over arms to Sudan's army
S20261030-37.s: A UAE court sentenced eight people, including Sudanese army figures Yasser Al Atta and Salah Gosh, to life imprisonment over arms supplies to the Sudanese Army, amid Khartoum-Abu Dhabi tensions.

S20261030-38.h: Lagarde to leave ECB early as bank holds rates
S20261030-38.s: Christine Lagarde is resigning effective 7 February, nine months early, opening a succession contest. The ECB held rates despite inflation driven by an energy crisis, and Lagarde signalled a December hike is possible.

S20261030-39.h: Italian EUFOR helicopter crashes in Bosnia, killing at least three
S20261030-39.s: An EUFOR helicopter crashed in Brcko during an EU mission, with reports of three or four dead and injured.

S20261030-40.h: UN envoy Holguin starts new Cyprus talks round
S20261030-40.s: Maria Angela Holguin will meet Christodoulides on Friday and Turkish Cypriot leader Erhürman on Monday ahead of a tripartite meeting on 9 November.
S20261030-40.t: Progress on Cyprus interacts with Ankara's maritime dispute with Greece and the Libya deal.

S20261030-41.h: Türkiye speeds $10bn railway plan for China-Europe freight corridor
S20261030-41.s: Türkiye is accelerating about $10 billion in rail projects to create a China-Europe freight corridor by 2031, per Nikkei Asia.
S20261030-41.t: Positions Türkiye as a Middle Corridor transit hub.

S20261030-42.h: Sinan Ülgen weighs Mecca Alliance benefits and defence risks for Türkiye
S20261030-42.s: Analyst Sinan Ülgen assessed the Mecca Alliance agreement, its benefits for Türkiye and the risks of its mutual defence obligations.
S20261030-42.t: The pact's mutual defence clauses could draw Türkiye into Gulf and Iran-related confrontations.

S20261030-43.h: Russian hybrid threats on NATO flank: sabotage claims, bunkers, conscription
S20261030-43.s: Reports allege a Russian sabotage and assassination campaign in Europe, with fears of escalation through drone incursions. Estonia plans about 150 border bunkers, Lithuania will introduce conscription for men aged 18-22 from 2032, and NATO reconnaissance flew near Kaliningrad.

S20261030-44.h: Ukraine reports record Russian losses in October
S20261030-44.s: Ukraine's General Staff said Russia lost 49,040 troops in October, the highest monthly figure of the full-scale war, and reported strikes on drone and fuel sites in Bryansk.

S20261030-45.h: Trump administration pushes US firms to take Russian diesel shipments
S20261030-45.s: Seven tankers with about 288,000 tonnes of Russian diesel are sailing to the US under a Trump-Putin deal amid a legal dispute. The administration is privately pressing companies to accept deliveries despite legal risks.

S20261030-46.h: Hezbollah's Qassem says Iran prioritises ending Israeli attacks on Lebanon
S20261030-46.s: Naim Qassem said Iran puts ending Israeli attacks and securing Israeli withdrawal first. The Israeli army fired an interceptor at a suspected aerial target in southern Lebanon amid airstrikes.

S20261031-01.h: IRGC says tankers hit mines or caught fire in Strait of Hormuz
S20261031-01.s: Iran's IRGC Navy said up to four oil tankers, including a supertanker with over 2 million barrels, were stopped, hit mines or caught fire after using a southern route it called unauthorised. UKMTO said a tanker was struck by explosives attached by a small boat, and Oman rescued 25 crew off Musandam. Analysts note limpet mines are a familiar Iranian tactic, which undercuts US claims that the strait was cleared.
S20261031-01.t: Disruption in Hormuz pushes energy prices up and raises risk for Türkiye's import bill and regional trade.

S20261031-02.h: US weighs renewed strikes on Iran after midterms, Gulf states warned
S20261031-02.s: Reports say Washington told Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense round of strikes on Iran after the November 3 midterms, and Senator Murphy said he was briefed on a plan to restart the war. Netanyahu is reportedly pushing for fresh strikes, while Israeli defence officials doubt a brief air campaign could topple Iran or end its nuclear programme. Axios reports Trump did not discuss strikes with the CENTCOM commander, and Haaretz says the threat is being used as leverage for talks.
S20261031-02.t: A renewed US-Iran war would hit Türkiye's southern neighbourhood, border security and energy supply.

S20261031-03.h: Qatari mediators return to Tehran to revive US-Iran deal
S20261031-03.s: A Qatari delegation led by a senior adviser to the prime minister made its second Tehran visit in a week, holding over 12 hours of talks on a US proposal. Iran International reports Iran rejected an earlier proposal and that the sides are deadlocked over who concedes first. Araghchi says Iran's seven-day plan could be implemented quickly.
S20261031-03.t: A US-Iran deal would lower regional escalation risk and reduce pressure on Türkiye's energy and border security.

S20261031-04.h: Vance reportedly offers to meet Iranian security chief Rezaei
S20261031-04.s: Reports say US Vice President Vance offered to meet Iranian Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei to discuss ending the war. A disclosed letter prompted contradictory narratives in Washington and a conditional response in Tehran. Rezaei is reportedly in contact with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.
S20261031-04.t: A direct US-Iran channel could open diplomatic room that Ankara has sought to use as a mediator.

S20261031-05.h: Trump says Iran war will end soon, demands nuclear guarantee
S20261031-05.s: Trump said in a radio interview that the war will end soon and he expects it wrapped up before the midterms, without giving details. He said the US needs a guarantee Iran will never have a nuclear weapon. Vance said Trump will not let the confrontation become a forever war.

S20261031-06.h: Pakistan's army cautiously optimistic about US-Iran mediation
S20261031-06.s: Army chief Asim Munir, a chief mediator, visited Tehran twice this month. Pakistan's military is cautiously optimistic about de-escalation but warns of spoilers.

S20261031-07.h: Oil surges on Hormuz attacks as BP posts record profit
S20261031-07.s: Oil rose above $114 as traders brace for Iran escalation after the midterms, with Brent over 60 percent above pre-war levels. BP reported its highest profit in about two decades from the Middle East war. Merz says higher energy prices have cost Europe over €100 billion, and EU states agreed to speed the release of 42.6 million barrels from reserves.
S20261031-07.t: High and volatile energy prices strain Türkiye's inflation and current account, as its central bank noted.

S20261031-08.h: Washington says Iran cannot pay troops or fund proxies
S20261031-08.s: Treasury Secretary Bessent says Operation Economic Outcast has left Iran unable to pay troops or fund proxies. A Treasury report says the rial is down about a quarter since August, inflation is near 90%, and no oil has been loaded since August 25.
S20261031-08.t: Iranian economic collapse could add instability and migration pressure on Türkiye's eastern border.

S20261031-09.h: US enforces Hormuz blockade as Iran moves hardware past it
S20261031-09.s: The WSJ reports US forces fly nightly missions to enforce the Hormuz blockade, straining aircraft and crews. Asharq Al-Awsat reports Iran's hidden military agencies are moving hardware past the blockade.

S20261031-10.h: IRGC claims downing and capture of US drones near Hormuz
S20261031-10.s: Iran said it destroyed a US unmanned surface vessel and captured a second reconnaissance drone intact, including an MQM-170 near Qeshm Island. CENTCOM denied losing any unmanned vessel, saying all are accounted for. Reports of a hostile fighter jet intercepted over Qeshm are unconfirmed.

S20261031-11.h: Zelensky to meet Erdoğan in Istanbul on Black Sea security
S20261031-11.s: The Turkish presidency said Zelensky will make a working visit to Istanbul on October 31 at Erdoğan's invitation. They will discuss bilateral ties, the war and Black Sea security. Zelensky said the talks come ahead of resumed Ukraine-Russia negotiations next month.
S20261031-11.t: Ankara reinforces its role as host and mediator in the Ukraine war and Black Sea security.

S20261031-12.h: Türkiye nominates Feridun Sinirlioğlu for UN Secretary-General
S20261031-12.s: Türkiye formally nominated OSCE Secretary General and former foreign minister Feridun Sinirlioğlu after an impasse in Security Council straw polls.
S20261031-12.t: Ankara bids for the UN's top post, raising its diplomatic profile if the deadlock persists.

S20261031-13.h: Fidan and Rubio meet at G20 in Atlanta on Iran, Gaza, Ukraine
S20261031-13.s: Hakan Fidan met Marco Rubio on the sidelines of the G20 foreign ministers' meeting. They discussed Iran talks, Gaza and the Ukraine war. Fidan also met his Indonesian and Japanese counterparts.
S20261031-13.t: Direct access to Rubio lets Ankara press its positions on Iran mediation, Gaza and Ukraine.

S20261031-14.h: G20 family photo cancelled as Europeans refuse to stand with Lavrov
S20261031-14.s: The US cancelled the G20 foreign ministers' group photo after several European ministers refused to pose with Lavrov. Rubio urged cooperation amid rifts over Ukraine and the Middle East. Lavrov said he held brief but constructive talks with Rubio.
S20261031-14.t: Ankara, which attends both Western and Russian-inclusive formats, is positioned between the camps.

S20261031-15.h: US approves $2.1bn sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
S20261031-15.s: The State Department approved the sale of 500 PAC-3 MSE missiles, to be funded by allies, with no delivery timeline. Zelensky warns deliveries could take years. NATO's SACEUR said third-party transfers and PURL packages are moving forward.

S20261031-16.h: Kremlin rules out ceasefire ahead of Abu Dhabi trilateral talks
S20261031-16.s: Russia and the US are coordinating a date for talks in Abu Dhabi, with only mid-November mentioned so far. Peskov said preparations do not require a pause in fighting. Moscow offered a Putin-Zelensky phone call instead of a meeting, which Kyiv suspects is a trap. Lavrov said Russia's position is unchanged.
S20261031-16.t: Abu Dhabi hosting, rather than Istanbul, shows the diplomatic track is moving to another Muslim-majority venue.

S20261031-17.h: Ukraine refinery strikes continue amid reported US-pressured pause
S20261031-17.s: Drones hit the Novokuibyshevsk refinery and Russia says it intercepted over 1,000 drones overnight. Reports say Ukraine paused refinery strikes under US pressure, while a Kremlin aide says Kyiv ignored Trump's request. Russia extended its diesel export ban to January 2027.
S20261031-17.t: Strikes on Russian energy and Black Sea shipping affect Türkiye's energy and maritime interests.

S20261031-18.h: Humanitarian ceasefire allows evacuation from occupied Oleshky
S20261031-18.s: Ukrainian and Russian ombudsmen visited Oleshky during a ceasefire that held for over 80 hours. Evacuees travelled via Crimea, Russia and Belarus, and Russia said its mission was completed. A volunteer alleged some people were moved outside the agreed terms.

S20261031-19.h: Russian strikes hit Dnipro, Chernihiv, Kremenchuk and Kyiv energy
S20261031-19.s: A Russian drone strike on a Dnipro train platform killed 15 and Dnipro was hit again, cutting power to over 350,000 customers. Russia launched missiles and over 110 drones overnight, and strikes also hit Chernihiv, Kharkiv and Kyiv infrastructure. Zelensky says Russia took no step toward energy de-escalation.

S20261031-20.h: Ukraine requests emergency UN Security Council meeting on Russian strikes
S20261031-20.s: Ukraine's UN envoy requested an emergency session over strikes on Dnipro, Chernihiv and Kremenchuk that killed 20 civilians.

S20261031-21.h: Ukraine hits Russian Iskander launcher and airfields, expands deep strikes
S20261031-21.s: Ukraine said it destroyed an Iskander-M launcher in Kursk and struck depots in occupied areas, and imagery reportedly shows two Su-34s destroyed at Marinovka. Zelensky announced expansion of the precision strike zone and long-range units.

S20261031-22.h: EU Commission proposes €45bn Ukraine funding for 2027
S20261031-22.s: The Commission proposed disbursing the remaining €45 billion of the €90 billion loan in 2027, with €31.7 billion for defence capacity. Canada pledged €500 million. Euroclear says it has passed €8 billion in frozen-asset proceeds to the Commission, and a Russian court rejected its appeal over a $250 billion ruling.

S20261031-23.h: Pentagon asks NATO allies to tone down Russia-threat rhetoric
S20261031-23.s: Four sources say Pentagon officials asked several NATO countries, including Baltic allies, to tone down public rhetoric about the Russian threat.
S20261031-23.t: A softer US line on Russia would affect NATO threat perceptions on which Ankara's own balancing relies.

S20261031-24.h: Trump holds off sanctions on Russian fund after prisoner release
S20261031-24.s: Trump said the US will not lift sanctions on the Russian Direct Investment Fund for now. He praised Russia for securing release of American Hubbard and called new sanctions foolish while he negotiates detainee releases.

S20261031-25.h: Mitsotakis calls Türkiye-Libya maritime deal void, urges Black Sea truce
S20261031-25.s: Greek PM Mitsotakis called the Turkey-Libya eastern parliament maritime deal blatantly illegal and urged a Black Sea shipping truce. Cyprus repeated at the UN Security Council that the 2019 MoU is null and void.
S20261031-25.t: The Libya maritime deal underpins Ankara's Eastern Mediterranean claims, and Athens and Nicosia are now contesting it internationally.

S20261031-26.h: Türkiye and Egypt to hold naval drills amid Eastern Mediterranean tensions
S20261031-26.s: Asharq Al-Awsat reports Türkiye and Egypt will hold naval drills amid tensions in the Eastern Mediterranean.
S20261031-26.t: The drills show Ankara-Cairo military rapprochement and add to Eastern Mediterranean signalling.

S20261031-27.h: Erdoğan hosts 13th Turkic States summit, Ankara Declaration signed
S20261031-27.s: The Organization of Turkic States summit opened under the theme Turkic Century and adopted a 163-point declaration covering defence, cybersecurity, trade, energy and transport. Erdoğan signed agreements with Uzbekistan and held bilaterals with the Turkmen and Kyrgyz presidents. He called for a Turkic trade, transport and energy hub.
S20261031-27.t: The summit consolidates Türkiye's leadership in Central Asia and Middle Corridor connectivity.

S20261031-28.h: Aliyev skips Ankara Turkic summit amid strained Türkiye-Azerbaijan ties
S20261031-28.s: Azerbaijani President Aliyev skipped the summit despite a personal invitation, and aides reportedly said it answered Erdoğan skipping a Baku meeting. Erdoğan received Azerbaijan's foreign minister afterward, who spoke on the Middle and Zangezur corridors.
S20261031-28.t: Open friction with Baku, Ankara's closest ally, threatens the Caucasus corridor agenda.

S20261031-29.h: Erdoğan and Trump hold two phone calls
S20261031-29.s: Erdoğan and Trump discussed bilateral ties, Ukraine, the Middle East and the upcoming Turkic states summit in Ankara.
S20261031-29.t: Frequent leader contact with Trump supports Ankara's bargaining on defence and regional files.

S20261031-30.h: Erdoğan meets Turkish Cypriot leader as UN envoy Holguin tours Cyprus
S20261031-30.s: Erdoğan received Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhürman and stressed Turkish Cypriot rights in any settlement. UN envoy Holguin is in Cyprus, plans a tripartite session on November 9 and is optimistic about an enlarged meeting before year's end. Christodoulides says progress is possible.
S20261031-30.t: Ankara is aligning with Erhürman and defending its two-state-leaning framework as UN diplomacy restarts.

S20261031-31.h: Netanyahu's bloc wins 53 seats, no majority; Arab parties surge to 19
S20261031-31.s: Final results give Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats against 48 for Eisenkot's bloc, with Arab parties nearly doubling to 19. Neither side has 61, and Netanyahu ruled out a government with Arab parties. Talks continue, including Democrats and the United Arab List.
S20261031-31.t: A weak or unstable Israeli government shapes Israeli behaviour in Syria and Gaza, where Ankara has stakes.

S20261031-32.h: Netanyahu camp alleges election fraud; Shin Bet probes foreign funding
S20261031-32.s: Netanyahu's party claimed the vote was stolen and accused Arab parties of taking foreign funding. Election officials rejected the fraud claims, and Shin Bet, with Mossad help, is probing possible Qatari funding. Türkiye denied interfering.
S20261031-32.t: Ankara is named in Israeli claims of foreign interference, which feeds Israel-Türkiye tension.

S20261031-33.h: Israeli forces demolish homes in south Lebanon; Qassem says framework void
S20261031-33.s: Israeli forces demolished homes and shelled towns in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah's Naim Qassem said the US-brokered framework is effectively nonexistent and Hezbollah will keep its weapons while Israel occupies Lebanese land. A Lebanese military court charged 13 over a truck of Hezbollah explosives.

S20261031-34.h: Israel's Hebron siege displaces thousands as UN warns on Gaza
S20261031-34.s: Israel declared a Hebron neighbourhood a closed military zone on the eighth day of raids that displaced thousands and demolished gunmen's homes. The UN rights office warns of ethnic cleansing risks in Gaza as Israeli forces treat the Yellow Line as a kill zone. The IDF said it killed Hamas militants in Gaza City strikes.
S20261031-34.t: Gaza and West Bank escalation sustains Ankara's confrontation with Israel and its diplomatic push on Palestine.

S20261031-35.h: US orders non-emergency staff out of Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
S20261031-35.s: The US ordered non-emergency personnel to leave Saudi Arabia, warning of possible attacks on airports. The Saudi-led coalition reports repeated Houthi missiles and drones, including near Riyadh, Jazan and Medina. It said it downed a drone over Mecca, which the Houthis deny.
S20261031-35.t: Houthi pressure on Saudi Arabia adds to Red Sea and Gulf instability that affects Turkish trade and Gulf partners.

S20261031-36.h: Houthi missiles hit Aden as Yemeni army claims offensive gains
S20261031-36.s: Houthi missiles struck Aden's airport and presidential palace, and residents fear a return to full war. Yemen's army says its Dawn of Yemen operation killed 336 Houthis in 1,087 operations. Houthis expanded the Taiz offensive toward Lahj, and the Taiz governor reports siege shortages.

S20261031-37.h: KCK says peace process with Türkiye has stalled
S20261031-37.s: KCK spokesperson Sozdar Avesta says the process has stalled and demands a monitoring commission and access to Öcalan.
S20261031-37.t: A stalled process raises the risk to the effort to end PKK violence, a central Turkish security objective.

S20261031-38.h: Iraq integrates Yezidi PKK-linked units in Sinjar; Karayılan endorses
S20261031-38.s: Baghdad is integrating Yezidi YBŞ units into Iraqi security forces, and PKK's Murat Karayılan endorsed the agreement. Anadolu says it reshapes regional balances.
S20261031-38.t: Integration of PKK-affiliated units into Iraqi forces touches Ankara's Sinjar concerns and the disarmament process.

S20261031-39.h: Barrack: Iraq is part of Iran's proxy plans; Baghdad PM takes intelligence control
S20261031-39.s: US envoy Barrack said Iraq is part of Iran's overall plans, with proxies under ministerial command, and that Iran talks are nearing de-escalation. Separately, Iraq's prime minister took direct control of the intelligence service.
S20261031-39.t: Iraq's alignment between Washington and Tehran bears on Türkiye's border security and trade routes.

S20261031-40.h: Turkey's opposition squeezed by CHP ruling and jailed challenger
S20261031-40.s: Analyses describe an opposition struggling after its presidential challenger was jailed and its main party split by a court ruling. YENİ Parti plans to take the CHP nullity ruling to the ECtHR, and Özgür Özel visited a freed official. Parliamentary resignations cost the Yeni Yol group its status.
S20261031-40.t: The domestic political contest shapes Erdoğan's room for foreign policy and Europe's view of Türkiye.

S20261031-41.h: Gulf states rethink defence models as Turkey's drone arsenal draws attention
S20261031-41.s: Analyses discuss Gulf efforts to bolster defence, including Qatar's domestic weapons and Turkey's drone arsenal. An IISS report argues Gulf states must rethink reliance on US bases after the war. Saudi Arabia and NATO discussed defence cooperation.
S20261031-41.t: Gulf demand for new suppliers is an opening for the Turkish defence industry.

S20261031-42.h: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal chief suspended, police deployed
S20261031-42.s: A judge suspended the court's chief and deputy and took control, and police cordoned off the court. The Tusk-backed move sparked clashes with protesters, and President Nawrocki cut short a Senegal trip.

S20261031-43.h: Syrian authorities clash with French jihadists as prices soar
S20261031-43.s: French jihadists clashed with Syrian authorities and accused the government of a three-month siege in a Telegram statement. BBC reports soaring prices after subsidy cuts are testing Ahmed al-Sharaa's government.
S20261031-43.t: Unrest and jihadist activity in Syria bear on Türkiye's border security and its support for Damascus.

S20261031-44.h: Turkish intelligence captures suspected ISIL Khorasan operative abroad
S20261031-44.s: MİT captured a suspected ISIL Afghanistan-branch operative, named as Uğur Bahadır, in the Afghanistan-Pakistan region and brought him to Türkiye.
S20261031-44.t: The operation shows MİT's reach against ISIL threats to Türkiye.

S20261031-45.h: EU and Canada sign trade deal and Alliance for the Future
S20261031-45.s: The EU and Canada signed a digital trade deal and launched an Alliance for the Future at a Montreal summit as Trump's tariff threats push allies closer. They aim to define a partnership by 2027, with talks possibly concluding in June.

S20261031-46.h: Novaya Gazeta announces closure after Russian pressure
S20261031-46.s: Russia's best-known independent newspaper said it will close after 30 years, citing authorities' pressure and its Moscow office eviction.

S20261031-47.h: Dockworkers strike at 113 ports against arms shipments
S20261031-47.s: Dockworkers at 113 ports in 22 countries struck over arms shipments to wars, including in Türkiye, Greece, Italy and Cyprus.
S20261031-47.t: Turkish ports took part in the action over arms transfers to Israel.

S20261031-48.h: Türkiye to host COP31 in Antalya with Lula attending
S20261031-48.s: Brazil's Lula will attend COP31 in Antalya on November 11-12, and Turkish officials say Türkiye will bridge developed and developing countries on climate action.
S20261031-48.t: COP31 gives Ankara a prominent multilateral platform.
